reflection_text.1:
The problem is the 2-D steady Stokes response of a viscous layer 0≤z≤h to a harmonic basal shear τ_b=S0 sin kx with a free surface at z=0. With ψ(x,z)=f(z) sin kx

u_x = f′ sin kx ,  u_z = -k f cos kx ,   ∇⁴ψ=0 → (D²−k²)²f=0

σ_xz = μ[ f″+k²f ] sin kx ,    σ_zz = μ[ f‴/k −3k f′ ] cos kx ,   P =−μ/k[ f‴−k²f′ ].

Top z=0 : u_x=0 ⇒ f′(0)=0, steady topography ⇒ u_z(0)=0 ⇒ f(0)=0
and σ_zz(0)= ρg e cos kx ⇒ μ/k f‴(0)=ρg e .

Base z=h : σ_zz(h)=0 ⇒ f‴(h)=3k²f′(h) ,   σ_xz(h)=S0 ⇒ μ[ f″(h)+k²f(h)]=S0 .

With f(0)=0, f′(0)=0 the biharmonic can be written
f(z)=B z cosh kz + D z sinh kz −(B/k) sinh kz ,   C=−B/k .
f‴(0)=2k²B so that e=2μkB/ρg .

The zero normal traction at the base gives
B(c−kh s)=D hk c ,   c=cosh kh , s=sinh kh,
D = B(c−kh s)/(hk c).

Then
f″+k²f =2k[ Bh k c + D c + D h k s ] .
Hence
2k[ Bh k c + D c + D h k s ] = S0/μ,

which with the expression for D gives
B = S0 h c/[2μ(c²+ k²h²)] .
Up to the sin/cos phase sign B>0 for the imposed shear.

Hence
ρg e_s =2μk B = S0 kh c/[c²+k²h²] ,
e_s = S0/(ρg) · kh cosh kh/[cosh²kh +k²h²] .

With the isostatic restoring stress Δρ g e the ρ in the normal stress
balance is replaced by Δρ, i.e.

e_s = χ S0/Δρ g ,   χ(kh)= kh cosh kh/[cosh²kh + k²h²]
     = [kh/ cosh kh + cosh kh/kh ]⁻¹ .

Viscosity drops out of the steady state.  Long wave kh≪1,
cosh kh≈1+½k²h²,
χ≈kh/[1+k²h²]≈kh,   e_s≈kh S0/Δρ g ,
and χ→2kh e^{−kh} for kh≫1.  The sign is opposite to the sin kx
shear, e∝−cos kx for the usual phase convention; magnitude is
quoted above.

This is the result obtained by Colleagues 1,4,5,8,10.  Colleagues 3,11,
6,7,13,14 obtain e_s∝ kh sinh kh/[cosh²+k²h²] or
χ=kh sinh kh/[sinh kh cosh kh−kh] ≈3/2kh for kh≪1. Those forms
follow from imposing an additional impermeability / no–vertical-flow
condition f(h)=0, i.e. u_z(h)=0, or from different normalisation of
σ_zz, which is not required by the stated boundary conditions
σ_zz(h)=0, σ_xz(h)=S0 with a free base.  The viscosity–independent
kh scaling is the conventional viscous dynamic topography for a basal
harmonic traction. ∎
reflection_text.8:
The Stokes stream function can be taken as 
$\psi(x,z)=f(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=f'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k f\cos kx$,
$\nabla^4\psi=0$, 
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu\big[f'''/k-3k f'\big]\cos kx$.
With a material free surface $u_x(0)=0$ gives $f'(0)=0$ and in the
steady state $u_z(0)=\dot e=0$ gives $f(0)=0$.  Then
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu f'''(0)/k\cos kx=\rho g e\cos kx$, i.e.
$f'''(0)=k\rho g e/\mu$.
The traction free base is $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, i.e. $f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$,
and the imposed basal shear is $\mu[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)]=S_{0}$.

With $f(z)=(p_{1}z)( \cosh kz)+(q_{1}z-a/k)\sinh kz$, $p_{0}=0$,
$f'(0)=0$, the conditions $f(0)=0$, $f'(0)=0$ are satisfied.  
Put $a\equiv p_{1}$,
$f'''(0)=2ak^{2}$, so $a=\rho g e/2\mu k$.
The zero normal stress at $z=h$ gives
$q_{1}=a\big[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh\big]/\big[kh\cosh kh\big]$.
Then
$f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)=2k\big[\,ahk\cosh kh+q_{1}\cosh kh
+k q_{1}h\sinh kh\,\big]$ and
$2\mu k[\,\cdots\,]=S_{0}$.

Eliminating $q_{1}$ gives
$\rho g e\,[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]/\big[kh\cosh kh\big]=S_{0}$,
i.e. in the steady state

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\;
       \dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}$,

so that with the buoyant restoring stress $\Delta\rho g$,
$e_{s}= \chi\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with

$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}
       =\Big[\dfrac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1}$,

the sign being the $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase
shift; the magnitude is the above.  In particular
$\chi\simeq kh$ for $kh\ll1$, $\chi\simeq2kh\,e^{-kh}$ for $kh\gg1$
and $\chi(1)\!\approx\!0.46$, the familiar viscosity-independent
dynamic topography $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ in the
long-wave lubrication limit.

This is the result obtained by colleagues 1,4,5,8,10.  The alternative
forms quoted by colleagues 3,6,7,11,13,14,15,
$\chi\sim kh\sinh kh/[\sinh kh\cosh kh-kh]$, 
$\chi\sim kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]$, etc., follow from
imposing an extra impermeability condition $u_{z}(h)=0$ or $f(h)=0$,
i.e. $W(0)=0$, $W(h)=0$, which is not required by the stated
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ base conditions.  With the
base free to move vertically the $f(0)=f'(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ set above is the correct one and gives the
$\,kh\cosh kh/(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh$ transfer function, up to the
conventional $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ replacement and an inessential sign.
The viscosity cancels in the steady state, as expected. ∎
reflection_text.6:
The Stokes stream function can be taken as 
$\psi=f(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=f'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k f\cos kx$, 
$\nabla^{4}\psi=0$.  

With the $k$ mode
$$
p=\mu\Big(kf'-\frac{f'''}{k}\Big)\cos kx,\qquad
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big(f''+k^{2}f\big)\sin kx,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= \mu\Big[\frac{f'''}{k}-3k f'\Big]\cos kx .
$$
Top $z=0$
$$
u_{x}=0\iff f'(0)=0,\qquad 
\dot e=u_{z}(0)=-kf(0)\cos kx,
$$
so that in the steady state $f(0)=0$ and
$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}f'''(0)\cos kx=\rho g e_{s}\cos kx .
\tag{1}
$$
Put $f(z)=B\big[z\cosh kz-k^{-1}\sinh kz\big]+Ez\sinh kz$, i.e.
$f(0)=f'(0)=0$ and $f(z)=(A+Bz)\cosh kz+(C+Dz)\sinh kz$ with the
usual $A=0$, $B+kC=0$.  The stress free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is
$f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$ and with the above form gives
$$
E=B\,\frac{\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh}{kh\cosh kh} .
$$
The imposed basal shear
$$
\mu\big[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)\big]=S_{0}
$$
then yields
$$
2\mu k\Big[Bhk\cosh kh+E\cosh kh+Ehk\sinh kh\Big]=S_{0},
$$
and with the $E$ relation above
$$
B=\frac{S_{0}\,h\cosh kh}{2\mu\big[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}\big]} .
$$
Now $f'''(0)=2k^{2}B$, so from (1)
$$
\rho g e_{s}= \frac{\mu}{k}f'''(0)=\frac{2\mu kB}{\rm }
          =\frac{S_{0}\,kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}} .
$$
Hence with the buoyancy restoring stress $\Delta\rho g$
$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}
       =\Bigg[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Bigg]^{-1},
$$
the sign being the usual $90^{\circ}$ $\sin\leftrightarrow\cos$
phase, $e_{s}\propto-\sin kx$.  The viscosity cancels in the steady
state.  In the long wave lubrication limit $kh\ll1$, $\cosh kh=1+O(k^{2}h^{2})$,
$$
\chi(kh)=kh\big[1+O(k^{2}h^{2})\big],\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$
the familiar $e_{s}\propto kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ viscous dynamic
topography, with the often quoted thin plate form
$\chi_{0}\approx kh$ and $|\chi(1)|\approx0.46$.  The $kh\sinh kh$
forms obtained with an additional impermeable base condition
$f(h)=0$ are the $u_{z}(h)=0$ variant; the $f(h)$ free base used in the
statement gives the $\cosh$ numerator above.  This is the steady,
viscosity independent response and the transient decays on the viscous
time $\mu/\Delta\rho gk$. ∎
reflection_text.4:
The Stokes stream function can be taken as $\psi=f(z)\sin kx$ with
$u_{x}=f'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k f\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big(f''+k^{2}f\big)\sin kx$,
$p=-\mu k^{-1}\big(f'''-k^{2}f'\big)\cos kx$ and
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}\big[f'''-3k^{2}f'\big]\cos kx$.
With $f(z)=(a_{0}+a_{1}z)\cosh kz+(b_{0}+b_{1}z)\sinh kz$ the free surface
conditions $u_{x}(0)=0$, $f'(0)=0$ and in the steady state $u_{z}(0)=0$,
$f(0)=0$ give $a_{0}=0,\;b_{0}=-a_{1}/k$.
Hence
$f'(z)=b_{1}kz\cosh kz+(a_{1}kz+b_{1})\sinh kz$,
$f'''(0)=2k^{2}a_{1}$,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)=\rho g e$,
so that $e=2\mu k a_{1}/\rho g$.

The base conditions are $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ i.e. $f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$ and
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ i.e. $\mu\big[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)\big]=S_{0}$.
$f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$ gives
$b_{1}=a_{1}\big[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh\big]/\big[kh\cosh kh\big]$.
With this
$f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)=2k\Big[b_{1}\cosh kh+b_{1}kh\sinh kh+a_{1}kh\cosh kh\Big]$,
so that
$2a_{1}\big[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}\big]/\big[h\cosh kh\big]=S_{0}/\mu$.
Using $a_{1}=\rho g e/2\mu k$ the steady topography is
$e_{s}=S_{0}kh\cosh kh/\big[\rho g\big(\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}\big)\big]$,
i.e. with the buoyancy restoring stress $\Delta\rho g$,
$e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with
$\chi(kh)=kh\cosh kh\big/\big[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}\big]
=\big[kh/\cosh kh+\cosh kh/kh\big]^{-1}$.
In particular $\chi\simeq kh$ for $kh\ll1$, $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
and $\chi\to0$ exponentially for $kh\gg1$. The viscosity cancels in the
steady state, the sign being the $90^{\circ}$ $\sin\leftrightarrow\cos$
phase shift between the imposed shear and the topography.

Colleagues 1,10,4,5,8 reproduce this result. Colleagues 11,3,6,7,13,14 quote
forms with a $\sinh kh$ numerator, e.g.
$\chi\propto kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]$ or
$\chi=kh\sinh kh/[\sinh kh\cosh kh-kh]$,
which follow from imposing an additional impermeability condition
$\Phi(h)=0$ or $u_{z}(h)=0$ at the base and/or a different normal-stress
normalisation. The statement imposes only $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ at the base,
no $u_{z}(h)=0$, so the $\cosh$ numerator form above is the one consistent
with the stated boundary data. Up to the conventional sign the magnitude is
the $O(kh)$ viscous dynamic topography $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
often quoted as $\chi\approx kh$ for $kh\ll1$.
reflection_text.10:
The steady harmonic Stokes problem is $u_{x}=f'(z)\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-kf(z)\cos kx$, $\nabla^{4}\psi=0$.
With the free surface $z=0$ rigid in $x$ and $u_{x}=0$,
$f'(0)=0$, and in the steady state $\dot e=u_{z}(0)=0$ so $f(0)=0$. 
With $\sigma_{zz}= \big[\mu k^{-1}f'''-3\mu k f'\big]\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ gives on the top
$\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)=\rho g e$, $f'(0)=0$ and at the base
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$.

With the $f(0)=f'(0)=0$ biharmonic,
$f(z)=A z\cosh kz+\big[-A/k+Bz\big]\sinh kz$,
$f'(z)=B\sinh kz+z\big[A k\sinh kz+B k\cosh kz\big]$,
$f'''(z)=2Ak^{2}\cosh kz+Ak^{3}z\sinh kz+3Bk^{2}\sinh kz+Bk^{3}z\cosh kz$.
$f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$ gives
$A\big[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh\big]=Bk h\cosh kh$,
i.e. $B=A\big[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh\big]/\big[kh\cosh kh\big]$.

The basal shear
$\mu\big[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)\big]=S_{0}$,
$f''+k^{2}f=2k\big[Akh\cosh kz+B\cosh kz+Bkh\sinh kz\big]$, gives
$2\mu k\big[Akh\cosh kh+B\cosh kh+Bkh\sinh kh\big]=S_{0}$.
Eliminating $B$,
$A=\displaystyle\frac{S_{0}h\cosh kh}{2\mu\big[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}\big]}$.

On the free surface
$f'''(0)=2Ak^{2}$ so that $\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)=2\mu kA=\rho g e_{s}$,
hence
$e_{s}= \displaystyle\frac{2\mu kA}{\rho g}
      =\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
        \frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}$.
Writing the hydrostatic restoring stress with the density contrast
$\Delta\rho$, $\rho\to\Delta\rho$,

$e_{s}= \chi\,\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,
$\displaystyle\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}
       =\Big[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Big]^{-1}$,
the $90^{\circ}$ phase shift $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ giving the usual sign.
In particular $\chi=kh+O(k^{3}h^{3})$ for $kh\ll1$,
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, and $\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$
for $kh\gg1$.  With the sign convention used in the statement the
magnitude is the expression above; up to sign this is the viscosity-
independent long-time dynamic topography of a harmonic basal shear.

The $kh^{-1}$ forms quoted by Colleagues 3, 11, 6, 7, etc.,
$\chi\propto kh\sinh kh/[\sinh kh\cosh kh-kh]\sim3/2kh$ for $kh\ll1$,
follow from imposing an additional impermeability condition
$u_{z}(h)=0$ or from using $f(0)\neq0$ in the steady limit, i.e. a
different set of kinematic base conditions. With the stated
conditions $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$ and no prescribed
vertical velocity at the base the $kh\cosh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]$
transfer function is the consistent steady solution and the viscosity
cancels out. The sign is conventional; the magnitude is usually quoted
as $|\chi|\approx kh$ for the geologically relevant $kh\lesssim1$ regime.
reflection_text.2:
The Stokes stream function can be written
$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$\nabla^4\psi=0$, $(D^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$.  With
$p=P(z)\cos kx$, $P=-\mu k^{-1}(\Phi'''-k^2\Phi')$,

$\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \big[\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''-3\mu k\Phi'\big]\cos kx$.

Top $z=0$: $u_x=0\iff\Phi'(0)=0$ and in a steady state
$u_z(0)=\dot e=0\iff\Phi(0)=0$,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx\iff \mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e$.

Base $z=h$: $\sigma_{zz}=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)$,
$\sigma_{xz}=S_0\sin kx\iff\mu\big[\Phi''(h)+k^2\Phi(h)\big]=S_0$.

With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$
$\Phi(z)=Bz\cosh kz+D z\sinh kz-(B/k)\sinh kz$,
$\Phi'(z)=s(kBz+D)+c\,kDz$, $s=\sinh kz$, $c=\cosh kz$.
$\Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)$ gives
$B c_h=k h\big(B s_h+D c_h\big)$, $c_h=\cosh kh$, $s_h=\sinh kh$,

$D=B\big(c_h-kh s_h\big)/(kh c_h)$.

The basal shear then gives
$\mu2k\big[c_h(kBh+D)+kDh s_h\big]=S_0$,
i.e.
$2\mu B\big[k^2h^2+c_h^2\big]/(h c_h)=S_0$,
$$
B=\frac{S_0 h c_h}{2\mu\big[k^2h^2+c_h^2\big]}\; .
$$

Now $\Phi'''(0)=2k^2B$, so that with $\Phi'(0)=0$
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=2\mu k B=\rho g e_s$,
hence
$$
e_s=\frac{2\mu k B}{\rho g}
     =\frac{S_0}{\rho g}\,
       \frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh}\;,
$$
up to the $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ sign.  With the
isostatic restoring density $\Delta\rho$, $\rho\to\Delta\rho$,

$e_s=\chi\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$,
$$
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh}
       =\Big[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1},
$$
viscosity cancels in the steady state.  Long wave $kh\ll1$,
$\cosh kh\simeq1$,
$\chi\simeq kh/(1+k^2h^2)\simeq kh$, so that the familiar thin-plate
limit is $e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$; $|\chi|\to0$ exponentially for
$kh\gg1$.

This is the result obtained by Colleagues 1,4,5,8,10,15.  The
$\sinh$-numerator forms e.g. $\chi=kh\sinh kh/( \cosh^2kh+k^2h^2)$
Colleagues 7,13,14 and the $kh\sinh kh/(\sinh kh\cosh kh-kh)$ forms
Colleagues 3,11,6 arise from different implementations of the
kinematic/zero-normal-stress conditions, e.g. imposing $\Phi(h)=0$
instead of $\Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)$ or using a different
$ \sigma_{zz}$ expression.  With the stated BCs $u_x(0)=0$,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0$
and the steady kinematic condition $u_z(0)=0$ the cosh-numerator
expression above is consistent.  Sign is conventional; the magnitude
is the quoted $\chi$.  The $kh\ll1$ thin-plate limit $\chi\approx kh$
is the often quoted $e_s\approx kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$ viscous dynamic
topography. ∎
reflection_text.5:
The stream function ansatz $\psi=F(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=F'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-kF\cos kx$ gives $\nabla^{4}\psi=0$, $F=(p_{0}+p_{1}z)\cosh kz+(q_{0}+q_{1}z)\sinh kz$, $\sigma_{xz}= \mu[F''+k^{2}F]\sin kx$ and $\sigma_{zz}= \mu[k^{-1}F'''-3kF']\cos kx$.  
The top $z=0$ conditions are $u_{x}=0\Leftrightarrow F'(0)=0$ and in the steady state $\dot e=0\Leftrightarrow F(0)=0$.  With the free surface $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}F'''(0)\cos kx$, i.e. $\rho g e=\mu k^{-1}F'''(0)$.  
The base $z=h$ conditions are $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\Leftrightarrow F'''(h)=3k^{2}F'(h)$ and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\Leftrightarrow\mu[F''+k^{2}F]_{h}=S_{0}$.  Up to the inessential $\sin\leftrightarrow\cos$ phase this gives the biharmonic solution with $F(0)=F'(0)=0$,
$F(z)=C_{1}\sinh kz+C_{3}z\sinh kz-kC_{1}z\cosh kz$,
$F''+k^{2}F=2k\big[C_{3}\cosh kz+C_{3}kz\sinh kz-k^{2}C_{1}z\cosh kz\big]$
and $F'''(z)=3C_{3}k^{2}\sinh kz+C_{3}k^{3}z\cosh kz-2k^{3}C_{1}\cosh kz-k^{4}C_{1}z\sinh kz$.
The zero normal traction at the base gives
$C_{1}=C_{3}h\cosh kh/[kh\sinh kh-\cosh kh]$,
and the imposed basal shear gives
$C_{3}=-S_{0}[kh\sinh kh-\cosh kh]/\{2\mu k[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]\}$,
hence
$C_{1}=-S_{0}h\cosh kh/\{2\mu k[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]\}$.
With $\rho g e_{s}= \mu k^{-1}F'''(0)=2\mu k^{2}C_{1}$,
$e_{s}=S_{0}/\rho g\;kh\cosh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]$.
Replacing the plate weight by the buoyancy restoring stress $\Delta\rho g$,
$e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with

$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}
       =\Big[\dfrac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1},$

up to the conventional $\sin\!-\!\cos$ sign.  Viscosity cancels in the steady state.  For $kh\ll1$, $\cosh kh=1+O(k^{2}h^{2})$,
$\chi(kh)=kh\,[1+O(k^{2}h^{2})]\approx kh$,
so that in the long-wave lubrication limit $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ and $|e_{s}|$ is $O(kh)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, often quoted as the $0.4\!-\!0.6\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ viscous dynamic topography for $kh\sim O(1)$.

The alternative forms $\chi\propto kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]$, $\chi=kh\sinh kh/[\sinh kh\cosh kh-kh]$, $\chi=\alpha/[\cosh\alpha+\alpha\sinh\alpha]$ etc. arise from imposing an extra impermeable condition $u_{z}(h)=0$ or $F(h)=0$, i.e. a no vertical flow base, which is not part of the stated boundary conditions.  Those give the $3/2kh$ long-wave law and the $\sinh$ numerator forms seen in Colleagues 3, 7, 11, 13, 14.  The consensus of the $F(0)=F'(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ solution is the $kh\cosh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]$ transfer function, with the familiar $kh$ long-wave limit.  Sign is set by the $90^{\circ}$ phase between the imposed $\sin kx$ shear and the $\cos kx$ topography; the magnitude is the expression above.
reflection_text.15:
The Stokes stream function can be taken as $\psi(x,z)=f(z)\sin kx$,
$u_x=f'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k f\cos kx$, $\nabla^{4}\psi=0$.  With $a=k$
$ f^{(iv)}-2a^{2}f''+a^{4}f=0 $ and

$\sigma_{xz}=\mu\,(f''+a^{2}f)\sin kx$, 
$p=\mu a^{-1}(a^{2}f'-f''')\cos kx$, 
$\sigma_{zz}=\mu\,[a^{-1}f'''-3a f']\cos kx$.

The free surface $z=0$ gives $u_{x}=0\Leftrightarrow f'(0)=0$ and,
in steady state, $u_{z}(0)=0\Leftrightarrow f(0)=0$.  Then
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu a^{-1}f'''(0)\cos kx=\rho g e\cos kx$ so that
$f'''(0)=a\rho g e/\mu$.
The basal conditions are $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\Leftrightarrow
f'''(h)=3a^{2}f'(h)$ and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$.
With $f(0)=f'(0)=0$

$f(z)=Bz\cosh az+\bigl(Dz-B/a\bigr)\sinh az$,
$f'(z)=aBz\sinh az+D\sinh az+aDz\cosh az$,
$f'''(0)=2a^{2}B$, so that $B=\rho g e/(2\mu a)$.

The zero normal–stress base gives $B\cosh ah=aBh\sinh ah+aDh\cosh ah$
i.e. $D=B/a h-B\tanh ah$.  The basal shear gives
$\mu\,[f''(h)+a^{2}f(h)]=S_{0}$, i.e.

$2\mu a\Big[\cosh ah\,(aBh+D)+aDh\sinh ah\Big]=S_{0}$,
which with the $D$ above reduces to

$ \mu\,2B\;\frac{a^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}ah}{h\cosh ah}=S_{0}$.

Hence

$B=\dfrac{S_{0}h\cosh ah}{2\mu\bigl[a^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}ah\bigr]}$,
and with $B=\rho g e_{s}/(2\mu a)$

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\frac{ah\cosh ah}{a^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}ah}
      =\dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}$ .

The viscosity cancels in steady state.  With the isostatic restoring
stress $\Delta\rho g$ the usual form is

$e_{s}= \chi\,\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Big[\dfrac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1}$,

the sign being that for which $e$ is in anti-phase with the imposed
$\sin kx$ shear.  In the long-wave lubrication limit $kh\ll1$,
$\cosh kh=1+O(k^{2}h^{2})$,

$\chi(kh)=kh\bigl[1+O(k^{2}h^{2})\bigr]\approx kh$, 
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,

i.e. the familiar $O(kh)$ viscous dynamic topography, and
$\chi\to2kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$.

The same expression is obtained in Colleagues 1,4,5,8,10,15.  The
alternative forms quoted by Colleagues 3,6,7,11,13,14,
$\chi\propto kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]$ or
$\chi=kh\sinh kh/[\sinh kh\cosh kh-kh]\simeq3/2kh$, follow from
imposing additionally $u_{z}(h)=0$ or a different normal-stress
normalisation at the base, i.e. an impermeable base
$\Phi(h)=0$.  The statement as given imposes only $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$
and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ at the base, so the $f(0)=f'(0)=0$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ solution above is the
physically consistent steady state.  Up to the conventional
$\rho/\Delta\rho$ replacement this is the $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$
transfer function usually quoted as $\chi\approx kh$ for $kh\ll1$.
reflection_text.9:
The Stokes stream function can be taken as $\psi=f(z)\sin kx$,
$u_{x}=f'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k f\cos kx$.  With $\nabla^{4}\psi=0$

$f''''-2k^{2}f''+k^{4}f=0$ and

$\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]\sin kx$,
$p=-(\mu/k)\big[f'''-k^{2}f'\big]\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}=(\mu/k)\big[f'''-3k^{2}f'\big]\cos kx$.

The free surface $z=0$ is $u_{x}=0\Rightarrow f'(0)=0$ and in the steady
state $\dot e=0\Rightarrow u_{z}(0)=0\Rightarrow f(0)=0$.  Then

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=(\mu/k)f'''(0)\cos kx=\rho g e\cos kx$ .

The base $z=h$ is $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, i.e. $f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$, and
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$, i.e. $\mu[\,f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)\,]=S_{0}$.

With $f(0)=f'(0)=0$

$f(z)=b\,z\cosh kz+(Dz-b/k)\sinh kz$ ,
$f'(z)=\sinh kz\,(b kz+D)+Dkz\cosh kz$,

$f'''(0)=2b k^{2}$, so that

$\rho g e=(\mu/k)f'''(0)=2\mu k b$,  $b=\rho g e/2\mu k$.

The zero normal stress at the base gives

$b\cosh kh=k h\big[b\sinh kh+D\cosh kh\big]$,

i.e. $D=b\big[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh\big]/kh\cosh kh$.
With $X=bkh+D$

$f''+k^{2}f=2k\big[\cosh kh\,X+Dkh\sinh kh\big]$,
and using the relation for $D$

$f''+k^{2}f=2kb\big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]/kh\cosh kh$.

Hence

$\mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]_{h}=S_{0}$ gives

$\displaystyle \frac{\rho g e}{k}\,
\frac{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}{h\cosh kh}=S_{0}$,

i.e.

$\displaystyle e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\frac{k h\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}$,

the sign being the $90^{\circ}$ $\sin\leftrightarrow\cos$ phase shift.
With the isostatic restoring stress $\Delta\rho g e$ the $\rho$ in the
normal stress balance is replaced by $\Delta\rho$,

$e_{s}= \chi\,\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,

$\displaystyle 
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}
      =\Big[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1}$,

up to the conventional sign.  For $kh\ll1$, $\cosh kh\simeq1$,

$\chi(kh)=kh\big[1+O(k^{2}h^{2})\big]$,
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,

the usual viscosity-independent $O(kh)$ dynamic topography.  In
particular $\chi(1)\approx0.46$, $\chi\approx0.4\!-\!0.6$ for the
geologically relevant $kh\sim O(1)$.  The $1/kh$ divergent forms
$\chi\propto kh\sinh kh/[\sinh kh\cosh kh-kh]\sim3/2kh^{-1}$ quoted by
Colleagues 3,11 arise from an inconsistent use of the kinematic /
normal-stress conditions and give the unphysical $e_{s}\to\infty$ as
$h\to0$.  The $\sinh$-numerator variants are the same expression up to
the $O(kh)$ series and reduce to the $kh$ law quoted above.  The
viscosity cancels in the steady state as required. ∎
reflection_text.11:
With the stream function $\psi (x,z)=f(z)\sin kx$,

\begin{equation*}
u_{x}=f'\sin kx ,\qquad u_{z}=-kf\cos kx ,
\end{equation*}
$$
\sigma_{xz}= \mu \big[f''+k^{2}f\big]\sin kx ,
\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}\big[f'''-3k^{2}f'\big]\cos kx ,
\qquad 
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[f'''-k^{2}f'\big] .
$$
The biharmonic equation is $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}f=0$.  With the rigid lid

\begin{equation*}
f(0)=f'(0)=0,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx ,
\end{equation*}
the steady solution can be written

\begin{equation*}
f(z)=\big(A+Bz\big)\sinh kz-kAz\cosh kz ,
\end{equation*}
so that
\begin{equation*}
f'''(0)=-2k^{3}A,\qquad 
f'''(0)=\frac{k\rho g}{\mu}e\;,
\end{equation*}
i.e.
\begin{equation*}
A=-\frac{\rho g}{2\mu k^{2}}e  .
\end{equation*}
The free normal stress at the base,
\begin{equation*}
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h),
\end{equation*}
gives
\begin{equation*}
B=A\Big(k\tanh kh-\frac1h\Big) ,
\end{equation*}
and the imposed basal shear

\begin{equation*}
\mu\big[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)\big]=S_{0}
\end{equation*}
gives with $C_{h}=\cosh kh$, $S_{h}=\sinh kh$

\begin{equation*}
2k\Big[B C_{h}+kBhS_{h}-k^{2}AhC_{h}\Big]=\frac{S_{0}}{\mu}\; .
\end{equation*}
Eliminating $B$ the $A$–term survives as
\begin{equation*}
\frac{\rho g e}{k hC_{h}}\Big[C_{h}^{2}+k^{2}h^{2}\Big]=S_{0},
\end{equation*}
i.e. on the free surface

\begin{equation*}
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}\equiv
\chi_{0}(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\;,
\end{equation*}
the sign being the one which makes the topography $\cos kx$ be in
anti–phase with the imposed $\sin kx$ shear.  In particular
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e_{s}\cos kx$ is balanced by the viscous normal
stress $\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)$.  With the buoyancy restoring stress
$\Delta\rho ge$ the $\rho$ in the normal stress balance is replaced
by $\Delta\rho$ and

\[
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}
      =\Bigg[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Bigg]^{-1},
\]

is the steady viscous dynamic topography produced by the harmonic
basal traction $S_{0}\sin kx$.  Up to the conventional sign $e_{s}
\to -e_{s}$ for the phase convention $\sin\leftrightarrow\cos$.
For $kh\ll1$, $\cosh kh=1+O(k^{2}h^{2})$ and

\[
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}+O\!\big(k^{3}h^{3}\big)
      \simeq kh ,
\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\]

the familiar long-wave viscous plate law $e_{s}\propto S_{0}kh/
\Delta\rho g$; the viscosity drops out of the steady state.  This is
normally quoted as $|e_{s}|\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, i.e. 
$\chi_{0}\approx kh$, and with the hyperbolic factor retained
$\chi(kh)=kh\cosh kh\big[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}\big]^{-1}$, 
which for $kh\sim O(1)$ is $0.3\!-\!0.6\,kh$ and tends to zero
exponentially for $kh\gg1$.  The minus sign expresses the
$90^{\circ}$ phase shift between the imposed $\sin kx$ shear and the
$\cos kx$ topography. ∎
reflection_text.12:
The public round shows two families of transfer functions.
With $\psi=F(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=F'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-kF\cos kx$,
$\nabla^{4}\psi=0$ gives $F=(a_{0}+a_{1}z)\cosh kz+(b_{0}+b_{1}z)\sinh kz$.
The free, no-slip top is $F'(0)=0$ and in the steady state $\dot e=0\Rightarrow
F(0)=0$, i.e. $a_{0}=0$, $a_{1}=-k b_{0}$.  Then

$\sigma_{zz}=\mu k^{-1}\!\left[F'''-3k^{2}F'\right]\cos kx$ ,
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu\left[F''+k^{2}F\right]\sin kx$,

and 
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, 
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$.
With $f''' (0)=-2k^{3}b_{0}$ the top normal stress gives
$b_{0}=-\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$.  The zero normal stress at the base
$F'''(h)=3k^{2}F'(h)$ gives
$b_{1}=b_{0}\!\left(k\tanh kh-1/h\right)$,
and the basal shear condition gives with $C=\cosh kh$, $S=\sinh kh$

$\mu\Big[F''+k^{2}F\Big]_{h}=2k\mu\Big[b_{1}C+k h\big(-k b_{0}C+b_{1}S\big)\Big]=S_{0}$.

Eliminating $b_{1}$ the $k^{2}h^{2}\big(C^{2}-S^{2}\big)=k^{2}h^{2}$
cancellation gives the viscosity independent steady relation

$\rho g\,e_{s}\,\dfrac{C^{2}+k^{2}h^{2}}{k h\,C}=S_{0}$,

i.e. with the buoyancy restoring stress $\Delta\rho g e$,

$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
\frac{k h\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}
\equiv \chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,

$\chi(kh)=\displaystyle 
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}
=\Bigg[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Bigg]^{-1}$,

the sign being the $90^{\circ}$ $\sin\leftrightarrow\cos$ phase shift.
In particular

$\chi(kh)=\frac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}+O(k^{4}h^{4})$, 
$\chi\simeq kh$ for $kh\ll1$, $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
and $\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}$ for $kh\gg1$.  For $kh=1$,
$\chi\approx0.46$, the usual $O(1)$ viscous dynamic topography number
$\chi\sim0.3\!-\!0.6\,kh$.

The $\chi=kh\sinh kh/[\sinh kh\cosh kh-kh]$ and the
$\chi=kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}+k^{2}h^{2}]$ forms quoted by several
colleagues follow from imposing an additional impermeable base
$F(h)=0$, i.e. $u_{z}(h)=0$, which is not required by the statement
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$.  With the stated stress free base the cosh
numerator form above is the correct steady, viscosity independent
amplitude. Up to the conventional sign this is the $e_{s}=\chi
S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ law, often quoted in the long wave limit as
$e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, i.e. $\chi_{0}\approx kh$.
∎

2.text:
With the harmonic mode

$$
\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx ,\qquad
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx,
$$

$\nabla^{4}\psi=0$ gives $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$ and with 
$p=P(z)\cos kx$

$$
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\bigl[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\bigr] ,\qquad
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\bigl[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\bigr]\sin kx,
$$
$$
\sigma_{zz}= \Big[\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''-3\mu k\Phi'\Big]\cos kx .
$$

In the steady state $u_{z}(0)=0$,

$$
\Phi(0)=0,\qquad \Phi'(0)=0 ,
$$

so that with $c_{h}=\cosh kh$, $s_{h}=\sinh kh$

$$
\Phi(z)=Bz\cosh kz+D z\sinh kz-\frac{B}{k}\sinh kz ,
$$
$$
\Phi'(0)=0,\qquad \Phi'''(0)=2k^{2}B .
$$

The free surface normal stress is

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\mu k\,2B =\rho g\,e_{s}\cos kx,
\tag{1}
$$

and the traction free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives

$$
\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)\iff
B c_{h}=kh\bigl(B s_{h}+D c_{h}\bigr) .
\tag{2}
$$

Hence

$$
D=B\,\frac{c_{h}-kh s_{h}}{khc_{h}} .
$$

The imposed basal shear

$$
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff
\mu\bigl[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\bigr]=S_{0}
$$

with (2) gives

$$
2\mu k\,\frac{B}{khc_{h}}\Big[k^{2}h^{2}+c_{h}^{2}\Big]=S_{0},
$$

i.e.

$$
B=\frac{S_{0}h\,c_{h}}{2\mu\bigl[k^{2}h^{2}+c_{h}^{2}\bigr]} .
$$

Using (1),

$$
e_{s}= \frac{2\mu kB}{\rho g}
     =\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
       \frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}\; .
$$

The viscosity drops out of the steady state.  With the isostatic
restoring stress $\Delta\rho g e$, $\rho\to\Delta\rho$,

$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Bigg[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Bigg]^{-1},
$$

up to the conventional $\sin\leftrightarrow\cos$ sign.  In particular

$$
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh}{\cosh kh+ k^{2}h^{2}{\rm sech}kh}\;\xrightarrow[kh\ll1]{}\;
\frac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}\simeq kh ,
$$

so that the familiar thin–plate, long–wave viscous dynamic topography
is

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
|\chi|\approx kh\,,
$$

and $|\chi|\to0$ exponentially for $kh\gg1$.  With the sign
convention $e>0$ upward the shear $\sin kx$ produces a topography
$\propto-\cos kx$.  This is the viscosity–independent steady amplitude
usually quoted as $e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with the
$\chi(kh)$ above, $ \chi\approx kh$ for $kh\ll1$ and
$\chi\approx2kh\,e^{-kh}$ for $kh\gg1$.  Dropping the inessential sign
this is the $kh\cosh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$ response. ∎

1.text:
For the harmonic mode write $\psi(x,z)=f(z)\sin kx$ so that

$$
u_{x}=f'\sin kx\,,\qquad u_{z}=-kf\cos kx\,,\qquad 
\nabla^{4}\psi=0\; \Longleftrightarrow\;(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}f=0,
$$

and with a constant viscosity

$$
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]\sin kx ,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= \mu\Big[\frac{f'''}{k}-3k f'\Big]\cos kx .
$$

On the free top $z=0$

$$
u_{x}(0)=0\;\Longleftrightarrow\;f'(0)=0,\qquad 
u_{z}(0)=\dot e\cos kx,
$$

so that in the steady state $f(0)=0$ and

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}f'''(0)\cos kx =\rho g\,e(t)\cos kx .
\tag{1}
$$

On the base $z=h$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\;\Longleftrightarrow\;f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h), \qquad
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\;\Longleftrightarrow\;
\mu\big[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)\big]=S_{0}.
\tag{2}
$$

With $f(0)=f'(0)=0$ the biharmonic can be put in the normal form

$$
f(z)=Bz\cosh kz+D\,z\sinh kz-\frac{B}{k}\sinh kz ,
$$

so that $f''(0)=0,\;f'''(0)=2k^{2}B$ and (1) gives

$$
\rho g\,e(t)=2\mu kB ,\qquad 
e(t)=\frac{2\mu k}{\rho g}B .
\tag{3}
$$

The zero normal traction (2) is

$$
B\big[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh\big]=D\,kh\cosh kh ,
$$

i.e.

$$
D= B\,\frac{\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh}{kh\cosh kh},
$$

and

$$
f''+k^{2}f=2k\Big[ B h k\cosh kh+D\cosh kh+D hk\sinh kh\Big].
$$

Hence with (2)

$$
2k\mu\Big[B hk\cosh kh+D\cosh kh+D hk\sinh kh\Big]=S_{0},
$$

which on elimination of $D$ gives

$$
B=\frac{S_{0} h\cosh kh}{2\mu\Big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\Big]}>0 .
$$

With (3)

$$
\rho g\,e_{s}=2\mu kB
       =\frac{S_{0}\,kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}} ,
$$

i.e. up to the $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase,

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\;
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}\;,
\qquad 
\chi_{0}(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}
          =\Bigg[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Bigg]^{-1}.
$$

Writing the isostatic restoring stress at the free surface as
$\Delta\rho g\,e$ the $\rho$ in (1) is replaced by the density
contrast $\Delta\rho$ and

$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}},
$$

the sign being $e\propto -\cos kx$ so that the topography is in
quadrature with the imposed $\sin kx$ basal shear.  The viscosity
cancels in the steady state.  In the long wave limit

$$
\cosh kh=1+O(k^{2}h^{2})\;\;\Longrightarrow\;\;
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}+O(k^{3}h^{3})\simeq kh,
$$

so that

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

and $\chi\to2kh\,e^{-kh}$ for $kh\gg1$.  With the conventional
magnitude convention $e_{s}=|\chi|S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ this is the
viscous dynamic topography produced by a harmonic basal traction
$S_{0}\sin kx$; e.g. for $kh=1$, $\chi(1)=\cosh1/[1+\cosh^{2}1]\approx0.46$.
The often quoted thin-plate form is $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
i.e. $\chi_{0}\approx kh$, the sign being opposite to the sense of the
applied shear.  This is the $O(kh)$ viscosity independent result, the
$kh\cosh kh\big/[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]$ factor being the exact
steady transfer function. ∎

4.text:
With the harmonic dependence
$$
\psi(x,z)=f(z)\sin kx ,\qquad 
u_{x}=f'\sin kx ,\qquad u_{z}=-k f\cos kx ,
$$
$\nabla^{4}\psi=0$ gives on $0\le z\le h$

$$
f^{iv}-2k^{2}f''+k^{4}f=0\;, \qquad 
f(z)=\big(a_{0}+a_{1}z\big)\cosh kz+\big(b_{0}+b_{1}z\big)\sinh kz .
$$
On the rigid lid
$$
u_{x}(0)=0\iff f'(0)=0,\qquad 
\dot e=u_{z}(0)=-k f(0)\cos kx ,
$$
so that in the steady state $f(0)=0$.  With $f(0)=f'(0)=0$
$a_{0}=0,\;b_{0}=-a_{1}/k$ and

$$
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big(f''+k^{2}f\big)\sin kx ,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}\big[f'''-3k^{2}f'\big]\cos kx .
$$

On the free surface $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$, $f'(0)=0$,
$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)\cos kx
              =2\mu k a_{1}\cos kx =\rho g e\cos kx ,
\tag{1}
$$
i.e. $e=2\mu k a_{1}/\rho g$ and $e(t)$ is in quadrature with the
imposed shear.

At the base $z=h$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h),\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff 
\mu\big[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)\big]=S_{0}.
\tag{2}
$$

With the $f(0)=f'(0)=0$ form
$$
f'(z)=b_{1}kz\cosh kz+\big(a_{1}kz+b_{1}\big)\sinh kz ,
$$
$f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$ gives
$$
b_{1}=a_{1}\frac{\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh}{kh\cosh kh} ,
$$
and
$$
f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)=2k\Big[b_{1}\cosh kh+b_{1}kh\sinh kh
                    +a_{1}kh\cosh kh\Big] .
$$
Hence with (2)
$$
2a_{1}\frac{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}{h\cosh kh}=\frac{S_{0}}{\mu} .
$$
Using (1), $a_{1}=\rho g e/2\mu k$, the steady free surface is

$$
\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}} ,
$$

i.e. with the buoyancy stress $\Delta\rho g$ which balances the
normal stress at the plate–air/water interface,

$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}
       =\Bigg[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Bigg]^{-1} .
$$

The viscosity drops out of the steady state.  In particular

$$
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}+O(k^{4}h^{4}),\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

so that for the long wave, lubrication limit

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi\simeq kh,
$$

the familiar $O(kh)$ viscous dynamic topography; for $kh\sim1$
$\chi\approx0.4\!-\!0.5$, e.g. $\chi(1)=\cosh1\big/\!\big[1+\cosh^{2}1\big]
\approx0.46$, and $\chi\to0$ exponentially for $kh\gg1$.  Up to the
conventional $\sin\!\leftrightarrow\!\cos$ sign, the magnitude is the
$|\chi|S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ viscous response, often quoted in the
thin-plate limit as $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.  The sign is
the $90^{\circ}$ phase shift between the imposed $\sin kx$ basal shear
and the $\cos kx$ topography.  Replacing $\rho$ by the density
contrast $\Delta\rho$ is the usual isostatic form $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/
\Delta\rho g$.  This is the steady state obtained with the stated
data $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and no imposed $u_{z}(h)=0$ at the base. ∎

15.text:
With the harmonic mode

$\psi(x,z)=f(z)\sin kx$, $\,a=k$,

$u_{x}=f'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-a f\cos kx$,
$\nabla^{4}\psi=0$,

\begin{equation*}
f^{(iv)}-2a^{2}f''+a^{4}f=0 ,\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\,(f''+a^{2}f)\sin kx,
\end{equation*}
\begin{equation*}
\sigma_{zz}=\mu\Big[a^{-1}f'''-3a f'\Big]\cos kx ,
\qquad 
p=\mu a^{-1}\big(a^{2}f'-f'''\big)\cos kx .
\end{equation*}
On the free top $z=0$

$u_{x}=0\iff f'(0)=0$, $\dot e=u_{z}(0)=-a f(0)\cos kx$.
In the steady state $\dot e=0$ so that

$f(0)=0,\qquad f'(0)=0,
\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu a^{-1}f'''(0)\cos kx=\rho g e\cos kx,
$

so that $f'''(0)=a\rho g e/\mu$.
With $f(0)=f'(0)=0$

$f(z)=Bz\cosh az+\big(Dz-B/a\big)\sinh az$,

$f'''(0)=2a^{2}B$, i.e.

$B=\dfrac{\rho g e}{2\mu a}$,

and

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff f'''(h)=3a^{2}f'(h)$

gives

$D=\dfrac{B}{a h}\Big[1-a h\tanh ah\Big]$.

The imposed basal shear

$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$,

$\mu\big[f''(h)+a^{2}f(h)\big]=S_{0}$,

gives with the $D$ above

$\mu\,2a\Big[\cosh ah\,(aB h+D)+aDh\sinh ah\Big]=S_{0}$,

i.e.

$2\mu B\,\dfrac{a^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}ah}{h\cosh ah}=S_{0}$.

Hence

$B=
\dfrac{S_{0}h\cosh ah}{2\mu\big[a^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}ah\big]}$,

and with $B=\rho ge_{s}/2\mu a$

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\frac{ah\cosh ah}{a^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}ah}
      =\dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}$,

the viscosity cancelling in the steady state.  Up to the
$\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ $90^{\circ}$ phase the $e$ is in
anti-phase with the imposed $\sin kx$ shear.  With the isostatic
restoring stress $\Delta\rho g$ , $\rho\to\Delta\rho$,

$e_{s}= \chi(kh)\,\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,

\[
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Bigg[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Bigg]^{-1},
\]

i.e. $e_{s}= - \chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with the sign convention
used above.  In particular

$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh}{1+(kh)^{2}}\,[1+O(k^{2}h^{2})]\simeq kh$,
$\qquad kh\ll1$,

so that the familiar long-wave viscous dynamic topography is

$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,

$\chi_{0}=kh$ to leading order, and $\chi\to 2kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for
$kh\gg1$.  With the conventional $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ this is the
usual $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\rho g$ transfer function quoted in the
literature, $\chi\approx0.4\!-\!0.6$ for $kh\sim O(1)$.  The sign is
the anti-phase $e\propto -\cos kx$ corresponding to a depression
under a positive $+\sin kx$ basal shear.  The $kh$ factor is the
thin-plate lubrication limit; the full hyperbolic factor is the
exact steady Stokes response with $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=
S_{0}\sin kx$ and $u_{x}(0)=0$. ∎

10.text:
With the harmonic dependence
$$ \psi(x,z)=f(z)\sin kx~,\qquad 
u_{x}=f'\sin kx ,\;u_{z}=-kf\cos kx , $$
$\nabla^{4}\psi=0$ is $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}f=0$ and for a constant
$\mu$

\begin{equation*}
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\bigl[f''+k^{2}f\bigr]\sin kx,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= \mu\Bigl[k^{-1}f'''-3k f'\Bigr]\cos kx ,
\end{equation*}
up to the hydrostatic part which is removed.  
On the rigid free surface

$$u_{x}(0)=0\iff f'(0)=0 ,\qquad 
\dot e =u_{z}(0)=-kf(0)\cos kx ,$$
so that in the steady state $f(0)=0$, $\dot e=0$, and

$$ \sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)\cos kx=\rho ge(t)\cos kx , $$

i.e. $ \mu k^{-1}f'''(0)=\rho ge$.  On the traction free base

$$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h),\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff 
\mu\bigl[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)\bigr]=S_{0} .$$

With $f(0)=f'(0)=0$
$$ 
f(z)=Az\cosh kz+\Big[-A/k+Bz\Big]\sinh kz ,
$$
\begin{align*}
f'(z)&=B\sinh kz+z\Big[Ak\sinh kz+Bk\cosh kz\Big],\\
f'''(z)&=2Ak^{2}\cosh kz+Ak^{3}z\sinh kz
        +3Bk^{2}\sinh kz+Bk^{3}z\cosh kz .
\end{align*}
$f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$ gives
$$A\bigl[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh\bigr]=Bk h\cosh kh ,$$
i.e.  

$$B=A\frac{\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh}{kh\cosh kh}. $$

Now
$$f''+k^{2}f=2k\Big[Ak h\cosh kz+B\cosh kz+Bkh\sinh kz\Big],$$
so that
$$\mu\bigl[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)\bigr]
=2\mu k\Big[Ak h\cosh kh+B\cosh kh+Bkh\sinh kh\Big]=S_{0}.$$
Eliminating $B$,

$$A=\frac{S_{0}h\cosh kh}
        {2\mu\Big[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}\Big]}.$$

On the top $f'''(0)=2Ak^{2}$ and with the normal stress balance
$\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)=\rho ge_{s}$,

$$e_{s}= \frac{2\mu kA}{\rho g}
      =\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
        \frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}  ,
$$
the viscosity cancelling in the steady state.  With the isostatic
restoring stress $\Delta\rho g e$ the usual form is
$e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with

\[
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}
       =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Bigg]^{-1}>0,
\]

the sign being the $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ phase shift,
$e_{s}\propto-\,\sin kx$, i.e. $e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for the
conventional upward positive sign.  In particular

\[
\chi(kh)=kh+O(k^{3}h^{3}),\qquad kh\ll1,
\qquad 
\chi(kh)\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}\to0,\qquad kh\gg1,
\]

so that for the geologically relevant long wave
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ and $|\chi|\approx kh$, the
viscous dynamic topography of a harmonic basal shear.  The
magnitude $|\chi|$ is often quoted as $\chi_{0}=kh\cosh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+
k^{2}h^{2}]$, $|\chi|\simeq kh$ for $kh\lesssim1$, and the usual
$-\,$sign is understood.  Up to the inessential sign this is the
viscosity independent steady response; imposing the additional
kinematic condition $u_{z}(h)=0$ gives the familiar
$\chi_{\rm imp}=kh\sinh kh/[\sinh kh\cosh kh-kh]$ form. ∎

13.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I think the stream-function set up in 1,10,4,5,8 is the right one to start from and I agree with the in-plane ansatz
$\psi(x,z)=F(z)\sin kx$,
$u_x=F'\sin kx$, $u_z=-kF\cos kx$, $\nabla^{4}\psi=0$,
so that $(\partial_z^{2}-k^{2})^{2}F=0$.
With the rigid lid $u_x(0)=0$ we have $F'(0)=0$ and in a steady state
$u_z(0)=0$ so that $F(0)=0$ can be imposed on the normal mode.
Writing the biharmonic solution with the two conditions at the top
satisfied,

$F(z)=C_1\sinh kz+C_3z\sinh kz-kC_1z\cosh kz$,

$F'(0)=F(0)=0$ is built in.  Then

$F''+k^{2}F=2k\Big[C_3\cosh kz+C_3kz\sinh kz-
k^{2}C_1z\cosh kz\Big],$

$\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[F''+k^{2}F\big]\sin kx$,

$\sigma_{zz}= \mu\Big[\,k^{-1}F'''-3kF'\Big]\cos kx$.

The normal stress at the free surface is therefore

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}F'''(0)\cos kx
      =\rho g\,e(t)\cos kx$,
$F'''(0)=2k^{3}C_1$,

so that in the steady state $e_s=-2\mu k^{2}C_1/\rho g$ up to sign.

The base conditions are $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and the imposed basal shear.
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is $F'''(h)=3k^{2}F'(h)$.  With the form above

$F'(z)=kC_1\cosh kz+C_3\sinh kz+C_3z k\cosh kz
      -kC_1\cosh kz-kC_1z k\sinh kz$,

so that $F'''(h)=3k^{2}F'(h)$ gives the relation between the two
constants.  Carrying the algebra through without dropping the
$z\sinh kz$ piece that is often absorbed in the even part one gets

$C_1=\frac{C_3h\sinh kh}{kh\cosh kh-\sinh kh}$,

the familiar $ \sinh$ coupling coming from the $F'$ term at $z=h$.
Using this in the basal shear condition

$\mu\big[F''(h)+k^{2}F(h)\big]=S_0$

gives

$C_3=-\frac{S_0}{2\mu k}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh-\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}},$

and hence

$C_1=-\frac{S_0h\sinh kh}{2\mu k\big[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}\big]}$.

Putting this in the free-surface normal stress balance,

$\rho g\,e_s=\mu k^{-1}F'''(0)=\! -2\mu k^{2}C_1$,

i.e. up to the $\sin/\cos$ phase

$e_s=\frac{S_0}{\rho g}\,
\frac{k h\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}\;,$

and with the usual isostatic replacement $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ for the
plate in air/water

$e_s=\chi\,\dfrac{S_0}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(kh)=\frac{k h\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}} $,

the sign being chosen so that the topography is $90^{\circ}$ out of
phase with the imposed $\sin kx$ shear.  The viscosity cancels as it
must in a steady Stokes balance.  For $kh\ll1$,
$\sinh kh=kh+O(k^{3}h^{3})$ and

$\chi\simeq k h\big[\,1+O(k^{2}h^{2})\big],$

so that the familiar long-wave dynamic topography
$e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$ is recovered, and for $kh\gg1$
$\chi\sim kh\,e^{-kh}$ as expected for efficient screening of short
wavelength basal tractions.  This is the $O(kh)$ viscous plate response
with the hyperbolic factor coming from the $F''+k^{2}F$ shear coupling
at the base; the $\sinh kh$ in the numerator is the one that survives
the $F'(0)=0$, $F(0)=0$ and $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ conditions together with the
prescribed $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0\sin kx$, and it is the form quoted in
13–14.  The $\rho/\Delta\rho$ factor is the usual buoyancy
normalisation. ∎
