combination that enters the shear traction.  In the conventional
normalisation the $C_{1}$ that enters the surface normal stress
is the coefficient of the $\sinh kz$ part of $f$ and the $k$-independent
$\cosh kh$ that appears in (2) is absorbed in the definition of the
shear amplitude.  Keeping the $k$-explicit form used in 13,14 the
steady value of (1) becomes

$$
\Delta\rho g e_{s}= -2\mu k^{2}C_{1}
      =\frac{S_{0}\,k h\,\sinh kh}
             {\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}},
$$

i.e.

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\;
      \chi(kh),\qquad 
\chi(kh)=\frac{k h\,\sinh kh}
               {\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}} ,
$$

the sign being the usual $90^{\circ}$ phase shift between the
$\sin kx$ basal shear and the $\cos kx$ topography.  The viscosity
drops out of the steady state as it must.  For $kh\ll1$,

$$
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}+O(k^{3}h^{3})\simeq kh,
$$

so that in the lubricating long-wave limit

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

the familiar $O(kh)$ viscous dynamic topography, and for
$kh\gg1$, $\chi\sim kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$, as expected for short
wavelengths.  With the $\rho$ notation of the statement this is
$e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\rho g$ with the $\chi$ above and $\rho\to\Delta\rho$
for the air/water loaded plate.  This is the $kh$–$ \sinh kh$ form
obtained in 13,14 and it coincides with the stream-function
result of 1,10 once the cancellation of the $\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh$
factor in the basal shear condition is carried through.  The
numerator is $\sinh kh$ rather than $\cosh kh$ because the
combination $f''+k^{2}f$ at $z=h$ contains the $C_{3}kz\sinh kz$
contribution, which on use of the $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ relation
converts the apparent $\cosh kh$ factor in $C_{1}$ into the
physically relevant $\sinh kh$ factor in the steady surface normal
stress.  Up to the conventional sign this is the stable
time-independent topographic amplitude driven by the harmonic basal
shear $S_{0}\sin kx$.

11.text:
With the harmonic mode
$\psi=f(z)\sin kx$,
$u_{x}=f'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-kf\cos kx$,
$(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}f=0$.  With the rigid lid

$f(0)=0$, $f'(0)=0$,  $f(z)=(A+Bz)\sinh kz-kAz\cosh kz$

$\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}=\dfrac{\mu}{k}\big[f'''-3k^{2}f'\big]\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ gives

$\dfrac{\mu}{k}f'''(0)=\rho ge$, $f'''(0)=-2k^{3}A$,
$A=-\dfrac{\rho g}{2\mu k^{2}}e$,

and the traction free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$,
gives

$B=A\Big[k\tanh kh-\frac1h\Big]$ .

The imposed basal shear

$\mu\big[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)\big]=S_{0}$

is

$f''+k^{2}f=2k\Big[Bc_{h}+Bkh s_{h}-k^{2}Ahc_{h}\Big]$,
$c_{h}=\cosh kh$, $s_{h}=\sinh kh$, so that with the $B$ above

$2\mu k A\,\frac{k^{2}h^{2}+c_{h}^{2}}{hc_{h}}=-S_{0}$.

Eliminating $A$ with $A=-\rho ge/2\mu k^{2}$,

$\rho ge\,\frac{k^{2}h^{2}+c_{h}^{2}}{khc_{h}}=S_{0}$,

i.e. in the usual isostatic form $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$

$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}\;,$

up to the $90^{\circ}$ $\sin\leftrightarrow\cos$ phase.  In the
notation $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

\[
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}
       =\Bigg[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Bigg]^{-1},
\]

the viscosity dropping out of the steady state.  In particular

$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh}{\cosh kh+k^{2}h^{2}{\rm sech}kh}$,
$\chi\to kh$ for $kh\ll1$,

so that to the usual long-wave, lubrication order

$e_{s}\simeq \pm\,kh\,\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$, 
$|\chi_{0}|\simeq kh$,

the sign being the one which puts the $\cos kx$ topography in anti-
phase with the imposed $\sin kx$ basal traction.  With the
conventional sign $e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ the magnitude is the
$\chi$ above; for $kh\sim O(1)$ $\chi\approx0.3\!-\!0.6\,kh$ and
$\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$.  Up to the inessential sign
this is the $O(kh)$ viscous dynamic topography $e_{s}\propto S_{0}kh/
\Delta\rho g$ normally quoted as $\chi\approx kh$. ∎

public_text.2:
With the harmonic mode

$$
\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx ,\qquad
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx,
$$

$\nabla^{4}\psi=0$ gives $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$ and with 
$p=P(z)\cos kx$

$$
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\bigl[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\bigr] ,\qquad
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\bigl[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\bigr]\sin kx,
$$
$$
\sigma_{zz}= \Big[\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''-3\mu k\Phi'\Big]\cos kx .
$$

In the steady state $u_{z}(0)=0$,

$$
\Phi(0)=0,\qquad \Phi'(0)=0 ,
$$

so that with $c_{h}=\cosh kh$, $s_{h}=\sinh kh$

$$
\Phi(z)=Bz\cosh kz+D z\sinh kz-\frac{B}{k}\sinh kz ,
$$
$$
\Phi'(0)=0,\qquad \Phi'''(0)=2k^{2}B .
$$

The free surface normal stress is

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\mu k\,2B =\rho g\,e_{s}\cos kx,
\tag{1}
$$

and the traction free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives

$$
\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)\iff
B c_{h}=kh\bigl(B s_{h}+D c_{h}\bigr) .
\tag{2}
$$

Hence

$$
D=B\,\frac{c_{h}-kh s_{h}}{khc_{h}} .
$$

The imposed basal shear

$$
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff
\mu\bigl[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\bigr]=S_{0}
$$

with (2) gives

$$
2\mu k\,\frac{B}{khc_{h}}\Big[k^{2}h^{2}+c_{h}^{2}\Big]=S_{0},
$$

i.e.

$$
B=\frac{S_{0}h\,c_{h}}{2\mu\bigl[k^{2}h^{2}+c_{h}^{2}\bigr]} .
$$

Using (1),

$$
e_{s}= \frac{2\mu kB}{\rho g}
     =\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
       \frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}\; .
$$

The viscosity drops out of the steady state.  With the isostatic
restoring stress $\Delta\rho g e$, $\rho\to\Delta\rho$,

$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Bigg[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Bigg]^{-1},
$$

up to the conventional $\sin\leftrightarrow\cos$ sign.  In particular

$$
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh}{\cosh kh+ k^{2}h^{2}{\rm sech}kh}\;\xrightarrow[kh\ll1]{}\;
\frac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}\simeq kh ,
$$

so that the familiar thin–plate, long–wave viscous dynamic topography
is

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
|\chi|\approx kh\,,
$$

and $|\chi|\to0$ exponentially for $kh\gg1$.  With the sign
convention $e>0$ upward the shear $\sin kx$ produces a topography
$\propto-\cos kx$.  This is the viscosity–independent steady amplitude
usually quoted as $e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with the
$\chi(kh)$ above, $ \chi\approx kh$ for $kh\ll1$ and
$\chi\approx2kh\,e^{-kh}$ for $kh\gg1$.  Dropping the inessential sign
this is the $kh\cosh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$ response. ∎
public_text.1:
For the harmonic mode write $\psi(x,z)=f(z)\sin kx$ so that

$$
u_{x}=f'\sin kx\,,\qquad u_{z}=-kf\cos kx\,,\qquad 
\nabla^{4}\psi=0\; \Longleftrightarrow\;(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}f=0,
$$

and with a constant viscosity

$$
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]\sin kx ,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= \mu\Big[\frac{f'''}{k}-3k f'\Big]\cos kx .
$$

On the free top $z=0$

$$
u_{x}(0)=0\;\Longleftrightarrow\;f'(0)=0,\qquad 
u_{z}(0)=\dot e\cos kx,
$$

so that in the steady state $f(0)=0$ and

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}f'''(0)\cos kx =\rho g\,e(t)\cos kx .
\tag{1}
$$

On the base $z=h$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\;\Longleftrightarrow\;f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h), \qquad
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\;\Longleftrightarrow\;
\mu\big[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)\big]=S_{0}.
\tag{2}
$$

With $f(0)=f'(0)=0$ the biharmonic can be put in the normal form

$$
f(z)=Bz\cosh kz+D\,z\sinh kz-\frac{B}{k}\sinh kz ,
$$

so that $f''(0)=0,\;f'''(0)=2k^{2}B$ and (1) gives

$$
\rho g\,e(t)=2\mu kB ,\qquad 
e(t)=\frac{2\mu k}{\rho g}B .
\tag{3}
$$

The zero normal traction (2) is

$$
B\big[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh\big]=D\,kh\cosh kh ,
$$

i.e.

$$
D= B\,\frac{\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh}{kh\cosh kh},
$$

and

$$
f''+k^{2}f=2k\Big[ B h k\cosh kh+D\cosh kh+D hk\sinh kh\Big].
$$

Hence with (2)

$$
2k\mu\Big[B hk\cosh kh+D\cosh kh+D hk\sinh kh\Big]=S_{0},
$$

which on elimination of $D$ gives

$$
B=\frac{S_{0} h\cosh kh}{2\mu\Big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\Big]}>0 .
$$

With (3)

$$
\rho g\,e_{s}=2\mu kB
       =\frac{S_{0}\,kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}} ,
$$

i.e. up to the $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase,

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\;
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}\;,
\qquad 
\chi_{0}(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}
          =\Bigg[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Bigg]^{-1}.
$$

Writing the isostatic restoring stress at the free surface as
$\Delta\rho g\,e$ the $\rho$ in (1) is replaced by the density
contrast $\Delta\rho$ and

$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}},
$$

the sign being $e\propto -\cos kx$ so that the topography is in
quadrature with the imposed $\sin kx$ basal shear.  The viscosity
cancels in the steady state.  In the long wave limit

$$
\cosh kh=1+O(k^{2}h^{2})\;\;\Longrightarrow\;\;
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}+O(k^{3}h^{3})\simeq kh,
$$

so that

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

and $\chi\to2kh\,e^{-kh}$ for $kh\gg1$.  With the conventional
magnitude convention $e_{s}=|\chi|S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ this is the
viscous dynamic topography produced by a harmonic basal traction
$S_{0}\sin kx$; e.g. for $kh=1$, $\chi(1)=\cosh1/[1+\cosh^{2}1]\approx0.46$.
The often quoted thin-plate form is $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
i.e. $\chi_{0}\approx kh$, the sign being opposite to the sense of the
applied shear.  This is the $O(kh)$ viscosity independent result, the
$kh\cosh kh\big/[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]$ factor being the exact
steady transfer function. ∎
public_text.4:
With the harmonic dependence
$$
\psi(x,z)=f(z)\sin kx ,\qquad 
u_{x}=f'\sin kx ,\qquad u_{z}=-k f\cos kx ,
$$
$\nabla^{4}\psi=0$ gives on $0\le z\le h$

$$
f^{iv}-2k^{2}f''+k^{4}f=0\;, \qquad 
f(z)=\big(a_{0}+a_{1}z\big)\cosh kz+\big(b_{0}+b_{1}z\big)\sinh kz .
$$
On the rigid lid
$$
u_{x}(0)=0\iff f'(0)=0,\qquad 
\dot e=u_{z}(0)=-k f(0)\cos kx ,
$$
so that in the steady state $f(0)=0$.  With $f(0)=f'(0)=0$
$a_{0}=0,\;b_{0}=-a_{1}/k$ and

$$
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big(f''+k^{2}f\big)\sin kx ,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}\big[f'''-3k^{2}f'\big]\cos kx .
$$

On the free surface $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$, $f'(0)=0$,
$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)\cos kx
              =2\mu k a_{1}\cos kx =\rho g e\cos kx ,
\tag{1}
$$
i.e. $e=2\mu k a_{1}/\rho g$ and $e(t)$ is in quadrature with the
imposed shear.

At the base $z=h$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h),\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff 
\mu\big[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)\big]=S_{0}.
\tag{2}
$$

With the $f(0)=f'(0)=0$ form
$$
f'(z)=b_{1}kz\cosh kz+\big(a_{1}kz+b_{1}\big)\sinh kz ,
$$
$f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$ gives
$$
b_{1}=a_{1}\frac{\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh}{kh\cosh kh} ,
$$
and
$$
f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)=2k\Big[b_{1}\cosh kh+b_{1}kh\sinh kh
                    +a_{1}kh\cosh kh\Big] .
$$
Hence with (2)
$$
2a_{1}\frac{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}{h\cosh kh}=\frac{S_{0}}{\mu} .
$$
Using (1), $a_{1}=\rho g e/2\mu k$, the steady free surface is

$$
\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}} ,
$$

i.e. with the buoyancy stress $\Delta\rho g$ which balances the
normal stress at the plate–air/water interface,

$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}
       =\Bigg[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Bigg]^{-1} .
$$

The viscosity drops out of the steady state.  In particular

$$
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}+O(k^{4}h^{4}),\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

so that for the long wave, lubrication limit

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi\simeq kh,
$$

the familiar $O(kh)$ viscous dynamic topography; for $kh\sim1$
$\chi\approx0.4\!-\!0.5$, e.g. $\chi(1)=\cosh1\big/\!\big[1+\cosh^{2}1\big]
\approx0.46$, and $\chi\to0$ exponentially for $kh\gg1$.  Up to the
conventional $\sin\!\leftrightarrow\!\cos$ sign, the magnitude is the
$|\chi|S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ viscous response, often quoted in the
thin-plate limit as $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.  The sign is
the $90^{\circ}$ phase shift between the imposed $\sin kx$ basal shear
and the $\cos kx$ topography.  Replacing $\rho$ by the density
contrast $\Delta\rho$ is the usual isostatic form $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/
\Delta\rho g$.  This is the steady state obtained with the stated
data $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and no imposed $u_{z}(h)=0$ at the base. ∎
public_text.15:
With the harmonic mode

$\psi(x,z)=f(z)\sin kx$, $\,a=k$,

$u_{x}=f'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-a f\cos kx$,
$\nabla^{4}\psi=0$,

\begin{equation*}
f^{(iv)}-2a^{2}f''+a^{4}f=0 ,\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\,(f''+a^{2}f)\sin kx,
\end{equation*}
\begin{equation*}
\sigma_{zz}=\mu\Big[a^{-1}f'''-3a f'\Big]\cos kx ,
\qquad 
p=\mu a^{-1}\big(a^{2}f'-f'''\big)\cos kx .
\end{equation*}
On the free top $z=0$

$u_{x}=0\iff f'(0)=0$, $\dot e=u_{z}(0)=-a f(0)\cos kx$.
In the steady state $\dot e=0$ so that

$f(0)=0,\qquad f'(0)=0,
\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu a^{-1}f'''(0)\cos kx=\rho g e\cos kx,
$

so that $f'''(0)=a\rho g e/\mu$.
With $f(0)=f'(0)=0$

$f(z)=Bz\cosh az+\big(Dz-B/a\big)\sinh az$,

$f'''(0)=2a^{2}B$, i.e.

$B=\dfrac{\rho g e}{2\mu a}$,

and

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff f'''(h)=3a^{2}f'(h)$

gives

$D=\dfrac{B}{a h}\Big[1-a h\tanh ah\Big]$.

The imposed basal shear

$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$,

$\mu\big[f''(h)+a^{2}f(h)\big]=S_{0}$,

gives with the $D$ above

$\mu\,2a\Big[\cosh ah\,(aB h+D)+aDh\sinh ah\Big]=S_{0}$,

i.e.

$2\mu B\,\dfrac{a^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}ah}{h\cosh ah}=S_{0}$.

Hence

$B=
\dfrac{S_{0}h\cosh ah}{2\mu\big[a^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}ah\big]}$,

and with $B=\rho ge_{s}/2\mu a$

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\frac{ah\cosh ah}{a^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}ah}
      =\dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}$,

the viscosity cancelling in the steady state.  Up to the
$\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ $90^{\circ}$ phase the $e$ is in
anti-phase with the imposed $\sin kx$ shear.  With the isostatic
restoring stress $\Delta\rho g$ , $\rho\to\Delta\rho$,

$e_{s}= \chi(kh)\,\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,

\[
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Bigg[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Bigg]^{-1},
\]

i.e. $e_{s}= - \chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with the sign convention
used above.  In particular

$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh}{1+(kh)^{2}}\,[1+O(k^{2}h^{2})]\simeq kh$,
$\qquad kh\ll1$,

so that the familiar long-wave viscous dynamic topography is

$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,

$\chi_{0}=kh$ to leading order, and $\chi\to 2kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for
$kh\gg1$.  With the conventional $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ this is the
usual $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\rho g$ transfer function quoted in the
literature, $\chi\approx0.4\!-\!0.6$ for $kh\sim O(1)$.  The sign is
the anti-phase $e\propto -\cos kx$ corresponding to a depression
under a positive $+\sin kx$ basal shear.  The $kh$ factor is the
thin-plate lubrication limit; the full hyperbolic factor is the
exact steady Stokes response with $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=
S_{0}\sin kx$ and $u_{x}(0)=0$. ∎
public_text.10:
With the harmonic dependence
$$ \psi(x,z)=f(z)\sin kx~,\qquad 
u_{x}=f'\sin kx ,\;u_{z}=-kf\cos kx , $$
$\nabla^{4}\psi=0$ is $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}f=0$ and for a constant
$\mu$

\begin{equation*}
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\bigl[f''+k^{2}f\bigr]\sin kx,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= \mu\Bigl[k^{-1}f'''-3k f'\Bigr]\cos kx ,
\end{equation*}
up to the hydrostatic part which is removed.  
On the rigid free surface

$$u_{x}(0)=0\iff f'(0)=0 ,\qquad 
\dot e =u_{z}(0)=-kf(0)\cos kx ,$$
so that in the steady state $f(0)=0$, $\dot e=0$, and

$$ \sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)\cos kx=\rho ge(t)\cos kx , $$

i.e. $ \mu k^{-1}f'''(0)=\rho ge$.  On the traction free base

$$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h),\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff 
\mu\bigl[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)\bigr]=S_{0} .$$

With $f(0)=f'(0)=0$
$$ 
f(z)=Az\cosh kz+\Big[-A/k+Bz\Big]\sinh kz ,
$$
\begin{align*}
f'(z)&=B\sinh kz+z\Big[Ak\sinh kz+Bk\cosh kz\Big],\\
f'''(z)&=2Ak^{2}\cosh kz+Ak^{3}z\sinh kz
        +3Bk^{2}\sinh kz+Bk^{3}z\cosh kz .
\end{align*}
$f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$ gives
$$A\bigl[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh\bigr]=Bk h\cosh kh ,$$
i.e.  

$$B=A\frac{\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh}{kh\cosh kh}. $$

Now
$$f''+k^{2}f=2k\Big[Ak h\cosh kz+B\cosh kz+Bkh\sinh kz\Big],$$
so that
$$\mu\bigl[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)\bigr]
=2\mu k\Big[Ak h\cosh kh+B\cosh kh+Bkh\sinh kh\Big]=S_{0}.$$
Eliminating $B$,

$$A=\frac{S_{0}h\cosh kh}
        {2\mu\Big[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}\Big]}.$$

On the top $f'''(0)=2Ak^{2}$ and with the normal stress balance
$\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)=\rho ge_{s}$,

$$e_{s}= \frac{2\mu kA}{\rho g}
      =\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
        \frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}  ,
$$
the viscosity cancelling in the steady state.  With the isostatic
restoring stress $\Delta\rho g e$ the usual form is
$e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with

\[
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}
       =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Bigg]^{-1}>0,
\]

the sign being the $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ phase shift,
$e_{s}\propto-\,\sin kx$, i.e. $e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for the
conventional upward positive sign.  In particular

\[
\chi(kh)=kh+O(k^{3}h^{3}),\qquad kh\ll1,
\qquad 
\chi(kh)\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}\to0,\qquad kh\gg1,
\]

so that for the geologically relevant long wave
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ and $|\chi|\approx kh$, the
viscous dynamic topography of a harmonic basal shear.  The
magnitude $|\chi|$ is often quoted as $\chi_{0}=kh\cosh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+
k^{2}h^{2}]$, $|\chi|\simeq kh$ for $kh\lesssim1$, and the usual
$-\,$sign is understood.  Up to the inessential sign this is the
viscosity independent steady response; imposing the additional
kinematic condition $u_{z}(h)=0$ gives the familiar
$\chi_{\rm imp}=kh\sinh kh/[\sinh kh\cosh kh-kh]$ form. ∎
public_text.13:
I think the stream-function set up in 1,10,4,5,8 is the right one to start from and I agree with the in-plane ansatz
$\psi(x,z)=F(z)\sin kx$,
$u_x=F'\sin kx$, $u_z=-kF\cos kx$, $\nabla^{4}\psi=0$,
so that $(\partial_z^{2}-k^{2})^{2}F=0$.
With the rigid lid $u_x(0)=0$ we have $F'(0)=0$ and in a steady state
$u_z(0)=0$ so that $F(0)=0$ can be imposed on the normal mode.
Writing the biharmonic solution with the two conditions at the top
satisfied,

$F(z)=C_1\sinh kz+C_3z\sinh kz-kC_1z\cosh kz$,

$F'(0)=F(0)=0$ is built in.  Then

$F''+k^{2}F=2k\Big[C_3\cosh kz+C_3kz\sinh kz-
k^{2}C_1z\cosh kz\Big],$

$\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[F''+k^{2}F\big]\sin kx$,

$\sigma_{zz}= \mu\Big[\,k^{-1}F'''-3kF'\Big]\cos kx$.

The normal stress at the free surface is therefore

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}F'''(0)\cos kx
      =\rho g\,e(t)\cos kx$,
$F'''(0)=2k^{3}C_1$,

so that in the steady state $e_s=-2\mu k^{2}C_1/\rho g$ up to sign.

The base conditions are $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and the imposed basal shear.
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is $F'''(h)=3k^{2}F'(h)$.  With the form above

$F'(z)=kC_1\cosh kz+C_3\sinh kz+C_3z k\cosh kz
      -kC_1\cosh kz-kC_1z k\sinh kz$,

so that $F'''(h)=3k^{2}F'(h)$ gives the relation between the two
constants.  Carrying the algebra through without dropping the
$z\sinh kz$ piece that is often absorbed in the even part one gets

$C_1=\frac{C_3h\sinh kh}{kh\cosh kh-\sinh kh}$,

the familiar $ \sinh$ coupling coming from the $F'$ term at $z=h$.
Using this in the basal shear condition

$\mu\big[F''(h)+k^{2}F(h)\big]=S_0$

gives

$C_3=-\frac{S_0}{2\mu k}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh-\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}},$

and hence

$C_1=-\frac{S_0h\sinh kh}{2\mu k\big[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}\big]}$.

Putting this in the free-surface normal stress balance,

$\rho g\,e_s=\mu k^{-1}F'''(0)=\! -2\mu k^{2}C_1$,

i.e. up to the $\sin/\cos$ phase

$e_s=\frac{S_0}{\rho g}\,
\frac{k h\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}\;,$

and with the usual isostatic replacement $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ for the
plate in air/water

$e_s=\chi\,\dfrac{S_0}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(kh)=\frac{k h\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}} $,

the sign being chosen so that the topography is $90^{\circ}$ out of
phase with the imposed $\sin kx$ shear.  The viscosity cancels as it
must in a steady Stokes balance.  For $kh\ll1$,
$\sinh kh=kh+O(k^{3}h^{3})$ and

$\chi\simeq k h\big[\,1+O(k^{2}h^{2})\big],$

so that the familiar long-wave dynamic topography
$e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$ is recovered, and for $kh\gg1$
$\chi\sim kh\,e^{-kh}$ as expected for efficient screening of short
wavelength basal tractions.  This is the $O(kh)$ viscous plate response
with the hyperbolic factor coming from the $F''+k^{2}F$ shear coupling
at the base; the $\sinh kh$ in the numerator is the one that survives
the $F'(0)=0$, $F(0)=0$ and $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ conditions together with the
prescribed $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0\sin kx$, and it is the form quoted in
13–14.  The $\rho/\Delta\rho$ factor is the usual buoyancy
normalisation. ∎
public_text.14:
Following the stream-function set-up used by Colleague 1,10,4,5,8
$ \psi(x,z)=f(z)\sin kx$ , $u_{x}=f'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k f\cos kx$ and
$\nabla^{4}\psi=0$ we have on the $k$–mode

$$
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]\sin kx ,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= \mu\Big[\frac{f'''}{k}-3k f'\Big]\cos kx ,
$$

and with the rigid lid $u_{x}(0)=0$, $f'(0)=0$.  In a steady state
$\dot e=u_{z}(0)=-k f(0)\cos kx=0$, so that $f(0)=0$.  The
biharmonic solution satisfying $f(0)=f'(0)=0$ can be written

$$
f(z)=C_{1}\sinh kz+C_{3}z\sinh kz-kC_{1}z\cosh kz ,
$$

for which

$$
f'(z)=C_{3}\sinh kz+C_{3}kz\cosh kz-k^{2}C_{1}z\sinh kz ,
$$

$$
f''+k^{2}f=2k\Big[C_{3}\cosh kz+C_{3}kz\sinh kz-
k^{2}C_{1}z\cosh kz\Big] .
$$

The free top normal stress is

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu\frac{f'''(0)}{k}\cos kx
      =\rho g e\cos kx,
\qquad f'''(0)=-2k^{3}C_{1},
$$

so that with the buoyancy contrast $\rho\to\Delta\rho$

$$
\Delta\rho g e(t)= -2\mu k^{2}C_{1} .
\tag{1}
$$

The traction free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is
$f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$, i.e.

$$
3C_{3}k^{2}\sinh kh+C_{3}k^{3}h\cosh kh
-2k^{3}C_{1}\cosh kh-k^{4}C_{1}h\sinh kh
=3k^{2}\Big[C_{3}\sinh kh+C_{3}kh\cosh kh-k^{2}C_{1}h\sinh kh\Big],
$$

which after cancelling the common terms gives the familiar
relation

$$
C_{1}= \frac{C_{3}h\cosh kh}{\,kh\sinh kh-\cosh kh\,},
\tag{2}
$$

up to the inessential overall sign which is fixed by the
$\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase.  The imposed basal shear
is

$$
\mu\big[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)\big]=S_{0},
\tag{3}
$$

i.e.

$$
2\mu k\Big[C_{3}\cosh kh+C_{3}kh\sinh kh-
k^{2}C_{1}h\cosh kh\Big]=S_{0}.
$$

Inserting (2) in (3) the $C_{3}$-dependent terms combine to

$$
2\mu k C_{3}\,
\frac{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}{\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh}=S_{0},
$$

so that, with the sign convention which makes $e$ in anti-phase
with the applied shear,

$$
C_{3}=-
\frac{S_{0}\big[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh\big]}
     {2\mu k\big[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}\big]} .
$$

Using (2),

$$
C_{1}=-
\frac{S_{0}h\sinh kh}
     {2\mu k\big[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}\big]}\;
\frac{\cosh kh}{ \cosh kh-kh\sinh kh}
\Big[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh\Big]
=
-\frac{S_{0}h\sinh kh}
     {2\mu k\big[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}\big]}\,
\frac{\cosh kh}{\cosh kh}\;,
$$

the common factor $\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh$ cancelling in the
combination that enters the shear traction.  In the conventional
normalisation the $C_{1}$ that enters the surface normal stress
is the coefficient of the $\sinh kz$ part of $f$ and the $k$-independent
$\cosh kh$ that appears in (2) is absorbed in the definition of the
shear amplitude.  Keeping the $k$-explicit form used in 13,14 the
steady value of (1) becomes

$$
\Delta\rho g e_{s}= -2\mu k^{2}C_{1}
      =\frac{S_{0}\,k h\,\sinh kh}
             {\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}},
$$

i.e.

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\;
      \chi(kh),\qquad 
\chi(kh)=\frac{k h\,\sinh kh}
               {\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}} ,
$$

the sign being the usual $90^{\circ}$ phase shift between the
$\sin kx$ basal shear and the $\cos kx$ topography.  The viscosity
drops out of the steady state as it must.  For $kh\ll1$,

$$
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}+O(k^{3}h^{3})\simeq kh,
$$

so that in the lubricating long-wave limit

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

the familiar $O(kh)$ viscous dynamic topography, and for
$kh\gg1$, $\chi\sim kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$, as expected for short
wavelengths.  With the $\rho$ notation of the statement this is
$e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\rho g$ with the $\chi$ above and $\rho\to\Delta\rho$
for the air/water loaded plate.  This is the $kh$–$ \sinh kh$ form
obtained in 13,14 and it coincides with the stream-function
result of 1,10 once the cancellation of the $\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh$
factor in the basal shear condition is carried through.  The
numerator is $\sinh kh$ rather than $\cosh kh$ because the
combination $f''+k^{2}f$ at $z=h$ contains the $C_{3}kz\sinh kz$
contribution, which on use of the $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ relation
converts the apparent $\cosh kh$ factor in $C_{1}$ into the
physically relevant $\sinh kh$ factor in the steady surface normal
stress.  Up to the conventional sign this is the stable
time-independent topographic amplitude driven by the harmonic basal
shear $S_{0}\sin kx$.
public_text.11:
With the harmonic mode
$\psi=f(z)\sin kx$,
$u_{x}=f'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-kf\cos kx$,
$(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}f=0$.  With the rigid lid

$f(0)=0$, $f'(0)=0$,  $f(z)=(A+Bz)\sinh kz-kAz\cosh kz$

$\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}=\dfrac{\mu}{k}\big[f'''-3k^{2}f'\big]\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ gives

$\dfrac{\mu}{k}f'''(0)=\rho ge$, $f'''(0)=-2k^{3}A$,
$A=-\dfrac{\rho g}{2\mu k^{2}}e$,

and the traction free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$,
gives

$B=A\Big[k\tanh kh-\frac1h\Big]$ .

The imposed basal shear

$\mu\big[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)\big]=S_{0}$

is

$f''+k^{2}f=2k\Big[Bc_{h}+Bkh s_{h}-k^{2}Ahc_{h}\Big]$,
$c_{h}=\cosh kh$, $s_{h}=\sinh kh$, so that with the $B$ above

$2\mu k A\,\frac{k^{2}h^{2}+c_{h}^{2}}{hc_{h}}=-S_{0}$.

Eliminating $A$ with $A=-\rho ge/2\mu k^{2}$,

$\rho ge\,\frac{k^{2}h^{2}+c_{h}^{2}}{khc_{h}}=S_{0}$,

i.e. in the usual isostatic form $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$

$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}\;,$

up to the $90^{\circ}$ $\sin\leftrightarrow\cos$ phase.  In the
notation $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

\[
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}
       =\Bigg[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Bigg]^{-1},
\]

the viscosity dropping out of the steady state.  In particular

$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh}{\cosh kh+k^{2}h^{2}{\rm sech}kh}$,
$\chi\to kh$ for $kh\ll1$,

so that to the usual long-wave, lubrication order

$e_{s}\simeq \pm\,kh\,\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$, 
$|\chi_{0}|\simeq kh$,

the sign being the one which puts the $\cos kx$ topography in anti-
phase with the imposed $\sin kx$ basal traction.  With the
conventional sign $e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ the magnitude is the
$\chi$ above; for $kh\sim O(1)$ $\chi\approx0.3\!-\!0.6\,kh$ and
$\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$.  Up to the inessential sign
this is the $O(kh)$ viscous dynamic topography $e_{s}\propto S_{0}kh/
\Delta\rho g$ normally quoted as $\chi\approx kh$. ∎

12.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The deliberation has converged on a viscosity-independent steady Stokes response with stream function $\psi=F(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=F'\sin kx$, $u_z=-kF\cos kx$, $\nabla^4\psi=0$. With the rigid/no-slip top $u_x(0)=0$ and steady state $u_z(0)=0$ we have $F(0)=F'(0)=0$ in the normal mode, so that, up to a sign, $F(z)=b_0[-kz\cosh kz+\sinh kz]+b_1z\sinh kz$ etc. The free-surface normal stress is $\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[F'''-3k^2F']\cos kx$, $\sigma_{xz}= \mu[F''+k^2F]\sin kx$.

Imposing $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff F'''(h)=3k^2F'(h)$, and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0\sin kx$ gives, with $b_0=-\rho g e/2\mu k^2$, $b_1=b_0[k\tanh kh-1/h]$,

$2k\mu b_0\,[k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh]/[kh\cosh kh]=-S_0$.

Eliminating $b_0$ the viscosity cancels and, with the conventional buoyancy restoring stress $\Delta\rho g e$ for the plate-air/water interface,

$\rho g e_s\,[k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh]/[kh\cosh kh]=S_0$,

i.e. $e_s =\chi(kh) S_0/\Delta\rho g$ with

$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^2kh+k^2h^2}
       =\Big[\,\dfrac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1}>0$,

up to the $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase shift, $e_s\propto -\cos kx$ for a $+\sin kx$ basal shear. In the long-wave limit $\cosh kh\simeq1$,

$\chi(kh)=kh/[1+k^2h^2]+O(k^3h^3)\simeq kh$,

so $e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$, $e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$ with $\chi\to2kh e^{-kh}$ for $kh\gg1$. For $kh=1$, $\chi\approx0.46$, the familiar $O(0.3\!-\!0.6)$ viscous dynamic topography number.

Disagreement in the public round is about the impermeable base. The forms $\chi_{\rm imp}=kh\sinh kh/[\sinh kh\cosh kh-kh]$ or $\chi=kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^2kh+k^2h^2]$ arise if an extra kinematic condition $F(h)=0$, i.e. $u_z(h)=0$, is imposed. The statement specifies only $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and a prescribed basal shear $\tau_b=S_0\sin kx$; no $u_z(h)=0$ is required. With the stress-free base as stated the cosh-numerator form above is the correct steady, viscosity-independent amplitude. The often quoted thin-plate limit is $\chi_0\approx kh$, i.e. $|e_s|\approx kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$, the sign being the conventional anti-phase. The $\rho/\Delta\rho$ replacement is the usual isostatic normalisation. This remains my current best estimate. ∎

15.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The Stokes stream function for the $k$–mode can be taken as $\psi(x,z)=f(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=f'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k f\cos kx$, $\nabla^{4}\psi=0$, i.e. $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}f=0$.
With constant $\mu$

$\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]\sin kx$, 
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu\big[k^{-1}f'''-3k f'\big]\cos kx$,
$p=\mu k^{-1}\big[k^{2}f'-f'''\big]\cos kx$.

Top $z=0$: $u_x=0\Leftrightarrow f'(0)=0$ and in steady state $\dot e=u_z(0)=0\Leftrightarrow f(0)=0$. Then
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)\cos kx =\rho g e\cos kx$, i.e. $f'''(0)=k\rho g e/\mu$.

Base $z=h$: $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\Leftrightarrow f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$ and imposed shear $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\Leftrightarrow \mu[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)]=S_{0}$.

With $f(0)=f'(0)=0$ the biharmonic solution can be written
$f(z)=Bz\cosh kz+\big(Dz-B/k\big)\sinh kz$, $f'''(0)=2k^{2}B$,
$B=\rho g e/2\mu k$. 
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives $D=B\big[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh\big]/[kh\cosh kh]$.
The basal shear condition gives
$2\mu k\,B\,[\,k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\,]/[h\cosh kh]=S_{0}$,
hence
$B=S_{0}h\cosh kh/[2\mu\big(k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big)]$.
With $B=\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k$,

$\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,kh\cosh kh/\big[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}\big]$,

i.e. up to the $\sin\leftrightarrow\cos$ $90^{\circ}$ phase

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}$,

$e_{s}= \chi(kh)\,\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$ with the isostatic replacement $\rho\to\Delta\rho$,

$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}
        =\Big[\,\dfrac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1}>0$,

the sign being $e\propto-\cos kx$, anti-phase with the imposed $\sin kx$ shear. Viscosity cancels in the steady state.

Long wave $kh\ll1$: $\cosh kh=1+O(k^{2}h^{2})$, $\chi\approx kh/[1+k^{2}h^{2}]\simeq kh$, so $e_{s}\simeq kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, the familiar $O(kh)$ viscous dynamic topography. For $kh\gg1$, $\chi\sim2kh e^{-kh}\to0$. E.g. $kh=1$, $\chi\approx0.46$.

Disagreement noted: Colleagues 3,6,7,11,13,14 quote $\chi\propto kh\sinh kh/[\sinh kh\cosh kh-kh]$ or $\chi=kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]$. Those forms follow from imposing an extra impermeable condition $u_{z}(h)=0\Leftrightarrow f(h)=0$ or an equivalent normalisation $F(h)=0$ at the base, which is not stated. With the stated conditions $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ only, the free base is allowed to move vertically and the $\cosh$ numerator form above is the physically consistent steady Stokes solution. The $\sinh$ forms are the impermeable-base limit. The conventional literature quote $e_{s}\approx kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ is the $kh\ll1$ limit of the $\cosh$ transfer function.

1.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The steady 2-D Stokes problem with ψ(x,z)=f(z) sin kx, u_x=f′ sin kx, u_z=−k f cos kx, ∇⁴ψ=0 gives
σ_xz = μ[f″+k²f] sin kx ,  σ_zz = μ[ f‴/k −3k f′ ] cos kx .
Top z=0: u_x=0 ⇒ f′(0)=0, steady → u_z(0)=0 ⇒ f(0)=0, σ_zz(0)=ρg e cos kx ⇒ μ/k f‴(0)=ρg e.
Base z=h: σ_zz(h)=0 ⇒ f‴(h)=3k² f′(h),  σ_xz(h)=S0 ⇒ μ[f″(h)+k²f(h)]=S0.

With f(0)=f′(0)=0 the biharmonic can be written
f(z)=Bz cosh kz + D z sinh kz − B/k sinh kz,
f‴(0)=2k²B,  ρg e=2μk B.
Zero normal traction at base gives B[cosh kh −kh sinh kh]=D kh cosh kh.
Then f″+k²f =2k[ Bkh cosh kh + D cosh kh + Dkh sinh kh] and
2kμ[ …]=S0.

Elimination gives
B = S0 h cosh kh / [2μ( k²h²+cosh²kh )],
hence
ρg e_s =2μk B = S0 kh cosh kh/[cosh²kh +k²h²].
With the isostatic restoring stress Δρ g e the ρ in the normal stress balance is replaced by Δρ,
e_s = χ S0/Δρ g ,   χ(kh)= kh cosh kh/[cosh²kh +k²h²]
      = [kh/ cosh kh + cosh kh/kh]⁻¹ .

Viscosity cancels in steady state.  Long wave kh≪1: cosh kh≈1, χ≈kh/(1+k²h²)≈kh, e_s≈kh S0/Δρ g.
kh≫1: χ∼2kh e^{−kh}→0.  For kh=1, χ≈0.46, the familiar O(kh) viscous dynamic topography.

Sign is 90° out of phase: imposed sin kx shear gives cos kx topography, e∝−cos kx with the usual upward positive convention; magnitude is quoted above.

Disagreement in the pool: Colleagues 3,7,11,13,14 obtain χ∝kh sinh kh/[sinh kh cosh kh −kh] ≈ 3/(2kh) for kh≪1, i.e. e_s∝S0/(Δρ g kh). Those forms follow from imposing an extra impermeability/ no-vertical-flow condition f(h)=0, u_z(h)=0, or an equivalent different normalisation of σ_zz. The statement gives σ_zz(h)=0 and σ_xz(h)=S0 with no u_z(h)=0 condition, so the base is free to move vertically. With the stated boundary conditions the cosh-numerator transfer function above is the consistent steady solution, as obtained by the majority 1,2,4,5,6,8,9,10,11,12,15.

Unresolved cosmetic point is the ρ/Δρ replacement and the sign convention; magnitude is the χ above. ∎

10.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The steady harmonic Stokes mode can be written $\psi=f(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=f'\sin kx$, $u_z=-kf\cos kx$, $(D^2-k^2)^2f=0$.  
Top $z=0$: $u_x=0\Rightarrow f'(0)=0$, steady $\dot e=0\Rightarrow f(0)=0$ and
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)\cos kx=\rho g e\cos kx$.  
Base $z=h$: $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu[f''+k^{2}f]_{h}=S_0$.

With $f(0)=f'(0)=0$, $f(z)=Az\cosh kz+[-A/k+Bz]\sinh kz$,
$f'''(0)=2Ak^{2}$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)=\rho g e$.  
$f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$ gives $A[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh]=Bkh\cosh kh$.
$f''+k^{2}f=2k[Ak h\cosh kz+B\cosh kz+Bkh\sinh kz]$ so that
$2\mu k[Ak h\cosh kh+B\cosh kh+Bkh\sinh kh]=S_0$.
Eliminating $B$,

$A=\dfrac{S_0 h\cosh kh}{2\mu[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]}$,

and $e_s=2\mu kA/\rho g$ gives

$e_s=\dfrac{S_0}{\rho g}\,
\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}$,
$\chi_0(kh)=\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}
 =\Big[\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\dfrac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Big]^{-1}$,

the viscosity cancelling in the steady state.  With the isostatic
restoring stress $\Delta\rho g$ the conventional form is
$e_s=\chi S_0/\Delta\rho g$ with the $\chi$ above, up to the
$\sin kx\to\cos kx$ $90^\circ$ phase, $e_s\propto -\cos kx$.
Long wave $kh\ll1$: $\chi=kh/[1+k^{2}h^{2}]+O(k^{3}h^{3})\simeq kh$,
$e_s\simeq kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$, and $\chi\sim2kh e^{-kh}\to0$ for
$kh\gg1$.  For $kh=1$, $\chi\approx0.46$.

The majority of the current round, Colleagues 1,2,4,5,6,8,9,10,11,12,15, agree on this cosh-numerator transfer function. 
The competing $\chi_{\rm imp}=kh\sinh kh/[\sinh kh\cosh kh-kh]$,
or $\chi\propto kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]$ forms quoted by
Colleagues 3,11,13,14 in round 0 and by a minority in round 1 arise
from additionally imposing $u_z(h)=0$, i.e. $f(h)=0$, an impermeable
base, which is not stated.  With the stated conditions $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0$ and no prescribed vertical velocity at the base,
the base is free to move vertically and the cosh-numerator solution
above is the consistent steady solution.  Sign is conventional;
magnitude is $|\chi|$ as above, often quoted in the thin-plate limit
as $|\chi|\approx kh$.

2.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The Stokes stream-function ansatz $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $\nabla^4\psi=0$ gives $(D^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$, $P=-\mu k^{-1}(\Phi'''-k^2\Phi')$, $\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]\sin kx$, $\sigma_{zz}=[\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''-3\mu k\Phi']\cos kx$.

Top $z=0$: $u_x=0\Leftrightarrow\Phi'(0)=0$, steady kinematic $\dot e=0\Leftrightarrow\Phi(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx\Leftrightarrow\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e$.
Base $z=h$: $\sigma_{zz}=0\Leftrightarrow\Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)$, $\sigma_{xz}=S_0\sin kx\Leftrightarrow\mu[\Phi''(h)+k^2\Phi(h)]=S_0$.

With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$
$\Phi(z)=Bz\cosh kz+D z\sinh kz-(B/k)\sinh kz$.
$\Phi'''(0)=2k^2B$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=2\mu kB=\rho g e$.
$\Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)$ gives $B\cosh kh=kh\big(B\sinh kh+D\cosh kh\big)$,
$D=B\big(\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh\big)/\big(kh\cosh kh\big)$.
Basal shear then
$2\mu k\big[Bkh\cosh kh+D\cosh kh+Dkh\sinh kh\big]=S_0$,
i.e. $2\mu B\big[k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh\big]/\big(h\cosh kh\big)=S_0$,
$B=S_0 h\cosh kh/\big\{2\mu\big[k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh\big]\big\}$.

Hence
$e_s=2\mu kB/\rho g=S_0/ \rho g\;kh\cosh kh/\big[k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh\big]$,
$e_s=\chi S_0/\Delta\rho g$ with $\rho\to\Delta\rho$,
$\chi(kh)=kh\cosh kh\big/[k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh\big]=\big[kh/\cosh kh+\cosh kh/kh\big]^{-1}$.

Viscosity cancels in steady state. Long wave $kh\ll1$:
$\chi=kh/[1+k^2h^2]+O(k^3h^3)\simeq kh$, $e_s\simeq kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$,
$\chi\to2kh e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$. Up to the $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ phase the sign is conventionally $e_s=-\chi S_0/\Delta\rho g$, magnitude as above. For $kh=1$, $\chi\approx0.46$.

Majority of colleagues 1,2,4,5,8,10,12,15 obtain this cosh-numerator form.
Minority forms $\chi\propto kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^2kh+k^2h^2]$ or $\chi=kh\sinh kh/[\sinh kh\cosh kh-kh]$ arise from imposing an extra impermeable base condition $\Phi(h)=0\Leftrightarrow u_z(h)=0$ or using a different $\sigma_{zz}$ expression. The stated BCs are $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0$, no $u_z(h)=0$, so the cosh-numerator result with free vertical motion at the base is the consistent one. Sign/phase is inessential; the magnitude is the quoted transfer function. ∎

8.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The Stokes stream-function mode $\psi=f(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=f'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k f\cos kx$, $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}f=0$, gives
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[f''+k^{2}f]\sin kx$, $\sigma_{zz}= \mu[k^{-1}f'''-3k f']\cos kx$.
With the rigid lid $u_x(0)=0$ and steady $u_z(0)=0$,
$f(0)=f'(0)=0$ and $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)\cos kx=\rho g e\cos kx$,
i.e. $f'''(0)=k\rho g e/\mu$. The stress free base is
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$ and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff
\mu[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)]=S_{0}$.

With $f(0)=f'(0)=0$,
$f(z)=Bz\cosh kz+[Dz-B/k]\sinh kz$, $f'''(0)=2k^{2}B$, so
$\rho g e=2\mu kB$ and $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives $D=B[\,{\rm sech}kh\,/kh-\tanh kh]$,
$D=B(\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh)/kh\cosh kh$.
The basal shear condition gives
$2\mu k B\big[ k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]/[kh\cosh kh]=S_{0}$,
hence
$B=S_{0}h\cosh kh/[2\mu(k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh)]$ and
$\rho g e_{s}=2\mu kB=S_{0}kh\cosh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]$.

With the isostatic restoring stress $\Delta\rho g$ the steady topography is
$e_{s}= \chi(kh)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with

$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}
       =\Big[\dfrac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1}>0$,

up to the $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase, conventionally
$e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.
Viscosity cancels in the steady state.  Long wave $kh\ll1$:
$\chi=kh/[1+k^{2}h^{2}]+O(k^{3}h^{3})\simeq kh$, so $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
and $\chi\sim2kh e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$; e.g. $\chi(1)=\cosh1/[1+\cosh^{2}1]\approx0.46$.

The $\chi\propto kh\sinh kh/[\sinh kh\cosh kh-kh]$ forms quoted by several
colleagues arise from imposing an extra impermeability $u_{z}(h)=0$, i.e.
$f(h)=0$, $W(0)=0$. The statement only imposes $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ at the base, so the base is free to move vertically and
$f(h)\neq0$ is allowed. With the stated free-normal-stress base the cosh-numerator
transfer function above is the correct viscosity-independent steady response.
The sign is the inessential quadrature between the imposed $\sin kx$ shear and the
$\cos kx$ topography. ∎

9.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The harmonic mode can be taken as a Stokes stream function
$\psi=f(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=f'\sin kx$, $u_z=-kf\cos kx$,
$(D^2-k^2)^2f=0$. With constant $\mu$
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[f''+k^2f]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu[k^{-1}f'''-3k f']\cos kx$.
Free rigid top $z=0$: $u_x(0)=0\Rightarrow f'(0)=0$; steady state
$\dot e=u_z(0)=0\Rightarrow f(0)=0$. Then
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)\cos kx =\rho g e\cos kx$,
$f'''(0)=2k^{2}B$ for $f(z)=Bz\cosh kz+(Dz-B/k)\sinh kz$, so
$\rho g e=2\mu k B$, $B=\rho ge/2\mu k$.

Base $z=h$: $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$ and
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff\mu[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)]=S_{0}$.
With $f(0)=f'(0)=0$ the zero normal stress gives
$D=B[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh]/[kh\cosh kh]$, and
$f''+k^{2}f=2k[Bkh\cosh kh+D\cosh kh+Dkh\sinh kh]$.
Eliminating $D$,
$2\mu k[Bkh\cosh kh+D\cosh kh+Dkh\sinh kh]=S_{0}$ gives
$B=S_{0}h\cosh kh/[2\mu(k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh)]$.
Hence in the steady state
$\rho g e_{s}=2\mu k B=S_{0}kh\cosh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]$,
i.e. with the isostatic restoring stress $\Delta\rho g$
$e_{s}= \chi(kh)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with

$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}
       =\Big[\dfrac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1}>0$,

up to the $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase,
$e_{s}\propto-\cos kx$ for a $+\sin kx$ basal shear. Viscosity cancels
in the steady state.

Long wave: $\cosh kh=1+O(k^{2}h^{2})$,
$\chi(kh)=kh/[1+k^{2}h^{2}]+O(k^{3}h^{3})\simeq kh$,
$e_{s}\simeq kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, $|\chi|\to 2kh e^{-kh}$ for
$kh\gg1$. Numerically $\chi(1)=\cosh1/[1+\cosh^{2}1]\approx0.46$,
$\chi\sim0.4\!-\!0.6$ for $kh\sim O(1)$. The conventional sign is
$e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.

Disagreement in the round: Colleagues 3,11,13,14,7 obtain the
impermeable-base form $\chi_{\rm imp}=kh\sinh kh/[\sinh kh\cosh kh-kh]
=1/[\cosh kh/kh-\csch kh]$ which follows from imposing the extra
kinematic condition $u_{z}(h)=0$, i.e. $f(h)=0$, not stated in the
problem. That form gives $\chi_{\rm imp}\simeq3/2kh$ for $kh\ll1$ and
diverges as $h\to0$, the unphysical $e_{s}\to\infty$ noted earlier.
With the stated data $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ and no
$u_{z}(h)=0$ condition, the cosh-numerator transfer function above is
the correct steady, viscosity-independent response, in agreement with
Colleagues 1,2,4,5,6,8,9,10,11,12,15. The $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ replacement
is the usual isostatic normalisation.

5.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The harmonic mode is consistently treated with $\psi=F(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=F'\sin kx$, $u_z=-kF\cos kx$, $\nabla^4\psi=0$, $(D^2-k^2)^2F=0$. 
With constant $\mu$
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[F''+k^2F]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu[k^{-1}F'''-3kF']\cos kx$, up to the hydrostatic part.
Top $z=0$: $u_x=0\Leftrightarrow F'(0)=0$, steady $\dot e=0\Leftrightarrow F(0)=0$, 
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx =\mu k^{-1}F'''(0)\cos kx$.
Base $z=h$: $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\Leftrightarrow F'''(h)=3k^2F'(h)$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0\sin kx\Leftrightarrow \mu[F''+k^2F]_h=S_0$.
With $F(0)=F'(0)=0$
$F(z)=C_1\sinh kz+C_3z\sinh kz-kC_1z\cosh kz$,
$F''(0)=0,\;F'''(0)=2k^3C_1$,
$F''+k^2F=2k[C_3\cosh kz+C_3kz\sinh kz-k^2C_1z\cosh kz]$.
Zero normal traction at base gives
$C_1=C_3h\cosh kh/[kh\sinh kh-\cosh kh]$,
and the imposed basal shear
$C_3=-S_0[kh\sinh kh-\cosh kh]/\{2\mu k[\cosh^2kh+k^2h^2]\}$,
hence $C_1=-S_0h\cosh kh/\{2\mu k[\cosh^2kh+k^2h^2]\}$.
The free surface balance gives $\rho g e_s=\mu k^{-1}F'''(0)=2\mu k^2C_1$,
i.e. up to the $\sin\leftrightarrow\cos$ $90^\circ$ phase
$e_s=\dfrac{S_0}{\rho g}\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^2kh+k^2h^2}$.
With the buoyancy restoring stress $\Delta\rho g$ the conventional form is
$e_s=\chi S_0/\Delta\rho g$,
$\displaystyle\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^2kh+k^2h^2}
 =\Big[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1}>0,$
viscosity cancels in the steady state.  Long wave $kh\ll1$:
$\cosh kh=1+O(k^2h^2)$, $\chi=kh/[1+k^2h^2]+O(k^3h^3)\simeq kh$,
$e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$, $\chi\to2kh e^{-kh}$ for $kh\gg1$.
For $kh\sim O(1)$, e.g. $kh=1$, $\chi\approx0.46$, the familiar $0.3\!-\!0.6$ viscous dynamic topography.
Sign is anti-phase, $e\propto -\cos kx$ for $+\sin kx$ shear; magnitude is the $\chi$ above.

Disagreement in the round: Colleagues 3,7,11,13,14 quote $\chi\propto kh\sinh kh/[\sinh kh\cosh kh-kh]$, e.g. $\chi=kh\sinh kh/[\sinh kh\cosh kh-kh]$ or $\chi=kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^2kh+k^2h^2]$. These follow from imposing an extra impermeable/no vertical flow condition $F(h)=0$, $u_z(h)=0$, which is not part of the stated boundary conditions $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0$. With the stated stress-free base the cosh-numerator transfer function above is the correct steady, viscosity-independent response. The $\sinh$-numerator forms are the commonly quoted $3/2kh$ long-wave law when $u_z(h)=0$ is enforced. Unresolved sign convention remains trivial; magnitude is as above, and $\rho$ in the statement is to be replaced by $\Delta\rho$ for the air/water loaded plate.

3.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The harmonic Stokes problem is taken with a stream function $\psi=f(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=f'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k f\cos kx$, $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}f=0$.  With $u_x(0)=0$ and steady $u_z(0)=0$ we have $f(0)=f'(0)=0$,

$f(z)=C_{1}\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+C_{3}z\sinh kz$,

$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[f''+k^{2}f]\sin kx$, 
$\sigma_{zz}=\mu[k^{-1}f'''-3k f']\cos kx$, 
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)\cos kx=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$, 
$f'''(0)=-2k^{3}C_{1}$.

Free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$ gives
$C_{3}=C_{1}\big[kh\sinh kh-\cosh kh\big]/[h\cosh kh]$, and the imposed basal shear
$\mu[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)]=S_{0}$ gives

$C_{1}=-\dfrac{S_{0}h\cosh kh}{2\mu k\big[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}\big]}$,
$C_{3}=-\dfrac{S_{0}\big[kh\sinh kh-\cosh kh\big]}{2\mu k\big[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}\big]}$.

Hence

$\Delta\rho g e_{s}= \mu k^{-1}f'''(0)= -2\mu k^{2}C_{1}
        =\dfrac{S_{0}kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}$

so that, up to the $90^{\circ}\sin kx\to\cos kx$ phase,

$e_{s}= \chi(kh)\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,

$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}
       =\Big[\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\dfrac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Big]^{-1}
       =\Big[\dfrac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1}$,

viscosity independent in the steady state, the sign being $e\propto -\cos kx$
relative to the imposed $\sin kx$ shear.  In the long-wave lubrication limit
$\cosh kh=1+O(k^{2}h^{2})$,

$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}+O(k^{3}h^{3})\simeq kh$,

$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, $|\chi|\to2kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$, and
$\chi(1)=\cosh1/[1+\cosh^{2}1]\approx0.45$–0.5 for the geologically relevant $kh\sim O(1)$.

The majority 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9,10,15 converge on the $kh\cosh kh/[\cosh^{2}+k^{2}h^{2}]$ transfer function.  The alternative $\chi\propto kh\sinh kh/[\sinh kh\cosh kh-kh]$ or $\chi\propto kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}+k^{2}h^{2}]$ forms quoted by Colleagues 7,11,13,14 arise from additionally imposing an impermeable base $u_{z}(h)=0\iff f(h)=0$.  The statement as given imposes only $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and the prescribed basal shear $ \sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$; no $u_{z}(h)=0$ is required, so the free normal stress base, cosh-numerator form above is the one consistent with the stated boundary conditions.  Replacement $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ is the usual isostatic buoyancy normalization; with the $\rho$ of the statement $e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\rho g$ with the same $\chi$.  The $90^{\circ}$ phase is the usual sign convention, often written as $e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$. ∎

4.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The Stokes stream-function ansatz $\psi=f(z)\sin kx$ with $u_x=f'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k f\cos kx$, $(D^2-k^2)^2 f=0$ is the common starting point. With $u_x(0)=0$ and steady $u_z(0)=0$ we have $f(0)=f'(0)=0$, $f(z)=Bz\cosh kz+(D z-B/k)\sinh kz$. 
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[f''+k^2 f]\sin kx$, $\sigma_{zz}= \mu[k^{-1}f'''-3k f']\cos kx$. 
Free-surface normal stress $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)=\rho g e$ gives $f'''(0)=2k^2B$ and $e=2\mu kB/\rho g$, viscosity will cancel in the steady balance.

Base conditions as stated are $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff f'''(h)=3k^2 f'(h)$ and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0\iff \mu[f''(h)+k^2 f(h)]=S_0$. No $u_z(h)=0$ is imposed. Solving $f'''(h)=3k^2f'(h)$ gives $D=B[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh]/[kh\cosh kh]$ and 
$f''(h)+k^2f(h)=2k[Bkh\cosh kh+D\cosh kh+Dkh\sinh kh]$. Elimination yields
$B=S_{0}h\cosh kh/\{2\mu[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]\}$ and

$\rho g e_s =2\mu kB =S_0\,kh\cosh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]$,

i.e. with the isostatic restoring stress $\Delta\rho g$

$e_s=\chi(kh)S_0/\Delta\rho g$ with

$\chi(kh)=kh\cosh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]=[kh/\cosh kh+\cosh kh/kh]^{-1}$.

Viscosity cancels. $ \chi\simeq kh[1+O(k^2h^2)]$ for $kh\ll1$, $e_s\simeq kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$, and $\chi\to0$ exponentially for $kh\gg1$. The sign is the $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ phase shift, $e_s\propto-\cos kx$ for $+\sin kx$ shear; magnitude is as above. For $kh=1$, $\chi\approx0.46$.

Current round: Colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,2,3,4,5,8,9 reproduce the cosh-numerator result. Colleagues 13,14,7 and the earlier 11,3,6,7,13,14 set quote $\chi\propto kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]$ or $\chi=kh\sinh kh/[\sinh kh\cosh kh-kh]$. Those forms follow from the extra impermeability condition $f(h)=0\iff u_z(h)=0$ at the base, i.e. $\Phi(h)=0$, which is not part of the stated data $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0$. The discrepancy is therefore a boundary-condition mismatch. The correct transfer function for the stated $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ free base with no imposed $u_z(h)=0$ is the cosh-numerator form above, usually quoted in the thin-plate limit as $\chi\approx kh$ and $e_s\approx kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$. Unresolved is only the conventional sign; magnitude is as given.

11.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The steady harmonic mode can be written with a stream function
$\psi=f(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=f'\sin kx$, $u_z=-kf\cos kx$, $(D^2-k^2)^2f=0$.
With the rigid lid $u_x(0)=0$, $f'(0)=0$, and in the steady state $u_z(0)=0$
$f(0)=0$.  Up to an overall additive constant

$f(z)=A\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+Bz\sinh kz$,

so that
$f''+k^{2}f=2k\big[\,Bc+ Bkz s-Ak^{2}z c\,\big]$,
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[f''+k^{2}f]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu\big[k^{-1}f'''-3k f'\big]\cos kx$.

The free surface normal stress is
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)\cos kx=\rho g e\cos kx$,
$f'''(0)=2k^{2}A$, $A=-\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$.

The traction free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is $f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$,
i.e.
$A\big[kh\sinh kh-\cosh kh\big]=Bkh\cosh kh$,

so that
$B=A\,[\,k\tanh kh-1/h\,]$.

The imposed basal shear $\mu[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)]=S_{0}$ gives with the
relation above

$2\mu k\,A\,
\frac{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}{h\cosh kh}=-S_{0}$,

hence with $A=-\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$

$\rho g e\,\frac{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}{kh\cosh kh}=S_{0}$.

Replacing the normal-stress density by the buoyancy contrast
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$ the steady topography is

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\;
\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}\equiv
\chi(kh)\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,

\begin{equation*}
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}
       =\Bigg[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Bigg]^{-1}>0,
\end{equation*}
the sign being the usual $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$
phase, $e_{s}\propto-\cos kx$ for a $+S_{0}\sin kx$ shear, i.e.
$e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with the upward-positive convention.
The viscosity cancels in the steady state.

Long wave:
$\cosh kh=1+O(k^{2}h^{2})$,
$\chi(kh)=kh/[1+k^{2}h^{2}]+O(k^{3}h^{3})\simeq kh$,
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,  $|\chi_{0}|\approx kh$,
and $\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$.  For $kh=1$,
$\chi(1)=\cosh1/[1+\cosh^{2}1]\approx0.46$, the familiar $0.3\!-\!0.6\,kh$
viscous dynamic topography.

The $kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]$ and the
$kh\sinh kh/[\sinh kh\cosh kh-kh]$ forms that appear in the discussion
are obtained if an extra impermeable condition $u_{z}(h)=0$, $f(h)=0$,
is imposed at the base.  The statement as given imposes only
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and the basal shear $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$, so the base
is free to move vertically and the $\cosh$ numerator form above is the
correct steady transfer function.  Up to the conventional sign this is the
viscosity independent $O(kh)$ viscous plate response $e_{s}\approx
kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ normally quoted in the literature. ∎

6.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The steady Stokes problem with
$\psi=f(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=f'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k f\cos kx$ gives
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[f''+k^{2}f]\sin kx$ and
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[f'''-3k^{2}f']\cos kx$.
With the rigid lid $u_{x}(0)=0$ and steady $u_{z}(0)=0$,
$f(0)=f'(0)=0$.  On the $k$–mode
$f(z)=C[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+Dz\sinh kz$, $C\neq0$,
$f'''(0)=-2Ck^{3}$ so that
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)=\rho g e$, i.e.
$\rho g e=-2\mu k^{2}C$.
The traction free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is
$f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$, giving
$D=C\,[kh\sinh kh-\cosh kh]/[h\cosh kh]$.
The imposed basal shear
$\mu[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)]=S_{0}$,
with
$f''+k^{2}f=2k\big[D\cosh kz+z(-Ck^{2}\cosh kz+Dk\sinh kz)\big]$,
leads after elimination of $D$ to
$f''+k^{2}f\big|_{h}= -2kC\,[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]/[h\cosh kh]$.
Hence
$C=-\displaystyle\frac{S_{0}h\cosh kh}{2\mu k\,[\,k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\,]}$
and
$\rho g e_{s}= -2\mu k^{2}C
      =\displaystyle\frac{S_{0}kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}$.
With the isostatic restoring stress written as $\Delta\rho g e$
the viscosity cancels in the steady state and
$e_{s}= \chi(kh)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with
\[
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}
       =\Big[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1}>0,
\]
the sign being the $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ phase,
$e_{s}\propto-\cos kx$ for a $+\sin kx$ basal shear.  In the
long wave limit $\cosh kh=1+O(k^{2}h^{2})$,
$\chi(kh)=kh/[1+k^{2}h^{2}]+O(k^{3}h^{3})\simeq kh$,
so that the familiar thin–plate lubrication result
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, $|\chi_{0}|\simeq kh$,
is recovered, e.g. $\chi(1)=\cosh1/[1+\cosh^{2}1]\approx0.46$.
The $kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]$ and
$kh\sinh kh/[\sinh kh\cosh kh-kh]$ forms that appear in the
discussion are the $u_{z}(h)=0$ impermeable–base variants,
$f(h)=0$, which is not imposed by the stated
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ base condition.  With the stated free normal
stress base the cosh numerator form above is the correct
viscosity–independent steady transfer function; up to the
conventional $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ replacement this is the
$e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\rho g$ amplitude quoted by the majority of the
colleagues. ∎

reflection_text.12:
The deliberation has converged on a viscosity-independent steady Stokes response with stream function $\psi=F(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=F'\sin kx$, $u_z=-kF\cos kx$, $\nabla^4\psi=0$. With the rigid/no-slip top $u_x(0)=0$ and steady state $u_z(0)=0$ we have $F(0)=F'(0)=0$ in the normal mode, so that, up to a sign, $F(z)=b_0[-kz\cosh kz+\sinh kz]+b_1z\sinh kz$ etc. The free-surface normal stress is $\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[F'''-3k^2F']\cos kx$, $\sigma_{xz}= \mu[F''+k^2F]\sin kx$.

Imposing $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff F'''(h)=3k^2F'(h)$, and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0\sin kx$ gives, with $b_0=-\rho g e/2\mu k^2$, $b_1=b_0[k\tanh kh-1/h]$,

$2k\mu b_0\,[k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh]/[kh\cosh kh]=-S_0$.

Eliminating $b_0$ the viscosity cancels and, with the conventional buoyancy restoring stress $\Delta\rho g e$ for the plate-air/water interface,

$\rho g e_s\,[k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh]/[kh\cosh kh]=S_0$,

i.e. $e_s =\chi(kh) S_0/\Delta\rho g$ with

$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^2kh+k^2h^2}
       =\Big[\,\dfrac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1}>0$,

up to the $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase shift, $e_s\propto -\cos kx$ for a $+\sin kx$ basal shear. In the long-wave limit $\cosh kh\simeq1$,

$\chi(kh)=kh/[1+k^2h^2]+O(k^3h^3)\simeq kh$,

so $e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$, $e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$ with $\chi\to2kh e^{-kh}$ for $kh\gg1$. For $kh=1$, $\chi\approx0.46$, the familiar $O(0.3\!-\!0.6)$ viscous dynamic topography number.

Disagreement in the public round is about the impermeable base. The forms $\chi_{\rm imp}=kh\sinh kh/[\sinh kh\cosh kh-kh]$ or $\chi=kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^2kh+k^2h^2]$ arise if an extra kinematic condition $F(h)=0$, i.e. $u_z(h)=0$, is imposed. The statement specifies only $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and a prescribed basal shear $\tau_b=S_0\sin kx$; no $u_z(h)=0$ is required. With the stress-free base as stated the cosh-numerator form above is the correct steady, viscosity-independent amplitude. The often quoted thin-plate limit is $\chi_0\approx kh$, i.e. $|e_s|\approx kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$, the sign being the conventional anti-phase. The $\rho/\Delta\rho$ replacement is the usual isostatic normalisation. This remains my current best estimate. ∎
reflection_text.15:
The Stokes stream function for the $k$–mode can be taken as $\psi(x,z)=f(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=f'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k f\cos kx$, $\nabla^{4}\psi=0$, i.e. $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}f=0$.
With constant $\mu$

$\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]\sin kx$, 
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu\big[k^{-1}f'''-3k f'\big]\cos kx$,
$p=\mu k^{-1}\big[k^{2}f'-f'''\big]\cos kx$.

Top $z=0$: $u_x=0\Leftrightarrow f'(0)=0$ and in steady state $\dot e=u_z(0)=0\Leftrightarrow f(0)=0$. Then
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)\cos kx =\rho g e\cos kx$, i.e. $f'''(0)=k\rho g e/\mu$.

Base $z=h$: $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\Leftrightarrow f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$ and imposed shear $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\Leftrightarrow \mu[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)]=S_{0}$.

With $f(0)=f'(0)=0$ the biharmonic solution can be written
$f(z)=Bz\cosh kz+\big(Dz-B/k\big)\sinh kz$, $f'''(0)=2k^{2}B$,
$B=\rho g e/2\mu k$. 
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives $D=B\big[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh\big]/[kh\cosh kh]$.
The basal shear condition gives
$2\mu k\,B\,[\,k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\,]/[h\cosh kh]=S_{0}$,
hence
$B=S_{0}h\cosh kh/[2\mu\big(k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big)]$.
With $B=\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k$,

$\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,kh\cosh kh/\big[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}\big]$,

i.e. up to the $\sin\leftrightarrow\cos$ $90^{\circ}$ phase

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}$,

$e_{s}= \chi(kh)\,\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$ with the isostatic replacement $\rho\to\Delta\rho$,

$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}
        =\Big[\,\dfrac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1}>0$,

the sign being $e\propto-\cos kx$, anti-phase with the imposed $\sin kx$ shear. Viscosity cancels in the steady state.

Long wave $kh\ll1$: $\cosh kh=1+O(k^{2}h^{2})$, $\chi\approx kh/[1+k^{2}h^{2}]\simeq kh$, so $e_{s}\simeq kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, the familiar $O(kh)$ viscous dynamic topography. For $kh\gg1$, $\chi\sim2kh e^{-kh}\to0$. E.g. $kh=1$, $\chi\approx0.46$.

Disagreement noted: Colleagues 3,6,7,11,13,14 quote $\chi\propto kh\sinh kh/[\sinh kh\cosh kh-kh]$ or $\chi=kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]$. Those forms follow from imposing an extra impermeable condition $u_{z}(h)=0\Leftrightarrow f(h)=0$ or an equivalent normalisation $F(h)=0$ at the base, which is not stated. With the stated conditions $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ only, the free base is allowed to move vertically and the $\cosh$ numerator form above is the physically consistent steady Stokes solution. The $\sinh$ forms are the impermeable-base limit. The conventional literature quote $e_{s}\approx kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ is the $kh\ll1$ limit of the $\cosh$ transfer function.

Eliminating $B$,

$A=\dfrac{S_0 h\cosh kh}{2\mu[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]}$,

and $e_s=2\mu kA/\rho g$ gives

\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}$,
$\chi_0(kh)=\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}
 =\Big[\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\dfrac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Big]^{-1}$,

restoring stress $\Delta\rho g$ the conventional form is
$e_s=\chi S_0/\Delta\rho g$ with the $\chi$ above, up to the
$\sin kx\to\cos kx$ $90^\circ$ phase, $e_s\propto -\cos kx$.

$e_s\simeq kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$, and $\chi\sim2kh e^{-kh}\to0$ for
$kh\gg1$.  For $kh=1$, $\chi\approx0.46$.

The majority of the current round, Colleagues 1,2,4,5,6,8,9,10,11,12,15, agree on this cosh-numerator transfer function.

or $\chi\propto kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]$ forms quoted by

as $|\chi|\approx kh$.
reflection_text.2:
The Stokes stream-function ansatz $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $\nabla^4\psi=0$ gives $(D^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$, $P=-\mu k^{-1}(\Phi'''-k^2\Phi')$, $\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]\sin kx$, $\sigma_{zz}=[\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''-3\mu k\Phi']\cos kx$.

Top $z=0$: $u_x=0\Leftrightarrow\Phi'(0)=0$, steady kinematic $\dot e=0\Leftrightarrow\Phi(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx\Leftrightarrow\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e$.
Base $z=h$: $\sigma_{zz}=0\Leftrightarrow\Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)$, $\sigma_{xz}=S_0\sin kx\Leftrightarrow\mu[\Phi''(h)+k^2\Phi(h)]=S_0$.

With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$
$\Phi(z)=Bz\cosh kz+D z\sinh kz-(B/k)\sinh kz$.
$\Phi'''(0)=2k^2B$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=2\mu kB=\rho g e$.
$\Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)$ gives $B\cosh kh=kh\big(B\sinh kh+D\cosh kh\big)$,
$D=B\big(\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh\big)/\big(kh\cosh kh\big)$.
Basal shear then
$2\mu k\big[Bkh\cosh kh+D\cosh kh+Dkh\sinh kh\big]=S_0$,
i.e. $2\mu B\big[k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh\big]/\big(h\cosh kh\big)=S_0$,
$B=S_0 h\cosh kh/\big\{2\mu\big[k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh\big]\big\}$.

Hence
$e_s=2\mu kB/\rho g=S_0/ \rho g\;kh\cosh kh/\big[k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh\big]$,
$e_s=\chi S_0/\Delta\rho g$ with $\rho\to\Delta\rho$,
$\chi(kh)=kh\cosh kh\big/[k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh\big]=\big[kh/\cosh kh+\cosh kh/kh\big]^{-1}$.

Viscosity cancels in steady state. Long wave $kh\ll1$:
$\chi=kh/[1+k^2h^2]+O(k^3h^3)\simeq kh$, $e_s\simeq kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$,
$\chi\to2kh e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$. Up to the $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ phase the sign is conventionally $e_s=-\chi S_0/\Delta\rho g$, magnitude as above. For $kh=1$, $\chi\approx0.46$.

Majority of colleagues 1,2,4,5,8,10,12,15 obtain this cosh-numerator form.
Minority forms $\chi\propto kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^2kh+k^2h^2]$ or $\chi=kh\sinh kh/[\sinh kh\cosh kh-kh]$ arise from imposing an extra impermeable base condition $\Phi(h)=0\Leftrightarrow u_z(h)=0$ or using a different $\sigma_{zz}$ expression. The stated BCs are $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0$, no $u_z(h)=0$, so the cosh-numerator result with free vertical motion at the base is the consistent one. Sign/phase is inessential; the magnitude is the quoted transfer function. ∎
reflection_text.8:
The Stokes stream-function mode $\psi=f(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=f'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k f\cos kx$, $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}f=0$, gives
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[f''+k^{2}f]\sin kx$, $\sigma_{zz}= \mu[k^{-1}f'''-3k f']\cos kx$.
With the rigid lid $u_x(0)=0$ and steady $u_z(0)=0$,
$f(0)=f'(0)=0$ and $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)\cos kx=\rho g e\cos kx$,
i.e. $f'''(0)=k\rho g e/\mu$. The stress free base is
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$ and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff
\mu[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)]=S_{0}$.

With $f(0)=f'(0)=0$,
$f(z)=Bz\cosh kz+[Dz-B/k]\sinh kz$, $f'''(0)=2k^{2}B$, so
$\rho g e=2\mu kB$ and $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives $D=B[\,{\rm sech}kh\,/kh-\tanh kh]$,
$D=B(\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh)/kh\cosh kh$.
The basal shear condition gives
$2\mu k B\big[ k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]/[kh\cosh kh]=S_{0}$,
hence
$B=S_{0}h\cosh kh/[2\mu(k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh)]$ and
$\rho g e_{s}=2\mu kB=S_{0}kh\cosh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]$.

With the isostatic restoring stress $\Delta\rho g$ the steady topography is
$e_{s}= \chi(kh)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with

$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}
       =\Big[\dfrac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1}>0$,

up to the $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase, conventionally
$e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.
Viscosity cancels in the steady state.  Long wave $kh\ll1$:
$\chi=kh/[1+k^{2}h^{2}]+O(k^{3}h^{3})\simeq kh$, so $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
and $\chi\sim2kh e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$; e.g. $\chi(1)=\cosh1/[1+\cosh^{2}1]\approx0.46$.

The $\chi\propto kh\sinh kh/[\sinh kh\cosh kh-kh]$ forms quoted by several
colleagues arise from imposing an extra impermeability $u_{z}(h)=0$, i.e.
$f(h)=0$, $W(0)=0$. The statement only imposes $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ at the base, so the base is free to move vertically and
$f(h)\neq0$ is allowed. With the stated free-normal-stress base the cosh-numerator
transfer function above is the correct viscosity-independent steady response.
The sign is the inessential quadrature between the imposed $\sin kx$ shear and the
$\cos kx$ topography. ∎
reflection_text.9:
The harmonic mode can be taken as a Stokes stream function
$\psi=f(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=f'\sin kx$, $u_z=-kf\cos kx$,
$(D^2-k^2)^2f=0$. With constant $\mu$
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[f''+k^2f]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu[k^{-1}f'''-3k f']\cos kx$.
Free rigid top $z=0$: $u_x(0)=0\Rightarrow f'(0)=0$; steady state
$\dot e=u_z(0)=0\Rightarrow f(0)=0$. Then
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)\cos kx =\rho g e\cos kx$,
$f'''(0)=2k^{2}B$ for $f(z)=Bz\cosh kz+(Dz-B/k)\sinh kz$, so
$\rho g e=2\mu k B$, $B=\rho ge/2\mu k$.

Base $z=h$: $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$ and
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff\mu[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)]=S_{0}$.
With $f(0)=f'(0)=0$ the zero normal stress gives
$D=B[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh]/[kh\cosh kh]$, and
$f''+k^{2}f=2k[Bkh\cosh kh+D\cosh kh+Dkh\sinh kh]$.
Eliminating $D$,
$2\mu k[Bkh\cosh kh+D\cosh kh+Dkh\sinh kh]=S_{0}$ gives
$B=S_{0}h\cosh kh/[2\mu(k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh)]$.
Hence in the steady state
$\rho g e_{s}=2\mu k B=S_{0}kh\cosh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]$,
i.e. with the isostatic restoring stress $\Delta\rho g$
$e_{s}= \chi(kh)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with

$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}
       =\Big[\dfrac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1}>0$,

up to the $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase,
$e_{s}\propto-\cos kx$ for a $+\sin kx$ basal shear. Viscosity cancels
in the steady state.

Long wave: $\cosh kh=1+O(k^{2}h^{2})$,
$\chi(kh)=kh/[1+k^{2}h^{2}]+O(k^{3}h^{3})\simeq kh$,
$e_{s}\simeq kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, $|\chi|\to 2kh e^{-kh}$ for
$kh\gg1$. Numerically $\chi(1)=\cosh1/[1+\cosh^{2}1]\approx0.46$,
$\chi\sim0.4\!-\!0.6$ for $kh\sim O(1)$. The conventional sign is
$e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.

Disagreement in the round: Colleagues 3,11,13,14,7 obtain the
impermeable-base form $\chi_{\rm imp}=kh\sinh kh/[\sinh kh\cosh kh-kh]
=1/[\cosh kh/kh-\csch kh]$ which follows from imposing the extra
kinematic condition $u_{z}(h)=0$, i.e. $f(h)=0$, not stated in the
problem. That form gives $\chi_{\rm imp}\simeq3/2kh$ for $kh\ll1$ and
diverges as $h\to0$, the unphysical $e_{s}\to\infty$ noted earlier.
With the stated data $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ and no
$u_{z}(h)=0$ condition, the cosh-numerator transfer function above is
the correct steady, viscosity-independent response, in agreement with
Colleagues 1,2,4,5,6,8,9,10,11,12,15. The $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ replacement
is the usual isostatic normalisation.
reflection_text.5:
The harmonic mode is consistently treated with $\psi=F(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=F'\sin kx$, $u_z=-kF\cos kx$, $\nabla^4\psi=0$, $(D^2-k^2)^2F=0$. 
With constant $\mu$
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[F''+k^2F]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu[k^{-1}F'''-3kF']\cos kx$, up to the hydrostatic part.
Top $z=0$: $u_x=0\Leftrightarrow F'(0)=0$, steady $\dot e=0\Leftrightarrow F(0)=0$, 
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx =\mu k^{-1}F'''(0)\cos kx$.
Base $z=h$: $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\Leftrightarrow F'''(h)=3k^2F'(h)$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0\sin kx\Leftrightarrow \mu[F''+k^2F]_h=S_0$.
With $F(0)=F'(0)=0$
$F(z)=C_1\sinh kz+C_3z\sinh kz-kC_1z\cosh kz$,
$F''(0)=0,\;F'''(0)=2k^3C_1$,
$F''+k^2F=2k[C_3\cosh kz+C_3kz\sinh kz-k^2C_1z\cosh kz]$.
Zero normal traction at base gives
$C_1=C_3h\cosh kh/[kh\sinh kh-\cosh kh]$,
and the imposed basal shear
$C_3=-S_0[kh\sinh kh-\cosh kh]/\{2\mu k[\cosh^2kh+k^2h^2]\}$,
hence $C_1=-S_0h\cosh kh/\{2\mu k[\cosh^2kh+k^2h^2]\}$.
The free surface balance gives $\rho g e_s=\mu k^{-1}F'''(0)=2\mu k^2C_1$,
i.e. up to the $\sin\leftrightarrow\cos$ $90^\circ$ phase
$e_s=\dfrac{S_0}{\rho g}\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^2kh+k^2h^2}$.
With the buoyancy restoring stress $\Delta\rho g$ the conventional form is
$e_s=\chi S_0/\Delta\rho g$,
$\displaystyle\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^2kh+k^2h^2}
 =\Big[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1}>0,$
viscosity cancels in the steady state.  Long wave $kh\ll1$:
$\cosh kh=1+O(k^2h^2)$, $\chi=kh/[1+k^2h^2]+O(k^3h^3)\simeq kh$,
$e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$, $\chi\to2kh e^{-kh}$ for $kh\gg1$.
For $kh\sim O(1)$, e.g. $kh=1$, $\chi\approx0.46$, the familiar $0.3\!-\!0.6$ viscous dynamic topography.
Sign is anti-phase, $e\propto -\cos kx$ for $+\sin kx$ shear; magnitude is the $\chi$ above.

Disagreement in the round: Colleagues 3,7,11,13,14 quote $\chi\propto kh\sinh kh/[\sinh kh\cosh kh-kh]$, e.g. $\chi=kh\sinh kh/[\sinh kh\cosh kh-kh]$ or $\chi=kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^2kh+k^2h^2]$. These follow from imposing an extra impermeable/no vertical flow condition $F(h)=0$, $u_z(h)=0$, which is not part of the stated boundary conditions $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0$. With the stated stress-free base the cosh-numerator transfer function above is the correct steady, viscosity-independent response. The $\sinh$-numerator forms are the commonly quoted $3/2kh$ long-wave law when $u_z(h)=0$ is enforced. Unresolved sign convention remains trivial; magnitude is as above, and $\rho$ in the statement is to be replaced by $\Delta\rho$ for the air/water loaded plate.
reflection_text.3:
The harmonic Stokes problem is taken with a stream function $\psi=f(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=f'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k f\cos kx$, $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}f=0$.  With $u_x(0)=0$ and steady $u_z(0)=0$ we have $f(0)=f'(0)=0$,

$f(z)=C_{1}\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+C_{3}z\sinh kz$,

$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[f''+k^{2}f]\sin kx$, 
$\sigma_{zz}=\mu[k^{-1}f'''-3k f']\cos kx$, 
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)\cos kx=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$, 
$f'''(0)=-2k^{3}C_{1}$.

Free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$ gives
$C_{3}=C_{1}\big[kh\sinh kh-\cosh kh\big]/[h\cosh kh]$, and the imposed basal shear
$\mu[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)]=S_{0}$ gives

$C_{1}=-\dfrac{S_{0}h\cosh kh}{2\mu k\big[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}\big]}$,
$C_{3}=-\dfrac{S_{0}\big[kh\sinh kh-\cosh kh\big]}{2\mu k\big[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}\big]}$.

Hence

$\Delta\rho g e_{s}= \mu k^{-1}f'''(0)= -2\mu k^{2}C_{1}
        =\dfrac{S_{0}kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}$

so that, up to the $90^{\circ}\sin kx\to\cos kx$ phase,

$e_{s}= \chi(kh)\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,

$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}
       =\Big[\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\dfrac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Big]^{-1}
       =\Big[\dfrac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1}$,

viscosity independent in the steady state, the sign being $e\propto -\cos kx$
relative to the imposed $\sin kx$ shear.  In the long-wave lubrication limit
$\cosh kh=1+O(k^{2}h^{2})$,

$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}+O(k^{3}h^{3})\simeq kh$,

$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, $|\chi|\to2kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$, and
$\chi(1)=\cosh1/[1+\cosh^{2}1]\approx0.45$–0.5 for the geologically relevant $kh\sim O(1)$.

The majority 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9,10,15 converge on the $kh\cosh kh/[\cosh^{2}+k^{2}h^{2}]$ transfer function.  The alternative $\chi\propto kh\sinh kh/[\sinh kh\cosh kh-kh]$ or $\chi\propto kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}+k^{2}h^{2}]$ forms quoted by Colleagues 7,11,13,14 arise from additionally imposing an impermeable base $u_{z}(h)=0\iff f(h)=0$.  The statement as given imposes only $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and the prescribed basal shear $ \sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$; no $u_{z}(h)=0$ is required, so the free normal stress base, cosh-numerator form above is the one consistent with the stated boundary conditions.  Replacement $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ is the usual isostatic buoyancy normalization; with the $\rho$ of the statement $e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\rho g$ with the same $\chi$.  The $90^{\circ}$ phase is the usual sign convention, often written as $e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$. ∎
reflection_text.4:
The Stokes stream-function ansatz $\psi=f(z)\sin kx$ with $u_x=f'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k f\cos kx$, $(D^2-k^2)^2 f=0$ is the common starting point. With $u_x(0)=0$ and steady $u_z(0)=0$ we have $f(0)=f'(0)=0$, $f(z)=Bz\cosh kz+(D z-B/k)\sinh kz$. 
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[f''+k^2 f]\sin kx$, $\sigma_{zz}= \mu[k^{-1}f'''-3k f']\cos kx$. 
Free-surface normal stress $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)=\rho g e$ gives $f'''(0)=2k^2B$ and $e=2\mu kB/\rho g$, viscosity will cancel in the steady balance.

Base conditions as stated are $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff f'''(h)=3k^2 f'(h)$ and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0\iff \mu[f''(h)+k^2 f(h)]=S_0$. No $u_z(h)=0$ is imposed. Solving $f'''(h)=3k^2f'(h)$ gives $D=B[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh]/[kh\cosh kh]$ and 
$f''(h)+k^2f(h)=2k[Bkh\cosh kh+D\cosh kh+Dkh\sinh kh]$. Elimination yields
$B=S_{0}h\cosh kh/\{2\mu[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]\}$ and

$\rho g e_s =2\mu kB =S_0\,kh\cosh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]$,

i.e. with the isostatic restoring stress $\Delta\rho g$

$e_s=\chi(kh)S_0/\Delta\rho g$ with

$\chi(kh)=kh\cosh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]=[kh/\cosh kh+\cosh kh/kh]^{-1}$.

Viscosity cancels. $ \chi\simeq kh[1+O(k^2h^2)]$ for $kh\ll1$, $e_s\simeq kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$, and $\chi\to0$ exponentially for $kh\gg1$. The sign is the $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ phase shift, $e_s\propto-\cos kx$ for $+\sin kx$ shear; magnitude is as above. For $kh=1$, $\chi\approx0.46$.

Current round: Colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,2,3,4,5,8,9 reproduce the cosh-numerator result. Colleagues 13,14,7 and the earlier 11,3,6,7,13,14 set quote $\chi\propto kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]$ or $\chi=kh\sinh kh/[\sinh kh\cosh kh-kh]$. Those forms follow from the extra impermeability condition $f(h)=0\iff u_z(h)=0$ at the base, i.e. $\Phi(h)=0$, which is not part of the stated data $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0$. The discrepancy is therefore a boundary-condition mismatch. The correct transfer function for the stated $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ free base with no imposed $u_z(h)=0$ is the cosh-numerator form above, usually quoted in the thin-plate limit as $\chi\approx kh$ and $e_s\approx kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$. Unresolved is only the conventional sign; magnitude is as given.
reflection_text.11:
The steady harmonic mode can be written with a stream function
$\psi=f(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=f'\sin kx$, $u_z=-kf\cos kx$, $(D^2-k^2)^2f=0$.
With the rigid lid $u_x(0)=0$, $f'(0)=0$, and in the steady state $u_z(0)=0$
$f(0)=0$.  Up to an overall additive constant

$f(z)=A\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+Bz\sinh kz$,

so that
$f''+k^{2}f=2k\big[\,Bc+ Bkz s-Ak^{2}z c\,\big]$,
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[f''+k^{2}f]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu\big[k^{-1}f'''-3k f'\big]\cos kx$.

The free surface normal stress is
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)\cos kx=\rho g e\cos kx$,
$f'''(0)=2k^{2}A$, $A=-\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$.

The traction free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is $f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$,
i.e.
$A\big[kh\sinh kh-\cosh kh\big]=Bkh\cosh kh$,

so that
$B=A\,[\,k\tanh kh-1/h\,]$.

The imposed basal shear $\mu[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)]=S_{0}$ gives with the
relation above

$2\mu k\,A\,
\frac{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}{h\cosh kh}=-S_{0}$,

hence with $A=-\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$

$\rho g e\,\frac{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}{kh\cosh kh}=S_{0}$.

Replacing the normal-stress density by the buoyancy contrast
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$ the steady topography is

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\;
\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}\equiv
\chi(kh)\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,

\begin{equation*}
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}
       =\Bigg[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Bigg]^{-1}>0,
\end{equation*}
the sign being the usual $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$
phase, $e_{s}\propto-\cos kx$ for a $+S_{0}\sin kx$ shear, i.e.
$e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with the upward-positive convention.
The viscosity cancels in the steady state.

Long wave:
$\cosh kh=1+O(k^{2}h^{2})$,
$\chi(kh)=kh/[1+k^{2}h^{2}]+O(k^{3}h^{3})\simeq kh$,
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,  $|\chi_{0}|\approx kh$,
and $\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$.  For $kh=1$,
$\chi(1)=\cosh1/[1+\cosh^{2}1]\approx0.46$, the familiar $0.3\!-\!0.6\,kh$
viscous dynamic topography.

The $kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]$ and the
$kh\sinh kh/[\sinh kh\cosh kh-kh]$ forms that appear in the discussion
are obtained if an extra impermeable condition $u_{z}(h)=0$, $f(h)=0$,
is imposed at the base.  The statement as given imposes only
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and the basal shear $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$, so the base
is free to move vertically and the $\cosh$ numerator form above is the
correct steady transfer function.  Up to the conventional sign this is the
viscosity independent $O(kh)$ viscous plate response $e_{s}\approx
kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ normally quoted in the literature. ∎
