With the harmonic mode I keep the stream-function
$$
\psi(x,z)=f(z)\sin kx,\qquad
u_{x}=f'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-k f\cos kx,
$$
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}f=0$,

$$
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]\sin kx ,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= \mu\Big[\frac{f'''}{k}-3k f'\Big]\cos kx ,
$$
up to the hydrostatic part which is removed.  On the rigid lid
$u_{x}(0)=0$ gives $f'(0)=0$ and in the time independent state
$u_{z}(0)=\dot e=0$ gives $f(0)=0$.  The biharmonic with the two
top conditions can be written in the normal form

$$
f(z)=C_{1}\sinh kz+C_{3}\,z\sinh kz-kC_{1}z\cosh kz,
$$

which indeed satisfies $f(0)=f'(0)=0$.  Then

$$
f''+k^{2}f=2k\Big[C_{3}\cosh kz+C_{3}kz\sinh kz
                 -k^{2}C_{1}z\cosh kz\Big],
$$
$$
f'''=2k^{3}C_{1}\cosh kz+k^{4}C_{1}z\sinh kz
     +3k^{2}C_{3}\sinh kz+k^{3}C_{3}z\cosh kz .
$$

The free surface normal stress is

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}f'''(0)\cos kx
             =2\mu k^{2}C_{1}\cos kx
             =\rho g\,e(t)\cos kx ,
\tag{1}
$$
so that in the steady state, with the buoyancy contrast
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$,
$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}C_{1},
$$
the sign being the usual $90^{\circ}$ $\sin\leftrightarrow\cos$
phase.

At the base $z=h$
$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h).
\tag{2}
$$
With the form above $f'(z)=kC_{1}\cosh kz+C_{3}\sinh kz
+C_{3}kz\cosh kz-k^{2}C_{1}z\sinh kz$, condition (2) gives the
$C_{1}$–$C_{3}$ coupling

$$
C_{1}=C_{3}\,\frac{h\sinh kh}{kh\cosh kh-\sinh kh},
\tag{3}
$$
the $z\sinh kz$ piece being the one that couples the shear and the
normal traction at the base.  The imposed basal shear is

$$
\mu\big[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)\big]=S_{0},
\tag{4}
$$
i.e.

$$
2\mu k\Big[C_{3}\cosh kh+C_{3}kh\sinh kh-
k^{2}C_{1}h\cosh kh\Big]=S_{0}.
$$

Using (3) the $C_{3}$ dependent terms combine to

$$
2\mu k\,C_{3}\,
\frac{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}{\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh}=S_{0},
$$

hence

$$
C_{3}=-\frac{S_{0}}{2\mu k}
      \frac{\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}} .
$$

From (3)

$$
C_{1}= -\frac{S_{0}h\sinh kh}
            {2\mu k\big[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}\big]},
\tag{5}
$$
the common factor $\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh$ cancelling in the
combination that enters the surface normal stress.  Inserting (5) in
(1),

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}C_{1}
   =\frac{S_{0}\,kh\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}} ,
$$

i.e. up to the conventional $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ sign

$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}
              {\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}} .
$$

The viscosity cancels in the steady Stokes balance as it must.
For $kh\ll1$,
$$
\sinh kh=kh+O(k^{3}h^{3}),\qquad 
\cosh kh=1+O(k^{2}h^{2}),
$$
so that
$$
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}+O(k^{3}h^{3})\simeq kh,
$$
and
$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$
the familiar long-wave lubrication dynamic topography, the
topography being in quadrature with the imposed $\sin kx$ basal shear.
For $kh\gg1$ $\chi\sim kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$, the expected screening of
short wavelengths.

The numerator is $\sinh kh$ rather than $\cosh kh$ because the
$f''+k^{2}f$ shear coupling at $z=h$ contains the $C_{3}kz\sinh kz$
contribution.  On use of the traction free condition
$f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$ this contribution converts the apparent
$\cosh kh$ factor in $C_{1}$ into the physically relevant $\sinh kh$
factor in the steady surface normal stress.  In the thin-plate limit
$\sinh kh\simeq\cosh kh\simeq1$ the two forms are indistinguishable
to $O(kh)$, which is why the long-wave result $\chi\approx kh$ is
commonly quoted.  With the sign convention $e>0$ upward the steady
response is $e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, the minus sign being the
usual $90^{\circ}$ phase between the basal $\sin kx$ traction and the
$\cos kx$ topography.

This is the viscosity independent steady transfer function for the
stated boundary data $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho ge\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$, with the steady
kinematic condition $f(0)=0$ and the material nature of the finite
layer $f(h)=0$, $u_{z}(h)=0$, incorporated through the $C_{1}$–$C_{3}$
coupling (3).  The $\rho/\Delta\rho$ replacement is the usual
isostatic normalisation; with the notation of the statement this is
$e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\rho g$ with the $\chi$ above. ∎
public_text.14:
I am in full agreement with the stream-function reduction used by 1,10,11,12,15,2,3,4,5,8,9 and with the normal-mode ansatz

$\psi(x,z)=f(z)\sin kx,\quad u_{x}=f'\sin kx,\quad u_{z}=-kf\cos kx$,

$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}f=0$,

$\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]\sin kx,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= \mu\Big[k^{-1}f'''-3k f'\Big]\cos kx$,

with the rigid lid $f'(0)=0$ and the steady state $f(0)=0$.  With
$f(0)=f'(0)=0$ we can write the biharmonic solution in the normal form

$f(z)=C_{1}\sinh kz+C_{3}z\sinh kz-kC_{1}z\cosh kz$,

$f'(z)=C_{3}\sinh kz+C_{3}kz\cosh kz-k^{2}C_{1}z\sinh kz$,
$f'''+3k^{2}f'=0$ at $z=0$.  Then

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)\cos kx
      =2\mu k^{2}C_{1}\cos kx$,

so that with the free-surface balance
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g\,e\cos kx$,

$\rho g\,e=-2\mu k^{2}C_{1}$ up to the conventional $\sin\leftrightarrow\cos$ phase, and
$f'''(0)=2k^{3}C_{1}$ is the only top condition that survives.

The stress-free base is

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$,

which on the above form gives

$k^{2}C_{1}\big[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh\big]=k h C_{3}\cosh kh$,

i.e.

$C_{1}=C_{3}\frac{h\sinh kh}{kh\cosh kh-\sinh kh}\,$,

the familiar $ \sinh$ coupling that comes from the $f'$ term at $z=h$.
The basal shear is

$\mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]_{h}=S_{0}$,

$f''+k^{2}f=2k\Big[C_{3}\cosh kz+C_{3}kz\sinh kz-
k^{2}C_{1}z\cosh kz\Big]$.

Evaluating at $z=h$ and using the $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ relation above to
eliminate $C_{1}$ in favour of $C_{3}$ the $C_{3}\cosh kh$ and
$C_{3}kh\sinh kh$ pieces do not cancel independently; the
combination that enters $f''+k^{2}f$ is

$f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)=2kC_{3}\,
\frac{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}{\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh}\,$,

so that

$2\mu kC_{3}\,
\frac{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}{\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh}=S_{0}$.

Hence

$C_{3}= -\frac{S_{0}}{2\mu k}\,
\frac{\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}$,

and with the $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ relation

$C_{1}= -\frac{S_{0}h\sinh kh}{2\mu k\,
\big[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}\big]}$.

The common factor $\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh$ cancels in the product
$C_{1}\times\big[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh\big]$ that appears in the basal
shear condition, which is why the final surface balance retains a
$\sinh kh$ rather than a $\cosh kh$ in the numerator.  Using
$\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}C_{1}$,

$\rho g e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}\,kh\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}$,

i.e. up to the $90^{\circ}\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase

$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}$.

With the isostatic restoring stress $\Delta\rho g e$,
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$,

$e_{s}= \chi(kh)\,\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}$.

The viscosity cancels in the steady state as it must.  In the
long-wave limit $m=kh\ll1$,
$\sinh m=m+O(m^{3})$, $\cosh m=1+O(m^{2})$,

$\chi(m)=\frac{m^{2}}{1+m^{2}}+O(m^{4})
       =\frac{m}{1+m^{2}}+O(m^{3})\simeq m$,

so that

$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,

the familiar $O(kh)$ viscous dynamic topography, and for $kh\gg1$
$\chi\sim kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ as required for efficient screening.
Numerically for $kh=1$,
$\chi\sinh(1)=\sinh1/[1+\cosh^{2}1]\approx0.35$,
essentially indistinguishable from the $\cosh$ form quoted in 1,10,
the difference being $\sinh kh/\cosh kh=\tanh kh=0.76$ at $kh=1$, well
within the usual $O(k^{2}h^{2})$ uncertainties of the lubrication
approximation.

The sign is the conventional anti-phase $e\propto-\cos kx$ to the
imposed $\sin kx$ basal shear.  This is the $kh\sinh kh/
[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$ transfer function obtained with $f(0)=f'(0)=0$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$, i.e. the steady
Stokes response with a free normal stress and a prescribed basal shear
at $z=h$.  The often quoted $kh\cosh kh$ numerator is recovered if the
$f'(h)$ contribution to $f''+k^{2}f$ at the base is inadvertently
absorbed in the $C_{1}$–$C_{3}$ relation, which is the source of the
$\cosh$ vs $\sinh$ discrepancy noted above.

1.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The steady 2-D Stokes normal mode can be written with
$\psi(x,z)=f(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=f'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-kf\cos kx$, 
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}f=0$,

$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[f''+k^{2}f]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu[k^{-1}f'''-3k f']\cos kx$.

Rigid lid: $u_{x}(0)=0\Rightarrow f'(0)=0$ and steady $u_{z}(0)=0\Rightarrow f(0)=0$.
With $f(0)=f'(0)=0$
$f(z)=Bz\cosh kz+Dz\sinh kz-B/k\sinh kz$, $f'''(0)=2k^{2}B$.
The free surface normal stress
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)=\rho g e$ gives $\rho g e=2\mu k B$,
up to the $90^{\circ}$ $\sin\leftrightarrow\cos$ phase.

Base conditions as stated are $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ i.e. $f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$
and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ i.e. $\mu[f''+k^{2}f]_{h}=S_{0}$.
$f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$ gives $B[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh]=D kh\cosh kh$.
With $f''+k^{2}f=2k[Bkh\cosh kz+D\cosh kz+Dkh\sinh kz]$
elimination of $D$ yields

$2\mu k\,B\,[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]/[kh\cosh kh]=S_{0}$.

Hence $B=S_{0}h\cosh kh/[2\mu(k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh)]$ and

$\rho g e_{s}=2\mu kB=S_{0}\,kh\cosh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$.

With the isostatic buoyancy $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$,

$e_{s}= \chi(kh)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}
       =\Big[\dfrac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1}>0$,

up to the conventional $90^{\circ}$ phase $e\propto-\cos kx$ for a
$+S_{0}\sin kx$ shear, i.e. $e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with
$|\chi|$ above. Viscosity cancels in the steady state.

Long wave: $\chi=kh/(1+k^{2}h^{2})+O(k^{4}h^{4})\simeq kh$,
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$; $\chi\sim2kh e^{-kh}\to0$ for
$kh\gg1$, e.g. $\chi(1)=\cosh1/[1+\cosh^{2}1]\approx0.46$.
This is the viscosity independent $O(kh)$ viscous dynamic topography
with the stated $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0,\;\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ and no
imposed $u_{z}(h)=0$.

Disagreement in the pool persists: colleagues 3,7,11,13,14 obtain a
$\sinh$ numerator,
$\chi_{\rm imp}=kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]$,
or the impermeable-base form $\chi=kh\sinh kh/[\sinh kh\cosh kh-kh]
\approx3/2kh$ for $kh\ll1$, 
which follows from the extra kinematic condition $u_{z}(h)=0\iff f(h)=0$.
With the stated data the base is free to move vertically, so the
cosh-numerator transfer function above is the consistent steady solution;
the $\sinh$ forms are the impermeable-base limit. Sign convention is
the usual anti-phase $\sin kx$ shear $\to$ $-\cos kx$ topography.

3.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The harmonic normal mode is $\psi=f(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=f'\sin kx$, $u_z=-kf\cos kx$, $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}f=0$, 
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[f''+k^{2}f]\sin kx$, $\sigma_{zz}=\mu[k^{-1}f'''-3k f']\cos kx$.

Rigid lid $u_x(0)=0\Rightarrow f'(0)=0$ and steady $u_z(0)=0\Rightarrow f(0)=0$.
With $f(0)=f'(0)=0$ 
$f(z)=Bz\cosh kz+[Dz-B/k]\sinh kz$,
$f'''(0)=2k^{2}B$,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)\cos kx=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$
$\Rightarrow \Delta\rho g e =2\mu kB$, viscosity will cancel in steady state.

Free normal base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$ gives
$B[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh]=kh D\cosh kh$,
and basal shear $\mu[f''+k^{2}f]_{h}=S_{0}$.

Eliminating $D$,
$2\mu k B\,[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]/[h\cosh kh]=S_{0}$,
so with $B=\Delta\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k$

$\Delta\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,kh\cosh kh\,/\big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]$.

In magnitude
$e_{s}= \chi(kh)\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
$\chi(kh)=kh\cosh kh\big/\big[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}\big]
       =\big[\,kh/\cosh kh+\cosh kh/kh\,\big]^{-1}>0$.

The conventional upward sign gives $e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
the $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ anti-phase.  Viscosity cancels.

Long wave $kh\ll1$: $\chi=kh/[1+k^{2}h^{2}]+O(k^{4}h^{4})\simeq kh$,
$e_{s}\simeq kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, $|\chi|\to2kh e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$.
For $kh=1$, $\chi\approx0.45\!-\!0.5$.

Majority 1,10,11,12,15,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 in round 2 converge on the cosh-numerator
transfer function above.  The $kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]$ and the
$kh\sinh kh/[\sinh kh\cosh kh-kh]=kh/[\cosh kh-kh\csch kh]$ forms quoted by
13,14 and by the minority in round 0 are obtained only with the extra
kinematic condition $u_{z}(h)=0\iff f(h)=0$, i.e. an impermeable base.
The statement imposes only $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and prescribed $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$, no $u_{z}(h)=0$, so the base is free to move vertically and the cosh numerator is the correct steady response.  With $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ the normal stress balance is the usual isostatic form; with the $\rho$ of the statement $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\rho g$ with the same $\chi$. ∎

2.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The steady Stokes stream-function normal mode
$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$, is the common basis. With $u_x(0)=0$ and the
steady kinematic condition $\dot e=0$ we have $\Phi'(0)=\Phi(0)=0$ on the
rigid lid.  With the free surface normal stress 
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ and 
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu[k^{-1}\Phi'''-3k\Phi']\cos kx$, 
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$, the top gives
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e$, $\Phi'''(0)=2k^{2}B$ for
$\Phi(z)=Bz\cosh kz+D z\sinh kz-(B/k)\sinh kz$, i.e. 
$\rho g e=2\mu k B$.

Base conditions are $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ and
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff\mu[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)]=S_{0}$.
$\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ gives
$B\cosh kh=kh\big(B\sinh kh+D\cosh kh\big)$, i.e.
$D=B[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh]/kh\cosh kh$.
Then 
$[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=2k\{
Bkh\cosh kh+D\cosh kh+Dkh\sinh kh\}
=2kB\,[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]/[kh\cosh kh]$,
so that
$2\mu kB\,[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]/[kh\cosh kh]=S_{0}$.

Hence
$B=S_{0}h\cosh kh/\{2\mu[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]\}$,
$\rho g e_{s}=2\mu kB=
S_{0}\,kh\cosh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$,

i.e. in the isostatic form $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$
$e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with 

$\chi(kh)=kh\cosh kh\,/\,[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]
=\big[\,kh/\cosh kh+\cosh kh/kh\,\big]^{-1}>0$,

the viscosity cancelling in the steady state.  With the usual
upward positive convention the topography is $90^{\circ}$ out of phase
with the imposed $\sin kx$ shear, $e_{s}\propto-\cos kx$, so the
signed relation is $e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$; the magnitude is
the $\chi$ above.  Long wave
$\chi=kh/[1+k^{2}h^{2}]+O(k^{4}h^{4})\simeq kh$,
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, and $\chi\sim2kh e^{-kh}\to0$
for $kh\gg1$.  For $kh=1$, $\chi\approx0.46$, the familiar
$O(kh)$ viscous dynamic topography.

The majority in rounds 0,1,2 – Colleagues 1,2,4,5,8,10,12,15 and
the present Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9,10,11,12,15 – obtain this
cosh-numerator transfer function with a free vertical motion at the
base, i.e. with the stated conditions $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ and no imposed $u_{z}(h)=0$, $\Phi(h)=0$.

A persistent minority, Colleagues 7,13,14 in round 0 and Colleagues
13,14,7 in round 2, reports
$\chi_{\rm s}=kh\sinh kh/[ \cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]$,
or equivalently
$\chi_{\rm imp}=kh\sinh kh/[\sinh kh\cosh kh-kh]$,
obtained when the extra kinematic condition $u_{z}(h)=0$, $\Phi(h)=0$,
i.e. an impermeable base, is imposed or when the $C_{1}\!-\!C_{3}$
coupling from $\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ is written as
$C_{1}\propto h\sinh kh$ rather than $h\cosh kh$.  In the thin plate
limit $\sinh kh\simeq\cosh kh\simeq1$ the two forms coincide to
$O(kh)$, which is why the long-wave $e_{s}\simeq kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$
is quoted by both camps.

I continue to regard the cosh-numerator form with free normal stress
and free vertical motion at the base as the one consistent with the
statement $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$, no $u_{z}(h)=0$.
The $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ replacement to the buoyancy contrast is the
usual isostatic normalisation; the sign is a conventional
$\sin\leftrightarrow\cos$ phase shift.  Unresolved cosmetic issue is
the overall sign convention and the exact $\rho$ vs $\Delta\rho$
labeling, but the magnitude transfer function is as above. ∎

4.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The Stokes normal mode is the persistent starting point. With
$\psi=f(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=f'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k f\cos kx$, $(D^2-k^2)^2f=0$,
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[f''+k^2f]\sin kx$, $\sigma_{zz}=\mu[k^{-1}f'''-3k f']\cos kx$.
Rigid lid $u_x(0)=0$ gives $f'(0)=0$ and in the steady state $\dot e=u_z(0)=0$
gives $f(0)=0$. Hence $f(0)=f'(0)=0$ and $f'''(0)=2k^2B$ with
$f(z)=Bz\cosh kz+(Dz-B/k)\sinh kz$.

Free surface $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ gives
$\rho g e=2\mu k B$, viscosity will cancel in the steady balance.
Free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is $f'''(h)=3k^2f'(h)$ and the prescribed basal
shear is $\mu[f''(h)+k^2f(h)]=S_0$. No $u_z(h)=0$ or $f(h)=0$ is imposed in the
statement; the base is traction free in normal stress and driven in shear.

With $f'''(h)=3k^2f'(h)$ one gets $D=B[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh]/[kh\cosh kh]$
and $f''+k^2f=2k[Bkh\cosh kh+D\cosh kh+Dkh\sinh kh]$. Elimination gives

$B=S_0h\cosh kh/\{2\mu[\cosh^2kh+k^2h^2]\}$,

$\rho g e_s=2\mu k B=S_0\,kh\cosh kh/[\cosh^2kh+k^2h^2]$,

so with the isostatic restoring stress $\Delta\rho g$

$e_s=\chi(kh)S_0/\Delta\rho g$,

$\chi(kh)=kh\cosh kh/[\cosh^2kh+k^2h^2]
      =\big[ kh/\cosh kh+\cosh kh/kh\big]^{-1}>0$.

Up to the $90^\circ$ $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ phase, $e_s\propto-\cos kx$ for
$+\sin kx$ shear; magnitude is as above. Viscosity cancels.
$ \chi\simeq kh[1+O(k^2h^2)]$ for $kh\ll1$, $e_s\simeq khS_0/\Delta\rho g$,
and $\chi\to0$ exponentially for $kh\gg1$. For $kh=1$, $\chi\approx0.46$.

Current round: Colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,2,3,4,5,8,9 reproduce the cosh-numerator
transfer function with the thin-plate limit $\chi_0\approx kh$.
Colleagues 13,14,7 persist with the sinh-numerator forms
$\chi\propto kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^2kh+k^2h^2]$ or
$\chi=kh\sinh kh/[\sinh kh\cosh kh-kh]$. Those forms are obtained only if an
additional impermeable base condition $u_z(h)=0\iff f(h)=0$ is imposed,
i.e. $\Phi(h)=0$, which is not part of the stated data
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0$. The discrepancy is therefore a
boundary-condition mismatch. With the stated free normal-stress base the
correct steady, viscosity-independent response is the cosh-numerator form
above; the $\sinh$ numerator coincides with it to $O(kh)$ for $kh\ll1$,
$\tanh kh\to1$, which is why the long-wave limit $e_s\approx khS_0/\Delta\rho g$
is universally quoted. The only remaining inessential point is the overall
sign/phase, conventionally $e_s=-\chi S_0/\Delta\rho g\cos kx$.

8.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The stream-function normal mode $\psi=f(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=f'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k f\cos kx$, $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}f=0$ is the common reduction.
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[f''+k^{2}f]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}=\mu[k^{-1}f'''-3k f']\cos kx$.
Rigid lid $u_x(0)=0\Rightarrow f'(0)=0$ and steady $u_z(0)=0\Rightarrow f(0)=0$.
With $f(0)=f'(0)=0$
$f(z)=Bz\cosh kz+[Dz-B/k]\sinh kz$,
$f'''(0)=2k^{2}B$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)=\rho g e$.
Hence $\rho g e=2\mu k B$, $B=\rho g e/2\mu k$, viscosity will cancel in steady state.

Free normal stress at the base
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$ gives
$B[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh]=khD\cosh kh$,
$D=B[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh]/[kh\cosh kh]$.

Basal shear
$\mu[f''+k^{2}f]_{h}=S_{0}$ with
$f''+k^{2}f=2k[Bkh\cosh kz+D\cosh kz+Dkh\sinh kz]$.
Eliminating $D$,
$2\mu k B\,[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]/[kh\cosh kh]=S_{0}$.

With $B=\Delta\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k$,
$\Delta\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,kh\cosh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$.
Hence in magnitude
$e_{s}= \chi(kh) S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
$\chi(kh)=kh\cosh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]
      =\big[kh/\cosh kh+\cosh kh/kh\big]^{-1}>0$.

Up to the $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase the sign is
$e_{s}\propto-\cos kx$, conventionally written $e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.
Viscosity cancels. Long wave $kh\ll1$:
$\chi=kh/[1+k^{2}h^{2}]+O(k^{4}h^{4})\simeq kh$,
$e_{s}\simeq kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
and $\chi\sim2kh e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$; e.g. $\chi(1)=\cosh1/[1+\cosh^{2}1]\approx0.46$.

Disagreement in the round: Colleagues 7,13,14 obtain $\chi_{s}=kh\sinh kh/[ \cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]$ and the related $\chi_{imp}=kh\sinh kh/[\sinh kh\cosh kh-kh]$. Those forms follow from imposing an additional kinematic impermeability $u_{z}(h)=0$, $f(h)=0$ at the base. The statement only imposes $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$; the base is free to move vertically, so $f(h)\neq0$ is allowed and the cosh-numerator transfer function above is the one consistent with the stated data. 10.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The steady normal mode can be written $\psi=f(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=f'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k f\cos kx$, $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}f=0$.
Top $z=0$ rigid lid: $u_x=0\Rightarrow f'(0)=0$ and steady $\dot e=0\Rightarrow f(0)=0$. 
$\sigma_{zz}=\mu[k^{-1}f'''-3k f']\cos kx$, $\sigma_{xz}=\mu[f''+k^{2}f]\sin kx$.
Top normal stress $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$, so with $f(0)=f'(0)=0$
$f(z)=Az\cosh kz+[-A/k+Bz]\sinh kz$, $f'''(0)=2Ak^{2}$, $\rho g e=2\mu kA$.

Base $z=h$: $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$ and prescribed shear $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$.
$f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$ gives $A[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh]=Bkh\cosh kh$.
$f''+k^{2}f=2k[Ak h\cosh kz+B\cosh kz+Bkh\sinh kz]$ so that
$\mu[f''+k^{2}f]_{h}=S_{0}$ gives
$A=\dfrac{S_{0}h\cosh kh}{2\mu[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]}$.

Hence $\rho g e_{s}=2\mu kA$,
$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}$,
with the $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase, conventionally $e_{s}\propto-\cos kx$.
With the isostatic restoring stress $\Delta\rho g$,
$e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with
$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}
       =\Big[\dfrac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1}>0$,
viscosity cancelling in the steady state. 
Long wave $kh\ll1$: $\chi\simeq kh/[1+k^{2}h^{2}]\simeq kh$, $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.
$kh\gg1$: $\chi\sim2kh e^{-kh}\to0$. For $kh=1$, $\chi\approx0.46$.

Majority of round 2, Colleagues 1,2,4,5,6,8,9,10,11,12,15, agree on this cosh-numerator transfer function, with the sign $e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ corresponding to anti-phase topography.

Competing minority forms $\chi_{\rm imp}=kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]$ or
$\chi=kh\sinh kh/[\sinh kh\cosh kh-kh]$ are obtained only if an extra kinematic impermeable base $u_{z}(h)=0\iff f(h)=0$ is imposed. The statement specifies only $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$; the base is free to move vertically, so $f(h)\neq0$ and the $\sinh$-numerator is not consistent with the stated data. The $kh\sinh kh/[\sinh kh\cosh kh-kh]\sim3/2kh$ small-$kh$ form is the impermeable-base limit.

Sign and $\rho$ vs $\Delta\rho$ are conventional: the problem writes $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ and then asks for $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$. The transfer function above is for $\rho\to\Delta\rho$; with the notation as written the magnitude is the same up to the $\rho/\Delta\rho$ factor. Transient decays on a viscous time $\mu/\Delta\rho g k$.

9.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The Stokes stream function normal mode can be taken as $\psi=f(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=f'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-kf\cos kx$, $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}f=0$.
For constant $\mu$

$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[f''+k^{2}f]\sin kx$, 
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu[k^{-1}f'''-3k f']\cos kx$.

Rigid lid $u_{x}(0)=0\Rightarrow f'(0)=0$ and steady state $\dot e=u_{z}(0)=0\Rightarrow f(0)=0$.
With $f(0)=f'(0)=0$

$f(z)=Bz\cosh kz+\big[D\,z-B/k\big]\sinh kz$, $f'''(0)=2k^{2}B$,

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)\cos kx=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,

$\Delta\rho g e=2\mu k B$, $B=\Delta\rho g e/2\mu k$.

Stress free base
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff\mu[f''+k^{2}f]_{h}=S_{0}$.

$f'''+3k^{2}f'=0$ at $h$ gives $B[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh]=khD\cosh kh$,
$D=B[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh]/kh\cosh kh$.
Then
$f''+k^{2}f=2k[\,Bkh\cosh kz+D\cosh kz+Dkh\sinh kz\,]$.

Eliminating $D$,
$2\mu kB[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]/[h\cosh kh]=S_{0}$.
With $B=\Delta\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k$,

$\Delta\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,kh\cosh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]$,

i.e. up to the $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase
$e_{s}= -\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with magnitude

$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}
       =\Big[\dfrac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1}>0$,

viscosity cancels in the steady state. Long wave $kh\ll1$:
$\chi=kh/[1+k^{2}h^{2}]+O(k^{4}h^{4})\simeq kh$,
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, $|\chi|\to2kh e^{-kh}$ for $kh\gg1$.
Numerically $\chi(1)=\cosh1/[1+\cosh^{2}1]\approx0.46$, $\chi\sim0.4\!-\!0.6$ for $kh\sim O(1)$.

This is the consensus of Colleagues 1,2,4,5,6,8,9,10,12,15 and the majority in both rounds.
The $\sinh$-numerator form
$\chi_{\rm sinh}=kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]$,
and the impermeable-base form
$\chi_{\rm imp}=kh\sinh kh/[\sinh kh\cosh kh-kh]=1/[\cosh kh/kh-\csch kh]$,
$\chi_{\rm imp}\simeq\frac32/kh^{-1}$ for $kh\ll1$, diverges as $h\to0$,
are obtained only if an extra kinematic condition $u_{z}(h)=0\iff f(h)=0$ is imposed at the base. The problem statement gives only $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$, no impermeability, so the base is free to move vertically and the cosh-numerator transfer function above is the correct stated-conditions steady, viscosity-independent response. The conventional sign is $e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, i.e. topography anti-phase with the imposed $\sin kx$ shear; the magnitude is $\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$. Replacement $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ is the usual isostatic normalisation.

5.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The normal mode is $\psi=F(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=F'\sin kx$, $u_z=-kF\cos kx$, $(D^2-k^2)^2F=0$.
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[F''+k^2F]\sin kx$, $\sigma_{zz}=\mu[k^{-1}F'''-3kF']\cos kx$ up to hydrostatic.

Top $z=0$: $u_x=0\Leftrightarrow F'(0)=0$, steady $\dot e=0\Leftrightarrow F(0)=0$, 
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx=\mu k^{-1}F'''(0)\cos kx$.
Base $z=h$: $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\Leftrightarrow F'''(h)=3k^2F'(h)$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0\sin kx\Leftrightarrow\mu[F''+k^2F]_h=S_0$.

With $F(0)=F'(0)=0$

$F(z)=C_1\sinh kz+C_3z\sinh kz-kC_1z\cosh kz$,

$F'''(0)=2k^3C_1$, $F''+k^2F=2k[C_3\cosh kz+C_3kz\sinh kz-k^2C_1z\cosh kz]$.

$F'''(h)=3k^2F'(h)$ gives

$C_1\big[hk\sinh kh-\cosh kh\big]=hC_3\cosh kh$,

i.e. $C_1=hC_3\cosh kh/[hk\sinh kh-\cosh kh]$.

Basal shear gives

$2\mu kC_3\big[-(\cosh^2kh+k^2h^2)\big]/[hk\sinh kh-\cosh kh]=S_0$,

hence

$C_3=-\dfrac{S_0\big[hk\sinh kh-\cosh kh\big]}{2\mu k\big[\cosh^2kh+k^2h^2\big]}$,

$C_1=-\dfrac{S_0h\cosh kh}{2\mu k\big[\cosh^2kh+k^2h^2\big]}$.

Then $\Delta\rho g e_s=\mu k^{-1}F'''(0)=2\mu k^2C_1$ up to the
$\sin\leftrightarrow\cos$ $90^{\circ}$ phase, i.e. in magnitude

$e_s=\dfrac{S_0}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^2kh+k^2h^2}$,

$e_s=\chi S_0/\Delta\rho g$,

$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^2kh+k^2h^2}
      =\Big[\,kh/\cosh kh+\cosh kh/kh\Big]^{-1}>0$,

viscosity cancels in the steady state.  Anti-phase $e\propto-\cos kx$
for $+\sin kx$ shear.  Long wave $kh\ll1$:
$\chi=kh/[1+k^2h^2]+O(k^4h^4)\simeq kh$, $e_s\simeq khS_0/\Delta\rho g$,
$\chi\to2kh e^{-kh}$ for $kh\gg1$.  For $kh=1$, $\chi\approx0.46$,
the familiar $0.3\!-\!0.6$ viscous dynamic topography.

The $\sinh$-numerator forms $\chi\propto kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^2kh+k^2h^2]$
or $\chi=kh\sinh kh/[\sinh kh\cosh kh-kh]$ quoted by Colleagues
7,13,14 result from the extra impermeable/no vertical flow condition
$F(h)=0$, $u_z(h)=0$, i.e. $ \Phi(h)=0$, which is not in the stated
data $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0$.  With the stated free normal
traction base the base is free to move vertically and the cosh-numerator
transfer function above is the correct viscosity-independent steady
response.  The $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ replacement is the usual isostatic
normalisation for a plate in air/water.  Sign convention is the
inessential $90^{\circ}$ phase; magnitude is as above.

6.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The steady Stokes normal mode can be written with $\psi=f(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=f'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-kf\cos kx$, $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}f=0$.  
With the rigid lid $u_{x}(0)=0$ and the steady kinematic condition $u_{z}(0)=0$

$f(0)=f'(0)=0$, so that up to the $k$–mode

$f(z)=A\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+Bz\sinh kz$,

$f'(0)=0$, $f'''(0)=2k^{2}A$,

$\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}=\mu\big[k^{-1}f'''-3k f'\big]\cos kx$.

On the free top

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)\cos kx=\rho g\,e\cos kx$,

$\rho g e=-2\mu k^{2}A$, $\;f'''(0)=2k^{3}A$.

The traction free base is 

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff\mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]_{h}=S_{0}$.

$f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$ gives the $A\!-\!B$ coupling

$A\big[kh\sinh kh-\cosh kh\big]=B\,h\cosh kh$,

$A=Bh\cosh kh/\big[kh\sinh kh-\cosh kh\big]$.

With $f''+k^{2}f=2k\big[B\cosh kz+Bkz\sinh kz-k^{2}Az\cosh kz\big]$

\[
\mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]_{h}=2\mu kB\,
\frac{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}{kh\sinh kh-\cosh kh},
\]

so that with the basal shear $S_{0}$

$B=-\displaystyle\frac{S_{0}\big[kh\sinh kh-\cosh kh\big]}
{2\mu k\big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]}$,

$A=-\displaystyle\frac{S_{0}h\cosh kh}
{2\mu k\big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]}$.

Hence

$\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}A
      =\displaystyle\frac{S_{0}\,kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}$.

With the isostatic restoring stress $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$,
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$,

$e_{s}= \chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,

\[
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}
       =\Bigg[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Bigg]^{-1}>0,
\]

up to the $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase, i.e. in the
conventional sign $e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g\;\cos kx$.  The viscosity
cancels in the steady balance.

Long wave: $\cosh kh=1+O(k^{2}h^{2})$,

$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}+O(k^{4}h^{4})\simeq kh$,

$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, $|\chi_{0}|\simeq kh$,
and $\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$.  For $kh=1$,
$\chi(1)=\cosh1/[1+\cosh^{2}1]\approx0.46$, the familiar $O(kh)$ viscous
dynamic topography.

The $kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]$ and
$kh\sinh kh/[\sinh kh\cosh kh-kh]$ forms appearing in Colleagues 7,13,14
are the impermeable–base $u_{z}(h)=0$, $f(h)=0$, i.e. $f(h)=0$ variants.
With the stated data $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ and no
imposed $u_{z}(h)=0$ the base is free to move vertically and the
$\cosh$–numerator transfer function above is the viscosity independent
steady response.  The $\sinh$ numerator is recovered only on imposing the
extra kinematic condition $f(h)=0$, which is not part of the problem
statement.  The overall sign is the usual anti-phase $e\propto-\cos kx$
to the imposed $S_{0}\sin kx$ basal shear; the magnitude is the $\chi$
above. ∎

15.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The normal mode can be taken as $\psi=f(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=f'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k f\cos kx$, $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}f=0$,
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[f''+k^{2}f]\sin kx$, $\sigma_{zz}= \mu[k^{-1}f'''-3k f']\cos kx$.
Rigid lid $u_x(0)=0\Rightarrow f'(0)=0$ and steady $u_z(0)=0\Rightarrow f(0)=0$.
Hence with $f(0)=f'(0)=0$
$f(z)=Bz\cosh kz+[Dz-B/k]\sinh kz$, $f'''(0)=2k^{2}B$,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)=\!2\mu kB=\rho g e$.
Base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$ and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$
give
$B[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh]=kh D\cosh kh$,
$2\mu k\!\left[Bkh\cosh kh+D\cosh kh+Dkh\sinh kh\right]=S_{0}$.
Eliminating $D$,
$B=S_{0}h\cosh kh/[2\mu(k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh)]$.
Hence in steady state the viscosity cancels,
$\rho g e_{s}=2\mu kB=S_{0}kh\cosh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]$,
i.e. up to the $90^{\circ}\sin\leftrightarrow\cos$ phase
$e_{s}= \chi(kh)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with the isostatic replacement
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$,

$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}
        =\Big[\dfrac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1}>0$,

$e\propto-\cos kx$ for a $+S_{0}\sin kx$ basal shear.  In magnitude
$|e_{s}|=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, $\chi\simeq kh/[1+k^{2}h^{2}]\simeq kh$
for $kh\ll1$, $\chi\sim2kh e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$, e.g. $\chi(1)\approx0.46$.
The $O(kh)$ long-wave limit $e_{s}\simeq kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ is the
familiar viscous dynamic topography and the viscosity drops out of the
steady balance.

Current round consensus: colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9,10,11,12,15 all obtain the
cosh-numerator transfer function above with the stated free-normal-stress
base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ and no imposed $u_{z}(h)=0$.
The minority statements of colleagues 7,13,14 with
$\chi\propto kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]$ or
$\chi=kh\sinh kh/[\sinh kh\cosh kh-kh]$ are obtained only if an extra
kinematic impermeable condition $u_{z}(h)=0\iff f(h)=0$ is imposed at the
base. With the data as stated the base is free to move vertically and the
free-normal-stress condition $f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$ leads to the
$C_{1}\propto h\cosh kh$ coupling, not $h\sinh kh$, giving the cosh
numerator above. The sign is the conventional anti-phase $e\propto-\cos kx$;
magnitude is quoted as $e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.
Unresolved notational point is the $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ isostatic replacement
and the inessential overall sign.

12.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The steady Stokes normal mode can be taken as $\psi(x,z)=f(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=f'\sin kx$, $u_z=-kf\cos kx$, $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}f=0$.  
With the rigid lid $u_x(0)=0$ and the steady kinematic condition $u_z(0)=0$

$f(0)=f'(0)=0$ and, up to an additive constant,

$f(z)=Az\cosh kz+\big[Bz-A/k\big]\sinh kz$

so that
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[f''+k^{2}f]\sin kx$, 
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu\big[k^{-1}f'''-3kf'\big]\cos kx$.
On the free top
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e$, 
$f'''(0)=2k^{2}A$, whence $\Delta\rho g\,e=2\mu kA$.

The traction free base is
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff \mu[f''+k^{2}f]_{h}=S_{0}$.

$f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$ gives
$A\big[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh\big]=Bkh\cosh kh$, i.e.
$B=A\big[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh\big]/kh\cosh kh$.
With
$f''+k^{2}f=2k\big[BC+kzA C+Bkz S\big]$, $C=\cosh kz$, $S=\sinh kz$,

$\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]_{h}=2A\big[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}\big]/(h\cosh kh)$.

Hence
$\mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]_{h}=S_{0}$ gives
$A=S_{0}h\cosh kh/2\mu\big[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}\big]$ and
$\Delta\rho g e_{s}=2\mu k A$
$=S_{0}\,kh\cosh kh/\big[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}\big]$.
The viscosity cancels in the steady state.  Up to the $90^{\circ}$ 
$\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase, $e\propto-\cos kx$ for a
$+S_{0}\sin kx$ shear, the magnitude can be written

$e_{s}= \chi(kh)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,

$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}
        =\Big[\,kh/\cosh kh+\cosh kh/kh\Big]^{-1}>0$,

with the usual sign convention $e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.
Long wave: $\cosh kh=1+O(k^{2}h^{2})$,
$\chi=kh/(1+k^{2}h^{2})+O(k^{4}h^{4})\simeq kh$,
so $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$, and
$\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$; e.g. $\chi(1)=\cosh1/
[1+\cosh^{2}1]\approx0.46$.

The sinh-numerator forms $ \chi\propto kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]$,
$\chi=kh\sinh kh/[\sinh kh\cosh kh-kh]$, etc., are obtained if the
additional kinematic condition $u_{z}(h)=0$, $f(h)=0$, i.e. an impermeable
base, is imposed.  With the data as stated, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ only, the base is free to move vertically and the
cosh-numerator transfer function above is the viscosity-independent
steady response.  The $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ replacement is the usual
isostatic normalisation.  The sign is the conventional anti-phase
between the imposed basal $\sin kx$ shear and the $\cos kx$ topography. ∎

11.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The steady normal mode can be written with a stream function
$\psi=f(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=f'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-kf\cos kx$, $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}f=0$.
With the rigid lid
$u_{x}(0)=0\iff f'(0)=0$ and in the steady state $u_{z}(0)=0\iff f(0)=0$.
Hence up to an additive constant

$f(z)=A\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+Bz\sinh kz$,

$f'''(0)= -2k^{3}A$, $f'(0)=0$,

$\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu\big[k^{-1}f'''-3k f'\big]\cos kx$.

Free surface
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$, i.e.

$\rho g e =-2\mu k^{2}A$,

and the traction free base
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$ gives

$A\big[kh\sinh kh-\cosh kh\big]=Bkh\cosh kh$,

so that

$f''+k^{2}f=2k\big[B\cosh kz+Bkz\sinh kz-Ak^{2}z\cosh kz\big]$.

The imposed basal shear

$\mu\big[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)\big]=S_{0}$

gives with the $f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$ relation

$-\,2\mu k B\,\dfrac{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}{kh\sinh kh-\cosh kh}=S_{0}$.

Eliminating $B$ with $A=Bkh\cosh kh/[kh\sinh kh-\cosh kh]$ and
$\rho g e=-2\mu k^{2}A$ the viscosity cancels and

$\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}\;,$

i.e. with the isostatic restoring stress $\Delta\rho g e$

$e_{s}= \chi(kh)\,\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,

$\displaystyle 
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}
       =\Bigg[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Bigg]^{-1}>0,
$

up to the $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase,
conventionally $e_{s}= -\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ so that the $\cos kx$
topography is anti–phase to the imposed $S_{0}\sin kx$ basal shear.

Viscosity cancels in the steady Stokes balance.  Long wave

$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}+O(k^{4}h^{4})\simeq kh$,

$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, and
$\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$.  For $kh=1$,
$\chi(1)=\cosh1/[1+\cosh^{2}1]\approx0.46$, the familiar $0.3\!-\!0.6\,kh$
viscous dynamic topography.

The $kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]$ and
$kh\sinh kh/[\sinh kh\cosh kh-kh]$ forms that appear in the discussion
are the impermeable–base $u_{z}(h)=0$, $f(h)=0$ limit.  With the
stated data $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ and no
$u_{z}(h)=0$ condition the base is free to move vertically and the
cosh-numerator transfer function above is the correct viscosity-
independent steady response.  The minority $\sinh$–numerator results
follow from imposing the extra kinematic condition $f(h)=0$ at the
base, which is not part of the problem statement.  The sign is the
usual anti-phase between basal shear and topography.

       =\Big[\dfrac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1}>0$,

reflection_text.2:
The steady Stokes stream-function normal mode
$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$, is the common basis. With $u_x(0)=0$ and the
steady kinematic condition $\dot e=0$ we have $\Phi'(0)=\Phi(0)=0$ on the
rigid lid.  With the free surface normal stress 
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ and 
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu[k^{-1}\Phi'''-3k\Phi']\cos kx$, 
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$, the top gives
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e$, $\Phi'''(0)=2k^{2}B$ for
$\Phi(z)=Bz\cosh kz+D z\sinh kz-(B/k)\sinh kz$, i.e. 
$\rho g e=2\mu k B$.

Base conditions are $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ and
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff\mu[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)]=S_{0}$.
$\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ gives
$B\cosh kh=kh\big(B\sinh kh+D\cosh kh\big)$, i.e.
$D=B[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh]/kh\cosh kh$.
Then 
$[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=2k\{
Bkh\cosh kh+D\cosh kh+Dkh\sinh kh\}
=2kB\,[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]/[kh\cosh kh]$,
so that
$2\mu kB\,[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]/[kh\cosh kh]=S_{0}$.

Hence
$B=S_{0}h\cosh kh/\{2\mu[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]\}$,
$\rho g e_{s}=2\mu kB=
S_{0}\,kh\cosh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$,

i.e. in the isostatic form $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$
$e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with 

$\chi(kh)=kh\cosh kh\,/\,[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]
=\big[\,kh/\cosh kh+\cosh kh/kh\,\big]^{-1}>0$,

the viscosity cancelling in the steady state.  With the usual
upward positive convention the topography is $90^{\circ}$ out of phase
with the imposed $\sin kx$ shear, $e_{s}\propto-\cos kx$, so the
signed relation is $e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$; the magnitude is
the $\chi$ above.  Long wave
$\chi=kh/[1+k^{2}h^{2}]+O(k^{4}h^{4})\simeq kh$,
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, and $\chi\sim2kh e^{-kh}\to0$
for $kh\gg1$.  For $kh=1$, $\chi\approx0.46$, the familiar
$O(kh)$ viscous dynamic topography.

The majority in rounds 0,1,2 – Colleagues 1,2,4,5,8,10,12,15 and
the present Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9,10,11,12,15 – obtain this
cosh-numerator transfer function with a free vertical motion at the
base, i.e. with the stated conditions $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ and no imposed $u_{z}(h)=0$, $\Phi(h)=0$.

13,14,7 in round 2, reports
$\chi_{\rm s}=kh\sinh kh/[ \cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]$,
or equivalently

obtained when the extra kinematic condition $u_{z}(h)=0$, $\Phi(h)=0$,

coupling from $\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ is written as

reflection_text.4:

$\psi=f(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=f'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k f\cos kx$, $(D^2-k^2)^2f=0$,
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[f''+k^2f]\sin kx$, $\sigma_{zz}=\mu[k^{-1}f'''-3k f']\cos kx$.

gives $f(0)=0$. Hence $f(0)=f'(0)=0$ and $f'''(0)=2k^2B$ with

$B=S_0h\cosh kh/\{2\mu[\cosh^2kh+k^2h^2]\}$,

$\rho g e_s=2\mu k B=S_0\,kh\cosh kh/[\cosh^2kh+k^2h^2]$,

so with the isostatic restoring stress $\Delta\rho g$

reflection_text.6:
The steady Stokes normal mode can be written with $\psi=f(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=f'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-kf\cos kx$, $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}f=0$.  
With the rigid lid $u_{x}(0)=0$ and the steady kinematic condition $u_{z}(0)=0$

$f(0)=f'(0)=0$, so that up to the $k$–mode

$f(z)=A\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+Bz\sinh kz$,

$f'(0)=0$, $f'''(0)=2k^{2}A$,

$\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}=\mu\big[k^{-1}f'''-3k f'\big]\cos kx$.

On the free top

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)\cos kx=\rho g\,e\cos kx$,

$\rho g e=-2\mu k^{2}A$, $\;f'''(0)=2k^{3}A$.

The traction free base is 

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff\mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]_{h}=S_{0}$.

$f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$ gives the $A\!-\!B$ coupling

$A\big[kh\sinh kh-\cosh kh\big]=B\,h\cosh kh$,

$A=Bh\cosh kh/\big[kh\sinh kh-\cosh kh\big]$.

With $f''+k^{2}f=2k\big[B\cosh kz+Bkz\sinh kz-k^{2}Az\cosh kz\big]$

\[
\mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]_{h}=2\mu kB\,
\frac{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}{kh\sinh kh-\cosh kh},
\]

so that with the basal shear $S_{0}$

$B=-\displaystyle\frac{S_{0}\big[kh\sinh kh-\cosh kh\big]}
{2\mu k\big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]}$,

$A=-\displaystyle\frac{S_{0}h\cosh kh}
{2\mu k\big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]}$.

Hence

$\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}A
      =\displaystyle\frac{S_{0}\,kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}$.

With the isostatic restoring stress $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$,
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$,

$e_{s}= \chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,

\[
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}
       =\Bigg[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Bigg]^{-1}>0,
\]

up to the $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase, i.e. in the
conventional sign $e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g\;\cos kx$.  The viscosity
cancels in the steady balance.

Long wave: $\cosh kh=1+O(k^{2}h^{2})$,

$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}+O(k^{4}h^{4})\simeq kh$,

$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, $|\chi_{0}|\simeq kh$,
and $\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$.  For $kh=1$,
$\chi(1)=\cosh1/[1+\cosh^{2}1]\approx0.46$, the familiar $O(kh)$ viscous
dynamic topography.

The $kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]$ and
$kh\sinh kh/[\sinh kh\cosh kh-kh]$ forms appearing in Colleagues 7,13,14
are the impermeable–base $u_{z}(h)=0$, $f(h)=0$, i.e. $f(h)=0$ variants.
With the stated data $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ and no
imposed $u_{z}(h)=0$ the base is free to move vertically and the
$\cosh$–numerator transfer function above is the viscosity independent
steady response.  The $\sinh$ numerator is recovered only on imposing the
extra kinematic condition $f(h)=0$, which is not part of the problem
statement.  The overall sign is the usual anti-phase $e\propto-\cos kx$
to the imposed $S_{0}\sin kx$ basal shear; the magnitude is the $\chi$
above. ∎

reflection_text.15:
The normal mode can be taken as $\psi=f(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=f'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k f\cos kx$, $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}f=0$,
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[f''+k^{2}f]\sin kx$, $\sigma_{zz}= \mu[k^{-1}f'''-3k f']\cos kx$.
Rigid lid $u_x(0)=0\Rightarrow f'(0)=0$ and steady $u_z(0)=0\Rightarrow f(0)=0$.
Hence with $f(0)=f'(0)=0$
$f(z)=Bz\cosh kz+[Dz-B/k]\sinh kz$, $f'''(0)=2k^{2}B$,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)=\!2\mu kB=\rho g e$.
Base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$ and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$
give
$B[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh]=kh D\cosh kh$,
$2\mu k\!\left[Bkh\cosh kh+D\cosh kh+Dkh\sinh kh\right]=S_{0}$.
Eliminating $D$,
$B=S_{0}h\cosh kh/[2\mu(k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh)]$.
Hence in steady state the viscosity cancels,
$\rho g e_{s}=2\mu kB=S_{0}kh\cosh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]$,
i.e. up to the $90^{\circ}\sin\leftrightarrow\cos$ phase
$e_{s}= \chi(kh)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with the isostatic replacement
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$,

$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}
        =\Big[\dfrac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1}>0$,

$e\propto-\cos kx$ for a $+S_{0}\sin kx$ basal shear.  In magnitude
$|e_{s}|=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, $\chi\simeq kh/[1+k^{2}h^{2}]\simeq kh$
for $kh\ll1$, $\chi\sim2kh e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$, e.g. $\chi(1)\approx0.46$.
The $O(kh)$ long-wave limit $e_{s}\simeq kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ is the
familiar viscous dynamic topography and the viscosity drops out of the
steady balance.

Current round consensus: colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9,10,11,12,15 all obtain the
cosh-numerator transfer function above with the stated free-normal-stress
base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ and no imposed $u_{z}(h)=0$.
The minority statements of colleagues 7,13,14 with
$\chi\propto kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]$ or
$\chi=kh\sinh kh/[\sinh kh\cosh kh-kh]$ are obtained only if an extra
kinematic impermeable condition $u_{z}(h)=0\iff f(h)=0$ is imposed at the
base. With the data as stated the base is free to move vertically and the
free-normal-stress condition $f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$ leads to the
$C_{1}\propto h\cosh kh$ coupling, not $h\sinh kh$, giving the cosh
numerator above. The sign is the conventional anti-phase $e\propto-\cos kx$;
magnitude is quoted as $e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.
Unresolved notational point is the $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ isostatic replacement
and the inessential overall sign.
reflection_text.12:
The steady Stokes normal mode can be taken as $\psi(x,z)=f(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=f'\sin kx$, $u_z=-kf\cos kx$, $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}f=0$.  
With the rigid lid $u_x(0)=0$ and the steady kinematic condition $u_z(0)=0$

$f(0)=f'(0)=0$ and, up to an additive constant,

$f(z)=Az\cosh kz+\big[Bz-A/k\big]\sinh kz$

so that
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[f''+k^{2}f]\sin kx$, 
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu\big[k^{-1}f'''-3kf'\big]\cos kx$.
On the free top
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e$, 
$f'''(0)=2k^{2}A$, whence $\Delta\rho g\,e=2\mu kA$.

The traction free base is
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff \mu[f''+k^{2}f]_{h}=S_{0}$.

$f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$ gives
$A\big[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh\big]=Bkh\cosh kh$, i.e.
$B=A\big[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh\big]/kh\cosh kh$.
With
$f''+k^{2}f=2k\big[BC+kzA C+Bkz S\big]$, $C=\cosh kz$, $S=\sinh kz$,

$\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]_{h}=2A\big[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}\big]/(h\cosh kh)$.

Hence
$\mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]_{h}=S_{0}$ gives
$A=S_{0}h\cosh kh/2\mu\big[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}\big]$ and
$\Delta\rho g e_{s}=2\mu k A$
$=S_{0}\,kh\cosh kh/\big[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}\big]$.
The viscosity cancels in the steady state.  Up to the $90^{\circ}$ 
$\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase, $e\propto-\cos kx$ for a
$+S_{0}\sin kx$ shear, the magnitude can be written

$e_{s}= \chi(kh)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,

$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}
        =\Big[\,kh/\cosh kh+\cosh kh/kh\Big]^{-1}>0$,

with the usual sign convention $e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.
Long wave: $\cosh kh=1+O(k^{2}h^{2})$,
$\chi=kh/(1+k^{2}h^{2})+O(k^{4}h^{4})\simeq kh$,
so $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$, and
$\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$; e.g. $\chi(1)=\cosh1/
[1+\cosh^{2}1]\approx0.46$.

The sinh-numerator forms $ \chi\propto kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]$,
$\chi=kh\sinh kh/[\sinh kh\cosh kh-kh]$, etc., are obtained if the
additional kinematic condition $u_{z}(h)=0$, $f(h)=0$, i.e. an impermeable
base, is imposed.  With the data as stated, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ only, the base is free to move vertically and the
cosh-numerator transfer function above is the viscosity-independent
steady response.  The $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ replacement is the usual
isostatic normalisation.  The sign is the conventional anti-phase
between the imposed basal $\sin kx$ shear and the $\cos kx$ topography. ∎
reflection_text.11:
The steady normal mode can be written with a stream function
$\psi=f(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=f'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-kf\cos kx$, $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}f=0$.
With the rigid lid
$u_{x}(0)=0\iff f'(0)=0$ and in the steady state $u_{z}(0)=0\iff f(0)=0$.
Hence up to an additive constant

$f(z)=A\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+Bz\sinh kz$,

$f'''(0)= -2k^{3}A$, $f'(0)=0$,

$\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu\big[k^{-1}f'''-3k f'\big]\cos kx$.

Free surface
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$, i.e.

$\rho g e =-2\mu k^{2}A$,

and the traction free base
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$ gives

$A\big[kh\sinh kh-\cosh kh\big]=Bkh\cosh kh$,

so that

$f''+k^{2}f=2k\big[B\cosh kz+Bkz\sinh kz-Ak^{2}z\cosh kz\big]$.

The imposed basal shear

$\mu\big[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)\big]=S_{0}$

gives with the $f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$ relation

$-\,2\mu k B\,\dfrac{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}{kh\sinh kh-\cosh kh}=S_{0}$.

Eliminating $B$ with $A=Bkh\cosh kh/[kh\sinh kh-\cosh kh]$ and
$\rho g e=-2\mu k^{2}A$ the viscosity cancels and

$\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}\;,$

i.e. with the isostatic restoring stress $\Delta\rho g e$

$e_{s}= \chi(kh)\,\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,

$\displaystyle 
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}
       =\Bigg[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Bigg]^{-1}>0,
$

up to the $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase,
conventionally $e_{s}= -\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ so that the $\cos kx$
topography is anti–phase to the imposed $S_{0}\sin kx$ basal shear.

Viscosity cancels in the steady Stokes balance.  Long wave

$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}+O(k^{4}h^{4})\simeq kh$,

$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, and
$\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$.  For $kh=1$,
$\chi(1)=\cosh1/[1+\cosh^{2}1]\approx0.46$, the familiar $0.3\!-\!0.6\,kh$
viscous dynamic topography.

The $kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]$ and
$kh\sinh kh/[\sinh kh\cosh kh-kh]$ forms that appear in the discussion
are the impermeable–base $u_{z}(h)=0$, $f(h)=0$ limit.  With the
stated data $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ and no
$u_{z}(h)=0$ condition the base is free to move vertically and the
cosh-numerator transfer function above is the correct viscosity-
independent steady response.  The minority $\sinh$–numerator results
follow from imposing the extra kinematic condition $f(h)=0$ at the
base, which is not part of the problem statement.  The sign is the
usual anti-phase between basal shear and topography.

1.text:
With the normal mode

$\psi(x,z)=f(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=f'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k f\cos kx$,
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}f=0$,

$$
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\bigl[f''+k^{2}f\bigr]\sin kx ,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= \mu\Big[\,k^{-1}f'''-3k f'\Big]\cos kx ,
$$

on the rigid lid

$$
u_{x}(0)=0\iff f'(0)=0 ,\qquad  \dot e=u_{z}(0)=-k f(0)\cos kx ,
$$

so that in the steady state $f(0)=f'(0)=0$.  With $f(0)=f'(0)=0$

$$
f(z)=Bz\cosh kz+Dz\sinh kz-\frac{B}{k}\sinh kz,
\qquad f'''(0)=2k^{2}B ,
$$

and

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}f'''(0)\cos kx=2\mu kB\cos kx
      =\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx ,
$$

i.e. up to the $\sin\leftrightarrow\cos$ phase

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e=2\mu kB,\qquad B=\frac{\Delta\rho g\,e}{2\mu k}. \tag{1}
$$

The free normal traction at the base is

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)
\Longleftrightarrow 
B\bigl[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh\bigr]=khD\cosh kh , \tag{2}
$$

and the imposed basal shear

$$
\mu\bigl[f''+k^{2}f\bigr]_{h}=S_{0},\qquad 
f''+k^{2}f=2k\Big[Bkh\cosh kz+D\cosh kz+Dkh\sinh kz\Big].
$$

Eliminating $D$ with (2),

$$
\mu\bigl[f''+k^{2}f\bigr]_{h}
=2\mu kB\,\frac{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}{h\cosh kh}=S_{0},
$$

so that with (1)

$$
B=\frac{S_{0}h\cosh kh}
        {2\mu\bigl[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\bigr]},\qquad
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=2\mu kB
      =S_{0}\,\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh} .
$$

Hence in magnitude

$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}
       =\Bigg[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Bigg]^{-1}>0,
$$

the viscosity cancelling in the steady Stokes balance.  With the
conventional upward positive sign the $\sin kx$ basal shear produces a
$\cos kx$ topography in anti-phase,

$$
e(x)=-\,\chi(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\cos kx ,
$$

i.e. $e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ in the usual sign convention.
In particular

$$
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}+O(k^{4}h^{4}),\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

so that in the long wave lubrication limit

$$
|e_{s}|\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
|\chi_{0}|\simeq kh,
$$

and $\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$.  For $kh=1$,
$\chi(1)=\cosh1/[1+\cosh^{2}1]\approx0.46$.  This is the viscosity
independent steady viscous dynamic topography with the stated
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$ stress free base, the
base being free to move vertically, $u_{z}(h)\neq0$.  The $kh\sinh
kh/\!\left[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}\right]$ forms are the impermeable
base $f(h)=0$, $u_{z}(h)=0$ limit. ∎

4.text:
The $k$ mode can be written in the stream function form

$$
\psi(x,z)=f(z)\sin kx ,\qquad 
u_{x}=f'\sin kx ,\qquad u_{z}=-k f\cos kx ,
$$

$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}f=0$ and for constant $\mu$

$$
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]\sin kx ,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= \mu\Big[k^{-1}f'''-3k f'\Big]\cos kx .
$$

On the rigid lid $u_{x}(0)=0$ gives $f'(0)=0$ and in the steady state
$\dot e=u_{z}(0)=-k f(0) =0$ gives $f(0)=0$.  With $f(0)=f'(0)=0$

$$
f(z)=Bz\cosh kz+\Big[D\,z-\frac{B}{k}\Big]\sinh kz,
\qquad f'''(0)=2k^{2}B ,
$$

so that on the free surface

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}f'''(0)\cos kx
            =2\mu kB\cos kx=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx ,
\tag{1}
$$

i.e. $\Delta\rho g\,e=2\mu kB$.

The traction free base is

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h),\qquad
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff \mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]_{h}=S_{0}.
\tag{2}
$$

Now $f''+k^{2}f=2k\big[Bkh\cosh kz+D\cosh kz+Dkh\sinh kz\big]$ and
$f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$ gives

$$
B\big[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh\big]=kh\,D\cosh kh ,
\qquad 
D=B\,\frac{\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh}{kh\cosh kh}\; .
$$

Hence

$$
\mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]_{h}
 =2\mu k\Big[Bkh\cosh kh+D\cosh kh+Dkh\sinh kh\Big]=S_{0},
$$

and on elimination of $D$

$$
2\mu k B\,
\frac{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}{h\cosh kh}=S_{0}.
$$

With (1) $B=\Delta\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k$ this is viscosity independent,

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}},
$$

i.e. up to the $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase

$$
e(x)=-\,\chi(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\cos kx ,
\qquad 
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}
       =\Bigg[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Bigg]^{-1}>0,
$$

so that in magnitude

$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}\; .
$$

The viscosity cancels in the steady Stokes balance.  In particular

$$
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}+O(k^{4}h^{4}),\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

and

$$
\chi(kh)\xrightarrow[kh\ll1]{}kh,\qquad 
\chi(kh)\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}\to0,\;kh\gg1,
$$

so that in the long wave lubrication, thin-plate limit

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
|\chi_{0}|\simeq kh ,
$$

the familiar $O(kh)$ viscous dynamic topography, $e\propto-\cos kx$
for a $+\sin kx$ basal shear.  For $kh=1$, $\chi(1)=\cosh1/[1+\cosh^{2}1]
\approx0.46$.  This is the steady, viscosity independent response with
the stated $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ stress free base,
the base being free to move vertically.  The $\,kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh
+k^{2}h^{2}]$ forms are obtained only on imposing the extra kinematic
impermeable condition $u_{z}(h)=0\iff f(h)=0$ at the base.  With the
conventional upward positive sign $e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$; the
magnitude quoted above is the usual $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$
result. ∎

6.text:
With the normal mode

$\psi(x,z)=f(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=f'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-kf\cos kx$, 
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}f=0$,

$\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]\sin kx$ , 
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu\big[k^{-1}f'''-3k f'\big]\cos kx $,

and on the rigid lid

$u_{x}(0)=0\iff f'(0)=0$,  $\dot e=u_{z}(0)=-kf(0)\cos kx$.
In the steady state $\dot e=0$,

$f(0)=f'(0)=0$,
$f(z)=A\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+Bz\sinh kz$,
$f'''(0)=2k^{2}A$,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)\cos kx$.

On the free surface with the isostatic normal stress

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$,

$\Delta\rho g e=2\mu k A$, $f'''(0)=2k^{3}A$,

i.e. up to the $\sin\leftrightarrow\cos$ phase

$\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=2\mu k A$.

The free base is

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff \mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]_{h}=S_{0}$.

With $f(0)=f'(0)=0$

$f''+k^{2}f=2k\Big[Akh\cosh kz+B\cosh kz+Bkh\sinh kz\Big]$,
$f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$ gives

$A\big[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh\big]=Bkh\cosh kh$ .

Hence

$\mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]_{h}
 =2\mu kB\,\frac{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}{h\cosh kh}=S_{0}$,

and with $\Delta\rho g e_{s}=2\mu kA$ and the $A\!-\!B$ relation

$A=-\,\dfrac{S_{0}h\cosh kh}
           {2\mu k\big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]}$,

$B=\dfrac{\Delta\rho g e_{s}}{2\mu k}$,

so that the viscosity cancels in the steady balance,

$\Delta\rho g e_{s}
   =S_{0}\,\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}$ .

In magnitude

$e_{s}= \chi(kh)\,\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,

$\displaystyle 
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}
       =\Bigg[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Bigg]^{-1}>0$ ,

and with the usual upward positive convention

$e_{s}(x)=-\chi(kh)\,\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\cos kx$,

i.e. the $\sin kx$ basal shear is $90^{\circ}$ out of phase with the
$\cos kx$ topography, the sign being the conventional anti-phase.
In particular

$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}+O(k^{4}h^{4})\simeq kh$, $kh\ll1$,

so that in the long wave lubrication limit

$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, $|\chi_{0}|\simeq kh$,

and $\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$, e.g.
$\chi(1)=\cosh1/[1+\cosh^{2}1]\approx0.46$.
The $kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]$ forms are obtained only on
imposing the extra kinematic condition $u_{z}(h)=0$, $f(h)=0$.  With the
stated free normal stress $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ the
base is free to move vertically and the viscosity independent
$\cosh$–numerator transfer function above is the steady Stokes
response, normally quoted in the thin-plate limit as
$e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.  With the $\rho$ notation of the
statement this is $e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\rho g$ up to the inessential
$-\,$ sign. ∎

9.text:
With the normal mode

$$
\psi(x,z)=f(z)\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{x}=f'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-k f\cos kx ,
$$

$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}f=0$,

$$
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]\sin kx,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= \mu\Big[k^{-1}f'''-3k f'\Big]\cos kx .
$$

On the rigid lid
$u_{x}(0)=0\iff f'(0)=0$ and in the steady state $u_{z}(0)=0\iff f(0)=0$.
With $f(0)=f'(0)=0$

$$
f(z)=Bz\cosh kz+\Big[D\,z-\frac{B}{k}\Big]\sinh kz,\qquad 
f'''(0)=2k^{2}B,
$$

so that

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}f'''(0)\cos kx
            =2\mu kB\cos kx
            =\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx ,
$$

i.e. up to the $\sin\leftrightarrow\cos$ phase

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e=2\mu kB,\qquad 
B=\frac{\Delta\rho g\,e}{2\mu k}. \tag{1}
$$

On the base

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h),\qquad
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff 
\mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]_{h}=S_{0}. \tag{2}
$$

Now
$$
f''+k^{2}f=2k\Big[Bkh\cosh kz+D\cosh kz+Dkh\sinh kz\Big]
$$
and $f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$ is

$$
B\big[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh\big]=khD\cosh kh,
\qquad 
D=B\frac{\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh}{kh\cosh kh}.
$$

Hence

$$
\mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]_{h}
 =2\mu kB\frac{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}{h\cosh kh}=S_{0}.
$$

With (1)

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=2\mu kB
   =S_{0}\,\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh},
$$

the viscosity cancelling in the steady Stokes balance.  In
magnitude

$$
|e_{s}|=\chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}
       =\Bigg[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Bigg]^{-1}>0,
$$

and with the conventional upward positive sign the topography is
$90^{\circ}$ out of phase with the imposed shear,
$e_{s}(x)=-\chi(kh)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g\,\cos kx$, i.e. 
$e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for the $\sin kx$ basal traction.
In particular

$$
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}+O(k^{4}h^{4})\simeq kh,\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

so that in the long wave lubrication limit

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad |\chi_{0}|\simeq kh,
$$

and $|\chi|\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$.  For $kh=1$, 
$\chi(1)=\cosh1/[1+\cosh^{2}1]\approx0.46$, the familiar
$0.3\!-\!0.6\,kh$ viscous dynamic topography.  The $\,kh\sinh kh/
[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]$ and $kh\sinh kh/[\sinh kh\cosh kh-kh]$ forms are
obtained only on the additional impermeable condition $u_{z}(h)=0\iff
f(h)=0$.  With the stated data $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$
the base is free to move vertically and the cosh-numerator transfer
function above is the viscosity independent steady response, usually
quoted in the thin plate limit as $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
the sign being the usual anti-phase $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$.
With the $\rho$ notation of the statement $\Delta\rho\to\rho$ this is
$e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\rho g$ up to the conventional $-$ sign. ∎

3.text:
With the normal mode

$$
\psi(x,z)=f(z)\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{x}=f'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-k f\cos kx,
\qquad (D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}f=0 ,
$$

\begin{equation*}
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\!\left[f''+k^{2}f\right]\sin kx ,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}= \mu\!\left[k^{-1}f'''-3k f'\right]\cos kx ,
\end{equation*}
the rigid lid is $u_{x}(0)=0$, i.e. $f'(0)=0$, and in the steady state
$\dot e=u_{z}(0)=0$, i.e. $f(0)=0$.  Put $f(0)=f'(0)=0$,

$$
f(z)=Bz\cosh kz+\Big[D\,z-\frac{B}{k}\Big]\sinh kz ,
$$

$$
f'''(0)=2k^{2}B ,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}f'''(0)\cos kx .
$$

On the free surface

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx ,
$$

hence

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e=2\mu kB ,\qquad 
B=\frac{\Delta\rho g\,e}{2\mu k},                               \tag{1}
$$

the $\rho$ of the statement being $\Delta\rho$ in the isostatic
balance.  On the base

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h),\qquad
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff
\mu\!\left[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)\right]=S_{0}.                     \tag{2}
$$

Now

$$
f''+k^{2}f=2k\Big[Bkh\cosh kz+D\cosh kz+Dkh\sinh kz\Big],
$$

and $f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$ gives

$$
B\big[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh\big]=kh\,D\cosh kh ,
\qquad 
D=B\,\frac{\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh}{kh\cosh kh}.                  \tag{3}
$$

Hence

$$
\mu\!\left[f''+k^{2}f\right]_{h}
 =2\mu k\Big[Bkh\cosh kh+D\cosh kh+Dkh\sinh kh\Big]=S_{0},
$$

and with (3)

$$
2\mu kB\,\frac{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}{h\cosh kh}=S_{0}.       \tag{4}
$$

Eliminating $B$ between (1) and (4),

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh},
$$

i.e. up to the inessential $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$
phase

$$
e(x)=-\chi(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\cos kx ,
$$

with the magnitude transfer function

\[
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Bigg[\,\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Bigg]^{-1}>0,
\]

and the viscosity cancels in the steady Stokes balance.  In
magnitude

$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}},
$$

the conventional sign being $e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, i.e. the
topography is anti-phase, $e\propto -\cos kx$, to the imposed
$\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$.

In particular

$$
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}+O(k^{4}h^{4})\simeq kh,
\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

so that in the lubrication long-wave limit

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
|\chi_{0}|\simeq kh,
$$

and $\chi\sim 2kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$.  E.g. 
$\chi(1)=\cosh1/[1+\cosh^{2}1]\approx0.46$, the familiar
$O(kh)$ viscous dynamic topography.  With the notation of the
statement $\Delta\rho\to\rho$, $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\rho g$ with the same
$\chi$.  The $kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]$ forms are obtained
only on the additional kinematic condition $u_{z}(h)=0$, $f(h)=0$,
i.e. an impermeable base.  With the stated data
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ the base is free to move
vertically and the cosh-numerator transfer function above is the
viscosity independent steady response, often quoted in the thin plate
limit as $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$. ∎

2.text:
With the normal mode

$$
\psi(x,z)=f(z)\sin kx,\qquad u_{x}=f'\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{z}=-k f\cos kx ,
$$

$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}f=0$ and for constant $\mu$

$$
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]\sin kx ,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= \mu\Big[k^{-1}f'''-3k f'\Big]\cos kx  .
$$

On the rigid lid $u_{x}(0)=0$ gives $f'(0)=0$ and in the steady state
$\dot e=u_{z}(0)=0$ gives $f(0)=0$, so that with $f(0)=f'(0)=0$

$$
f(z)=Bz\cosh kz+\Big[D\,z-\frac{B}{k}\Big]\sinh kz ,
\qquad f'''(0)=2k^{2}B,
$$

and

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}f'''(0)\cos kx
      =2\mu k B\cos kx .
$$

Hence on the free surface with the buoyancy restoring stress
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$

\begin{equation*}
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=2\mu kB ,\qquad 
B=\frac{\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}}{2\mu k} ,
\tag{1}
\end{equation*}
the $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase being the usual
anti-phase between the imposed basal shear and the topography.

On the base

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h),\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff\mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]_{h}=S_{0} ,
$$

i.e.

$$
B\big[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh\big]=khD\cosh kh ,
\qquad 
D=B\,\frac{\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh}{kh\cosh kh} .
$$

Now

$$
f''+k^{2}f=2k\Big[Bkh\cosh kz+D\cosh kz+Dkh\sinh kz\Big],
$$

so that

$$
\mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]_{h}
 =2\mu k\Big[Bkh\cosh kh+D\cosh kh+Dkh\sinh kh\Big]=S_{0}.
$$

Eliminating $D$,

$$
2\mu kB\,\frac{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}{h\cosh kh}=S_{0},
$$

and with (1)

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}
   =S_{0}\,\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}\; .
$$

In magnitude

$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Bigg[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Bigg]^{-1}>0 ,
$$

the viscosity cancelling in the steady Stokes balance.  With the
conventional upward positive sign the topography is in quadrature and
anti-phase with the imposed $\sin kx$ shear,

$$
e(x)=-\,\chi(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\cos kx\,,
\qquad e_{s}= -\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g ,
$$

so that $|e_{s}|=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.

In particular

$$
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}+O(k^{4}h^{4}),\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

so that in the long wave lubrication limit

$$
|e_{s}|\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad |\chi_{0}|\simeq kh,
$$

and $\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$.  For $kh=1$,
$\chi(1)=\cosh1/[1+\cosh^{2}1]\approx0.46$, the familiar $O(kh)$
viscous dynamic topography.  With $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ this is the
usual $e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\rho g$ form.  The $kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+
k^{2}h^{2}]$ transfer function is obtained only on the additional
kinematic imposition $u_{z}(h)=0$, $f(h)=0$, i.e. an impermeable base;
with the stated free normal traction $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ the base is
free to move vertically and the cosh-numerator expression above is the
steady, viscosity independent response, usually quoted in the thin
plate limit as $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$. ∎

10.text:
With the normal mode
$\psi(x,z)=f(z)\sin kx$ 
$$
u_{x}=f'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-kf\cos kx ,\qquad (D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}f=0
$$
$$
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\bigl[f''+k^{2}f\bigr]\sin kx ,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}=\mu\Bigl[k^{-1}f'''-3kf'\Bigr]\cos kx ,
$$
the rigid lid is
$$
u_{x}(0)=0\iff f'(0)=0 ,\qquad \dot e=u_{z}(0)=-kf(0)\cos kx .
$$
In the steady state $\dot e=0$ hence with $f(0)=f'(0)=0$
$$
f(z)=Az\cosh kz+\Big[-\frac{A}{k}+Bz\Big]\sinh kz ,
\qquad f'''(0)=2Ak^{2},
$$
and
$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}f'''(0)\cos kx
               =2\mu kA\cos kx .
$$
With the isostatic normal stress $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$
$$
\Delta\rho g\,e=2\mu kA,\qquad A=\frac{\Delta\rho g\,e}{2\mu k}\tag{1}
$$
up to the $ \sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ quadrature.

The free base is 
$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h),\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff\mu\bigl[f''+k^{2}f\bigr]_{h}=S_{0}.
$$
With $f(0)=f'(0)=0$
$$
f'''+3k^{2}f'=0\ {\rm at}\ h\Longleftrightarrow 
A\bigl[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh\bigr]=Bkh\cosh kh,
$$
and
$$
f''+k^{2}f=2k\Big[Ak h\cosh kz+B\cosh kz+Bkh\sinh kz\Big].
$$
Hence
$$
\mu\bigl[f''+k^{2}f\bigr]_{h}
=2\mu kA\frac{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}{h\cosh kh}=S_{0}. \tag{2}
$$
Eliminating $A$ between (1) and (2) the viscosity cancels in the
steady Stokes balance and
$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}\;,
$$
i.e. in magnitude with the conventional $90^{\circ}$ phase
$e(x)\propto\cos kx$ to the imposed $\sin kx$ shear,
$$
e_{s}(x)=-\,\chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\cos kx,
$$
$$
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}
       =\Bigg[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Bigg]^{-1}>0,
$$
so that with the magnitude convention
$$
|e_{s}|=\chi(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
e_{s}= \chi\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\ {\rm up\ to\ sign}.
$$
The response is viscosity independent in the steady state.  In
particular
$$
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}+O(k^{4}h^{4})\simeq kh,\qquad kh\ll1,
$$
so that in the long wave lubrication limit
$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad |\chi_{0}|\simeq kh,
$$
and $\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$.  For $kh=1$
$\chi(1)=\cosh1/[1+\cosh^{2}1]\approx0.46$, the familiar $O(kh)$
viscous dynamic topography.  With the notation of the statement
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$ the same transfer function is $e_{s}= \chi
S_{0}/\rho g$ up to the conventional anti-phase sign
$e_{s}\propto-\cos kx$.  The $kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]$ forms
are the $u_{z}(h)=0$, $f(h)=0$ impermeable base limit and are not
required by $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0,\;\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ alone; the base
is free to move vertically here. ∎

8.text:
With the normal mode
$\psi(x,z)=f(z)\sin kx$,
$u_{x}=f'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k f\cos kx$,
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}f=0$,

$$
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]\sin kx,
\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}= \mu\Big[k^{-1}f'''-3k f'\Big]\cos kx ,
$$
up to the hydrostatic part.  On the rigid lid

$$
u_{x}(0)=0\iff f'(0)=0,
\qquad \dot e=u_{z}(0)=-k f(0)\cos kx,
$$

so that in the steady state $f(0)=f'(0)=0$.  With $f(0)=f'(0)=0$

$$
f(z)=Bz\cosh kz+\Big[D z-\frac{B}{k}\Big]\sinh kz,
\qquad f'''(0)=2k^{2}B,
$$

and

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}f'''(0)\cos kx
     =2\mu kB\cos kx .
$$

Putting the buoyancy restoring stress on the free surface
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$,

\begin{equation*}
\Delta\rho g\,e=2\mu kB,\qquad
B=\frac{\Delta\rho g\,e}{2\mu k} ,
\tag{1}
\end{equation*}
the $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase being the usual
anti-phase of the topography with the imposed shear.

The traction free base is

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h),\qquad
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff 
\mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]_{h}=S_{0}.
$$

Now

$$
f''+k^{2}f=2k\Big[Bkh\cosh kz+D\cosh kz+Dkh\sinh kz\Big],
$$

and $f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$ gives

$$
B\big[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh\big]=khD\cosh kh,
\qquad
D=B\frac{\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh}{kh\cosh kh}.
$$

Hence

$$
\mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]_{h}
 =2\mu k B\frac{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}{h\cosh kh}=S_{0},
$$

i.e. with (1)

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}\;,
$$

the viscosity cancelling in the steady Stokes balance.  In magnitude

$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}
       =\Bigg[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Bigg]^{-1}>0,
$$

with the conventional upward positive sign $e_{s}\propto-\cos kx$, i.e.
$e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}\Delta\rho g^{-1}\cos kx$ for the imposed
$\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$.  In the long wave lubrication limit

$$
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}+O(k^{4}h^{4})\simeq kh,\qquad
kh\ll1,
$$

so that

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad |\chi_{0}|\simeq kh,
$$

and $\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$, e.g.
$\chi(1)=\cosh1/[1+\cosh^{2}1]\approx0.46$.  With the $\rho$ notation of
the statement $\Delta\rho\to\rho$ this is the usual
$e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\rho g$ steady dynamic topography.

The $kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]$ and
$kh\sinh kh/[\sinh kh\cosh kh-kh]$ forms quoted by Colleagues 7,13,14
are obtained on imposing the additional kinematic condition
$u_{z}(h)=0$, $f(h)=0$, i.e. an impermeable base.  With the stated data
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ the base is free to move
vertically, $f(h)\neq0$, and the cosh-numerator transfer function above
is the viscosity independent steady response with the stated free
normal traction base.  Up to the inessential $\sin\leftrightarrow\cos$
sign this is the $O(kh)$ viscous plate response normally quoted as
$e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.

5.text:
With the $k$ mode $\psi(x,z)=f(z)\sin kx$

$$
u_{x}=f^{\prime}\sin kx ,\qquad u_{z}=-k f\cos kx ,\qquad 
(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}f=0 ,
$$

$$
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[f^{\prime\prime}+k^{2}f\big]\sin kx ,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= \mu\Big[k^{-1}f^{\prime\prime\prime}-3k f^{\prime}\Big]\cos kx ,
$$

the hydrostatic part being removed.  On the rigid lid

$$
u_{x}(0)=0\iff f^{\prime}(0)=0 ,\qquad 
\dot e=u_{z}(0)=-k f(0)\cos kx ,
$$

so that in the steady state $\dot e=0$,

$$
f(0)=f^{\prime}(0)=0 .
$$

Put $f(0)=f^{\prime}(0)=0$

$$
f(z)=Bz\cosh kz+\Big[D\,z-\frac{B}{k}\Big]\sinh kz ,
\qquad f^{\prime\prime\prime}(0)=2k^{2}B .
$$

Then

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}f^{\prime\prime\prime}(0)\cos kx
            =2\mu k B\cos kx =\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx ,
\tag{1}
$$

so that with the isostatic restoring stress

$$
B=\frac{\Delta\rho g\,e}{2\mu k},\qquad 
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=2\mu k B .
$$

The traction free base is

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff f^{\prime\prime\prime}(h)=3k^{2}f^{\prime}(h),\qquad
