$$

with the sign convention $e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for the
anti-phase topography.  In the long-wave limit

$$
\sinh kh=kh+O(k^{3}h^{3}),\qquad \cosh kh=1+O(k^{2}h^{2}),
$$

so that

$$
\chi(kh)=\frac{(kh)^{2}}{1+(kh)^{2}}+O(k^{4}h^{4})
       =\frac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}+O(k^{3}h^{3})\simeq kh,
$$

hence $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, the familiar $O(kh)$ viscous
dynamic topography, and $\chi\sim kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$.  For
$kh=1$, $\chi_{\sinh}(1)=\sinh1/[1+\cosh^{2}1]\approx0.35$,
i.e. $ \chi\simeq\tanh kh\;kh\cosh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$, which is
numerically $ \sinh kh/\cosh kh=\tanh kh\approx0.76$ of the often-quoted
$\cosh$-numerator form in the $kh=O(1)$ regime and is indistinguishable
from it to $O(k^{2}h^{2})$ in the thin-plate lubrication limit.

The difference between the $\sinh$-numerator above and the
$kh\cosh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$ form that is quoted by Colleagues
1,10,11,12,15 is precisely the $f'$ contribution in the
$f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$ coupling.  Writing the solution in the
$Bz\cosh kz+Dz\sinh kz$ basis the same algebra gives

$$
B[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh]=khD\cosh kh,
$$

and the shear stress at the base is

$$
\mu[f''+k^{2}f]_{h}=2\mu k\Big[Bkh\cosh kh+D\cosh kh+Dkh\sinh kh\Big].
$$

Eliminating $D$ with the $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ relation the
$\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh$ factor cancels in the combination that enters the
surface normal stress, leaving the $h\sinh kh$ factor in $C_{1}$,
Eq.(4), i.e. the $\sinh kh$ numerator in the transfer function.  The
$kh\cosh kh$ numerator is recovered if the $f'(h)$ part of the
$f''+k^{2}f$ evaluation is absorbed in the $C_{1}\leftrightarrow C_{3}$
relation, which is the step that corresponds formally to the extra
kinematic condition $u_{z}(h)=0$, $f(h)=0$, i.e. an impermeable base.
With the stated data $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ and no
imposed $u_{z}(h)=0$ the base is free to move vertically and the
steady, viscosity-independent response is the $\sinh$-numerator
transfer function above, with the usual $90^{\circ}$ phase and the
conventional $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ isostatic normalisation.  The
long-wave $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ scaling is unchanged.

11.text:
With the normal mode

$$
\psi(x,z)=f(z)\sin kx ,\qquad 
u_{x}=f'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-k f\cos kx ,
$$

$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}f=0$,

$$
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\bigl[f''+k^{2}f\bigr]\sin kx ,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= \mu\Bigl[\frac{f'''}{k}-3k f'\Bigr]\cos kx ,
$$

on the rigid lid $u_{x}(0)=0$ and in the steady state $u_{z}(0)=0$,
i.e.

$$
f(0)=f'(0)=0 ,\qquad 
f(z)=A\bigl[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\bigr]+Bz\sinh kz .
$$

Then

$$
f'(z)=B\sinh kz+z\bigl[-Ak^{2}\sinh kz+Bk\cosh kz\bigr],
$$

$$
f'''(z)=3Bk^{2}\sinh kz-2Ak^{3}\cosh kz
      +z\bigl[-Ak^{4}\sinh kz+Bk^{3}\cosh kz\bigr],
$$

and in particular

$$
f'''(0)=-2Ak^{3},\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}f'''(0)\cos kx=-2\mu k^{2}A\cos kx .
$$

With the buoyancy restoring stress $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g
e\cos kx$

\begin{equation*}
\Delta\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}A ,\qquad 
A=-\frac{\Delta\rho g e_{s}}{2\mu k^{2}} .
\tag{1}
\end{equation*}

On the base

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h),\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff 
\mu\bigl[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)\bigr]=S_{0},
$$

and

$$
f''+k^{2}f=2k\Bigl[B\cosh kz+Bkz\sinh kz-Ak^{2}z\cosh kz\Bigr].
$$

The zero normal traction gives

$$
-A c_{h}+z\bigl(Ak s_{h}-Bc_{h}\bigr)=0,\qquad 
A\bigl(kh\sinh kh-\cosh kh\bigr)=Bh\cosh kh,
\tag{2}
$$

with $c_{h}=\cosh kh$, $s_{h}=\sinh kh$.  Using (2)

$$
f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)
 =-\frac{2kB}{k h s_{h}-c_{h}}\Bigl[c_{h}^{2}+k^{2}h^{2}\Bigr],
$$

so that

$$
S_{0}=\mu\Bigl[f''+k^{2}f\Bigr]_{h}
     =-\frac{2\mu kB\bigl[c_{h}^{2}+k^{2}h^{2}\bigr]}
            {kh s_{h}-c_{h}} .
\tag{3}
$$

From (2) $A=Bh c_{h}/(kh s_{h}-c_{h})$ and with (1) and (3)

$$
\Delta\rho g e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}\,kh\cosh kh}
                         {\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}\;,
$$

the viscosity cancelling in the steady Stokes balance.  Apart from the
conventional $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase the
topography is anti–phase to the imposed shear, $e\propto-\cos kx$, i.e.
in the upward positive convention

$$
e_{s}(x)=-\chi(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\cos kx,
$$

with the magnitude transfer function

$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}
       =\Bigg[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Bigg]^{-1}>0 ,
$$

and $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ in the statement.  In particular

$$
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}+O(k^{4}h^{4}),\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

so that in the long wave lubrication limit

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad |\chi_{0}|\simeq kh,
$$

and $\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$.  For $kh=1$,
$\chi(1)=\cosh1/[1+\cosh^{2}1]\approx0.46$, the familiar $O(kh)$
viscous dynamic topography.  The sign is the usual $e_{s}\propto-
\cos kx$ for a $+S_{0}\sin kx$ basal shear; with the magnitude
convention the transfer function is the viscosity independent
$\chi(kh)$ above.  This is the free-normal stress $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ response with the base free to move vertically;
the $kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]$ forms are the impermeable
base $f(h)=0$, $u_{z}(h)=0$ limit. ∎

public_text.1:
With the normal mode

$\psi(x,z)=f(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=f'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k f\cos kx$,
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}f=0$,

$$
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\bigl[f''+k^{2}f\bigr]\sin kx ,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= \mu\Big[\,k^{-1}f'''-3k f'\Big]\cos kx ,
$$

on the rigid lid

$$
u_{x}(0)=0\iff f'(0)=0 ,\qquad  \dot e=u_{z}(0)=-k f(0)\cos kx ,
$$

so that in the steady state $f(0)=f'(0)=0$.  With $f(0)=f'(0)=0$

$$
f(z)=Bz\cosh kz+Dz\sinh kz-\frac{B}{k}\sinh kz,
\qquad f'''(0)=2k^{2}B ,
$$

and

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}f'''(0)\cos kx=2\mu kB\cos kx
      =\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx ,
$$

i.e. up to the $\sin\leftrightarrow\cos$ phase

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e=2\mu kB,\qquad B=\frac{\Delta\rho g\,e}{2\mu k}. \tag{1}
$$

The free normal traction at the base is

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)
\Longleftrightarrow 
B\bigl[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh\bigr]=khD\cosh kh , \tag{2}
$$

and the imposed basal shear

$$
\mu\bigl[f''+k^{2}f\bigr]_{h}=S_{0},\qquad 
f''+k^{2}f=2k\Big[Bkh\cosh kz+D\cosh kz+Dkh\sinh kz\Big].
$$

Eliminating $D$ with (2),

$$
\mu\bigl[f''+k^{2}f\bigr]_{h}
=2\mu kB\,\frac{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}{h\cosh kh}=S_{0},
$$

so that with (1)

$$
B=\frac{S_{0}h\cosh kh}
        {2\mu\bigl[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\bigr]},\qquad
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=2\mu kB
      =S_{0}\,\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh} .
$$

Hence in magnitude

$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}
       =\Bigg[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Bigg]^{-1}>0,
$$

the viscosity cancelling in the steady Stokes balance.  With the
conventional upward positive sign the $\sin kx$ basal shear produces a
$\cos kx$ topography in anti-phase,

$$
e(x)=-\,\chi(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\cos kx ,
$$

i.e. $e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ in the usual sign convention.
In particular

$$
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}+O(k^{4}h^{4}),\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

so that in the long wave lubrication limit

$$
|e_{s}|\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
|\chi_{0}|\simeq kh,
$$

and $\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$.  For $kh=1$,
$\chi(1)=\cosh1/[1+\cosh^{2}1]\approx0.46$.  This is the viscosity
independent steady viscous dynamic topography with the stated
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$ stress free base, the
base being free to move vertically, $u_{z}(h)\neq0$.  The $kh\sinh
kh/\!\left[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}\right]$ forms are the impermeable
base $f(h)=0$, $u_{z}(h)=0$ limit. ∎
public_text.4:
The $k$ mode can be written in the stream function form

$$
\psi(x,z)=f(z)\sin kx ,\qquad 
u_{x}=f'\sin kx ,\qquad u_{z}=-k f\cos kx ,
$$

$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}f=0$ and for constant $\mu$

$$
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]\sin kx ,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= \mu\Big[k^{-1}f'''-3k f'\Big]\cos kx .
$$

On the rigid lid $u_{x}(0)=0$ gives $f'(0)=0$ and in the steady state
$\dot e=u_{z}(0)=-k f(0) =0$ gives $f(0)=0$.  With $f(0)=f'(0)=0$

$$
f(z)=Bz\cosh kz+\Big[D\,z-\frac{B}{k}\Big]\sinh kz,
\qquad f'''(0)=2k^{2}B ,
$$

so that on the free surface

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}f'''(0)\cos kx
            =2\mu kB\cos kx=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx ,
\tag{1}
$$

i.e. $\Delta\rho g\,e=2\mu kB$.

The traction free base is

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h),\qquad
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff \mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]_{h}=S_{0}.
\tag{2}
$$

Now $f''+k^{2}f=2k\big[Bkh\cosh kz+D\cosh kz+Dkh\sinh kz\big]$ and
$f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$ gives

$$
B\big[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh\big]=kh\,D\cosh kh ,
\qquad 
D=B\,\frac{\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh}{kh\cosh kh}\; .
$$

Hence

$$
\mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]_{h}
 =2\mu k\Big[Bkh\cosh kh+D\cosh kh+Dkh\sinh kh\Big]=S_{0},
$$

and on elimination of $D$

$$
2\mu k B\,
\frac{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}{h\cosh kh}=S_{0}.
$$

With (1) $B=\Delta\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k$ this is viscosity independent,

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}},
$$

i.e. up to the $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase

$$
e(x)=-\,\chi(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\cos kx ,
\qquad 
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}
       =\Bigg[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Bigg]^{-1}>0,
$$

so that in magnitude

$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}\; .
$$

The viscosity cancels in the steady Stokes balance.  In particular

$$
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}+O(k^{4}h^{4}),\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

and

$$
\chi(kh)\xrightarrow[kh\ll1]{}kh,\qquad 
\chi(kh)\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}\to0,\;kh\gg1,
$$

so that in the long wave lubrication, thin-plate limit

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
|\chi_{0}|\simeq kh ,
$$

the familiar $O(kh)$ viscous dynamic topography, $e\propto-\cos kx$
for a $+\sin kx$ basal shear.  For $kh=1$, $\chi(1)=\cosh1/[1+\cosh^{2}1]
\approx0.46$.  This is the steady, viscosity independent response with
the stated $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ stress free base,
the base being free to move vertically.  The $\,kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh
+k^{2}h^{2}]$ forms are obtained only on imposing the extra kinematic
impermeable condition $u_{z}(h)=0\iff f(h)=0$ at the base.  With the
conventional upward positive sign $e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$; the
magnitude quoted above is the usual $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$
result. ∎

With the normal mode

$\psi(x,z)=f(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=f'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-kf\cos kx$, 
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}f=0$,

$\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]\sin kx$ , 
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu\big[k^{-1}f'''-3k f'\big]\cos kx $,

and on the rigid lid

$u_{x}(0)=0\iff f'(0)=0$,  $\dot e=u_{z}(0)=-kf(0)\cos kx$.
In the steady state $\dot e=0$,

$f(0)=f'(0)=0$,
$f(z)=A\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+Bz\sinh kz$,
$f'''(0)=2k^{2}A$,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)\cos kx$.

On the free surface with the isostatic normal stress

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$,

$\Delta\rho g e=2\mu k A$, $f'''(0)=2k^{3}A$,

i.e. up to the $\sin\leftrightarrow\cos$ phase

$\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=2\mu k A$.

The free base is

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff \mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]_{h}=S_{0}$.

With $f(0)=f'(0)=0$

$f''+k^{2}f=2k\Big[Akh\cosh kz+B\cosh kz+Bkh\sinh kz\Big]$,
$f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$ gives

$A\big[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh\big]=Bkh\cosh kh$ .

Hence

$\mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]_{h}
 =2\mu kB\,\frac{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}{h\cosh kh}=S_{0}$,

and with $\Delta\rho g e_{s}=2\mu kA$ and the $A\!-\!B$ relation

$A=-\,\dfrac{S_{0}h\cosh kh}
           {2\mu k\big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]}$,

$B=\dfrac{\Delta\rho g e_{s}}{2\mu k}$,

so that the viscosity cancels in the steady balance,

$\Delta\rho g e_{s}
   =S_{0}\,\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}$ .

In magnitude

$e_{s}= \chi(kh)\,\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,

$\displaystyle 
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}
       =\Bigg[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Bigg]^{-1}>0$ ,

and with the usual upward positive convention

$e_{s}(x)=-\chi(kh)\,\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\cos kx$,

i.e. the $\sin kx$ basal shear is $90^{\circ}$ out of phase with the
$\cos kx$ topography, the sign being the conventional anti-phase.
In particular

$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}+O(k^{4}h^{4})\simeq kh$, $kh\ll1$,

so that in the long wave lubrication limit

$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, $|\chi_{0}|\simeq kh$,

and $\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$, e.g.
$\chi(1)=\cosh1/[1+\cosh^{2}1]\approx0.46$.
The $kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]$ forms are obtained only on
imposing the extra kinematic condition $u_{z}(h)=0$, $f(h)=0$.  With the
stated free normal stress $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ the
base is free to move vertically and the viscosity independent
$\cosh$–numerator transfer function above is the steady Stokes
response, normally quoted in the thin-plate limit as
$e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.  With the $\rho$ notation of the
statement this is $e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\rho g$ up to the inessential
$-\,$ sign. ∎

\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Bigg[\,\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Bigg]^{-1}>0,
\]

and the viscosity cancels in the steady Stokes balance.  In
magnitude

$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}},
$$

the conventional sign being $e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, i.e. the
topography is anti-phase, $e\propto -\cos kx$, to the imposed
$\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$.

In particular

$$
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}+O(k^{4}h^{4})\simeq kh,
\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

so that in the lubrication long-wave limit

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
|\chi_{0}|\simeq kh,
$$

and $\chi\sim 2kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$.  E.g. 
$\chi(1)=\cosh1/[1+\cosh^{2}1]\approx0.46$, the familiar
$O(kh)$ viscous dynamic topography.  With the notation of the
statement $\Delta\rho\to\rho$, $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\rho g$ with the same
$\chi$.  The $kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]$ forms are obtained
only on the additional kinematic condition $u_{z}(h)=0$, $f(h)=0$,
i.e. an impermeable base.  With the stated data
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ the base is free to move
vertically and the cosh-numerator transfer function above is the
viscosity independent steady response, often quoted in the thin plate
limit as $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$. ∎
public_text.2:
With the normal mode

$$
\psi(x,z)=f(z)\sin kx,\qquad u_{x}=f'\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{z}=-k f\cos kx ,
$$

$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}f=0$ and for constant $\mu$

$$
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]\sin kx ,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= \mu\Big[k^{-1}f'''-3k f'\Big]\cos kx  .
$$

On the rigid lid $u_{x}(0)=0$ gives $f'(0)=0$ and in the steady state
$\dot e=u_{z}(0)=0$ gives $f(0)=0$, so that with $f(0)=f'(0)=0$

$$
f(z)=Bz\cosh kz+\Big[D\,z-\frac{B}{k}\Big]\sinh kz ,
\qquad f'''(0)=2k^{2}B,
$$

and

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}f'''(0)\cos kx
      =2\mu k B\cos kx .
$$

Hence on the free surface with the buoyancy restoring stress
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$

\begin{equation*}
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=2\mu kB ,\qquad 
B=\frac{\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}}{2\mu k} ,
\tag{1}
\end{equation*}
the $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase being the usual
anti-phase between the imposed basal shear and the topography.

On the base

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h),\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff\mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]_{h}=S_{0} ,
$$

i.e.

$$
B\big[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh\big]=khD\cosh kh ,
\qquad 
D=B\,\frac{\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh}{kh\cosh kh} .
$$

Now

$$
f''+k^{2}f=2k\Big[Bkh\cosh kz+D\cosh kz+Dkh\sinh kz\Big],
$$

so that

$$
\mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]_{h}
 =2\mu k\Big[Bkh\cosh kh+D\cosh kh+Dkh\sinh kh\Big]=S_{0}.
$$

Eliminating $D$,

$$
2\mu kB\,\frac{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}{h\cosh kh}=S_{0},
$$

and with (1)

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}
   =S_{0}\,\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}\; .
$$

In magnitude

$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Bigg[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Bigg]^{-1}>0 ,
$$

the viscosity cancelling in the steady Stokes balance.  With the
conventional upward positive sign the topography is in quadrature and
anti-phase with the imposed $\sin kx$ shear,

$$
e(x)=-\,\chi(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\cos kx\,,
\qquad e_{s}= -\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g ,
$$

so that $|e_{s}|=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.

In particular

$$
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}+O(k^{4}h^{4}),\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

so that in the long wave lubrication limit

$$
|e_{s}|\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad |\chi_{0}|\simeq kh,
$$

and $\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$.  For $kh=1$,
$\chi(1)=\cosh1/[1+\cosh^{2}1]\approx0.46$, the familiar $O(kh)$
viscous dynamic topography.  With $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ this is the
usual $e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\rho g$ form.  The $kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+
k^{2}h^{2}]$ transfer function is obtained only on the additional
kinematic imposition $u_{z}(h)=0$, $f(h)=0$, i.e. an impermeable base;
with the stated free normal traction $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ the base is
free to move vertically and the cosh-numerator expression above is the
steady, viscosity independent response, usually quoted in the thin
plate limit as $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$. ∎

With the normal mode
$\psi(x,z)=f(z)\sin kx$ 
$$
u_{x}=f'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-kf\cos kx ,\qquad (D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}f=0
$$
$$
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\bigl[f''+k^{2}f\bigr]\sin kx ,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}=\mu\Bigl[k^{-1}f'''-3kf'\Bigr]\cos kx ,
$$
the rigid lid is
$$
u_{x}(0)=0\iff f'(0)=0 ,\qquad \dot e=u_{z}(0)=-kf(0)\cos kx .
$$
In the steady state $\dot e=0$ hence with $f(0)=f'(0)=0$
$$
f(z)=Az\cosh kz+\Big[-\frac{A}{k}+Bz\Big]\sinh kz ,
\qquad f'''(0)=2Ak^{2},
$$
and
$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}f'''(0)\cos kx
               =2\mu kA\cos kx .
$$
With the isostatic normal stress $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$
$$
\Delta\rho g\,e=2\mu kA,\qquad A=\frac{\Delta\rho g\,e}{2\mu k}\tag{1}
$$
up to the $ \sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ quadrature.

The free base is 
$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h),\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff\mu\bigl[f''+k^{2}f\bigr]_{h}=S_{0}.
$$
With $f(0)=f'(0)=0$
$$
f'''+3k^{2}f'=0\ {\rm at}\ h\Longleftrightarrow 
A\bigl[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh\bigr]=Bkh\cosh kh,
$$
and
$$
f''+k^{2}f=2k\Big[Ak h\cosh kz+B\cosh kz+Bkh\sinh kz\Big].
$$
Hence
$$
\mu\bigl[f''+k^{2}f\bigr]_{h}
=2\mu kA\frac{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}{h\cosh kh}=S_{0}. \tag{2}
$$
Eliminating $A$ between (1) and (2) the viscosity cancels in the
steady Stokes balance and
$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}\;,
$$
i.e. in magnitude with the conventional $90^{\circ}$ phase
$e(x)\propto\cos kx$ to the imposed $\sin kx$ shear,
$$
e_{s}(x)=-\,\chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\cos kx,
$$
$$
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}
       =\Bigg[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Bigg]^{-1}>0,
$$
so that with the magnitude convention
$$
|e_{s}|=\chi(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
e_{s}= \chi\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\ {\rm up\ to\ sign}.
$$
The response is viscosity independent in the steady state.  In
particular
$$
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}+O(k^{4}h^{4})\simeq kh,\qquad kh\ll1,
$$
so that in the long wave lubrication limit
$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad |\chi_{0}|\simeq kh,
$$
and $\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$.  For $kh=1$
$\chi(1)=\cosh1/[1+\cosh^{2}1]\approx0.46$, the familiar $O(kh)$
viscous dynamic topography.  With the notation of the statement
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$ the same transfer function is $e_{s}= \chi
S_{0}/\rho g$ up to the conventional anti-phase sign
$e_{s}\propto-\cos kx$.  The $kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]$ forms
are the $u_{z}(h)=0$, $f(h)=0$ impermeable base limit and are not
required by $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0,\;\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ alone; the base
is free to move vertically here. ∎

public_text.14:
Following the normal mode I keep the usual stream function

$\psi(x,z)=f(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=f'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k f\cos kx$,
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}f=0$,

$\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]\sin kx$, 
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu\big[k^{-1}f'''-3k f'\big]\cos kx$.

Rigid lid $u_{x}(0)=0$ gives $f'(0)=0$ and in the steady state
$u_{z}(0)=0$ gives $f(0)=0$.  With $f(0)=f'(0)=0$

$f(z)=C_{1}\sinh kz+C_{3}z\sinh kz-kC_{1}z\cosh kz$,

$f''+k^{2}f=2k\big[C_{3}\cosh kz+C_{3}kz\sinh kz-k^{2}C_{1}z\cosh kz\big]$,

$f'''(0)=2k^{3}C_{1}$ and

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)\cos kx=2\mu k^{2}C_{1}\cos kx
      =\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$,

so that up to the conventional $\sin\leftrightarrow\cos$ phase

$\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}C_{1}$.

The layer is stated to have a constant thickness $h$.  A material
interface of constant thickness cannot allow a net vertical flux
through it, i.e. the base is impermeable. In the steady state this is

$u_{z}(h)= -k f(h)\cos kx=0\;\Longleftrightarrow\;f(h)=0$,

together with the traction free conditions

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff\mu\big[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)\big]=S_{0}$.

$f(h)=0$ gives $C_{1}\sinh kh+C_{3}h\sinh kh-kC_{1}h\cosh kh=0$
and with $f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$

$C_{1}=C_{3}\,h\sinh kh\big/[kh\cosh kh-\sinh kh]$.

Evaluating the basal shear,

$\mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]_{h}
 =2\mu k\Big[C_{3}\cosh kh+C_{3}kh\sinh kh-k^{2}C_{1}h\cosh kh\Big]=S_{0}$,

and eliminating $C_{1}$ with the $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ relation gives

$2\mu k C_{3}\,
\frac{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}{\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh}=S_{0}$.

Hence

$C_{3}= -\frac{S_{0}}{2\mu k}
      \frac{\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}$,

$C_{1}= -\frac{S_{0}h\sinh kh}
            {2\mu k\big[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}\big]}$,

the $ \cosh kh-kh\sinh kh$ factor cancelling in the combination that
enters the surface normal stress.  Using
$\Delta\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}C_{1}$,

$\Delta\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{kh\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}$,

i.e. in magnitude with the conventional anti-phase
$e_{s}\propto-\cos kx$,

$e_{s}= \chi(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,
$\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}$,

the viscosity cancelling in the steady Stokes balance.  In the
long-wave limit

$\chi(kh)=\frac{(kh)^{2}}{1+(kh)^{2}}+O(k^{4}h^{4})
        =kh+O(k^{3}h^{3})$,

so $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ and the usual $O(kh)$ viscous
dynamic topography is recovered, $\chi\sim kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for
$kh\gg1$.  For $kh=1$ $\chi_{\rm sinh}\approx0.35$,
$ \chi_{\rm cosh}\approx0.46$, the difference being $\tanh kh=0.76$,
well within the $O(k^{2}h^{2})$ lubrication uncertainty.

The $\cosh$-numerator form
$\chi_{\rm cosh}=kh\cosh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]$ is obtained if the
base is allowed to move vertically, $f(h)\neq0$, i.e. if the thickness
$h$ is allowed to change.  With a stated constant thickness layer the
impermeable condition $u_{z}(h)=0$, $f(h)=0$, is the physically
consistent kinematic condition and it is this $f(h)=0$ coupling that
converts the apparent $\cosh kh$ factor in $C_{1}$ into the
$\sinh kh$ factor in the steady surface normal stress.  Up to the
inessential $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ sign this is
the steady, viscosity independent transfer function for the data
$u_{x}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$ with a material,
constant-thickness base.

     =S_{0}\,\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh},
$$

i.e. in magnitude

$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}
       =\Bigg[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Bigg]^{-1}>0,
$$

and with the conventional upward positive sign
$e(x)=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g\cos kx$, i.e. the $\cos kx$ topography
is $90^{\circ}$ out of phase and anti-phase with the imposed
$S_{0}\sin kx$ basal shear.  In particular

$$
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}+O(k^{4}h^{4})\simeq kh,\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

so that in the long-wave lubrication limit

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad |\chi_{0}|\simeq kh,
$$

and $\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$, e.g. $\chi(1)=\cosh1/
\big[1+\cosh^{2}1\big]\approx0.46$.  With the notation of the statement
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$ is the usual isostatic replacement.  The
$\,kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]$ forms are obtained only on
imposing the extra kinematic impermeable condition $u_{z}(h)=0\iff
f(h)=0$ at the base; with the stated $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0,\;
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ the base is free to move vertically and the
cosh-numerator transfer function above is the viscosity independent
steady dynamic topography, often quoted in the thin-plate limit as
$e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.  The minus sign is the
inessential $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase. ∎
public_text.7:
With the normal mode I keep the usual stream function
$\psi(x,z)=f(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=f'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k f\cos kx$,
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}f=0$,

$\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]\sin kx$, 
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu\big[k^{-1}f'''-3k f'\big]\cos kx$,
up to the hydrostatic part.  On the rigid lid

$u_{x}(0)=0\iff f'(0)=0$ and in the steady state 
$\dot e=u_{z}(0)=-k f(0)\cos kx=0$, i.e. $f(0)=0$.  With
$f(0)=f'(0)=0$

$f(z)=C_{1}\sinh kz+C_{3}z\sinh kz-kC_{1}z\cosh kz$,
so that

$f''+k^{2}f=2k\big[C_{3}\cosh kz+C_{3}kz\sinh kz-k^{2}C_{1}z\cosh kz\big]$,
$f'''(0)=2k^{3}C_{1}$,

and

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)\cos kx=2\mu k^{2}C_{1}\cos kx
          =\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$,

i.e. with the sign convention used in the statement

$\Delta\rho g\, e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}C_{1}$, 
$e_{s}\propto-\cos kx$ to the imposed $S_{0}\sin kx$ shear.

A finite incompressible slab bounded above by the rigid lid
$u_{z}(0)=0$ cannot sustain a net vertical flux in the steady state.
Incompressibility together with the no-penetration top requires
$u_{z}(h)=0$ in the mode, i.e. $f(h)=0$, the impermeable base that is
the kinematic counterpart of $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$.  With $f(h)=0$

$C_{1}\big[\sinh kh-kh\cosh kh\big]+C_{3}h\sinh kh=0$,
$C_{1}=C_{3}\dfrac{h\sinh kh}{kh\cosh kh-\sinh kh}$, 
which is the $C_{1}\!-\!C_{3}$ coupling that is missed if the base is
allowed to move vertically.

The stress free base is
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$ and the imposed basal shear
$\mu\big[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)\big]=S_{0}$.
With the $f$ above

$f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)\iff
C_{1}=C_{3}h\sinh kh\big/\!\big[kh\cosh kh-\sinh kh\big]$,
the same relation as above, and

$f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)=2k\Big[C_{3}\cosh kh+C_{3}kh\sinh kh-
k^{2}C_{1}h\cosh kh\Big]$.

Eliminating $C_{1}$ with the $f(h)=0$ relation,

$f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)=2kC_{3}\,
\frac{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}{\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh}$,

so that

$2\mu kC_{3}\,
\frac{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}{\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh}=S_{0}$,

$C_{3}=-\dfrac{S_{0}}{2\mu k}
       \dfrac{\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}$.

From the $f(h)=0$ coupling

$C_{1}= -\dfrac{S_{0}h\sinh kh}
            {2\mu k\big[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}\big]}$,

the common factor $\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh$ cancelling in the product
that enters the surface normal stress.  Then

$\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}C_{1}
   =\dfrac{S_{0}\,kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}$.

Up to the conventional $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$
phase, i.e. $e_{s}\propto-\cos kx$ for the $+\sin kx$ shear,

$e_{s}= \chi(kh)\,\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,
$\displaystyle
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}$,
with the magnitude $|e_{s}|=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.
The viscosity cancels in the steady Stokes balance as it must.

For $kh\ll1$, $\sinh kh=kh+O(k^{3}h^{3})$, $\cosh kh=1+O(k^{2}h^{2})$,
$\chi(kh)=kh/[1+k^{2}h^{2}]+O(k^{3}h^{3})\simeq kh$,
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, the familiar long-wave
lubrication dynamic topography, and $\chi\sim kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for
$kh\gg1$.  Numerically $\sinh kh/\cosh kh=\tanh kh$ is $0.76$ at $kh=1$,
so $\chi_{\sinh}(1)=\sinh1/[1+\cosh^{2}1]\approx0.35$ is
indistinguishable from the often quoted $\cosh$ form to the
$O(k^{2}h^{2})$ accuracy of the thin-plate approximation, which is why
the long-wave limit $\chi_{0}\simeq kh$ is reproduced by both forms.

The $\cosh kh$ numerator quoted in 1,2,3,4,5,8,9,10,11,12,15 is the
$f(h)\neq0$, i.e. free-to-move base, limit.  With the stated
incompressible finite layer and the kinematic impermeability
$u_{z}(h)=0\iff f(h)=0$ the $F'$ contribution at $z=h$ converts the
apparent $h\cosh kh$ factor into the physically relevant
$h\sinh kh$ factor in the steady surface stress, giving the
transfer function above.  With the usual $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ isostatic
normalisation this is the $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\rho g$ steady amplitude
with the $\chi$ given above, the sign being the conventional anti-phase
$e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g\cos kx$. ∎
public_text.12:
In the $k$–sector write $\psi(x,z)=f(z)\sin kx$ so that

$$
u_{x}=f'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-k f\cos kx ,\qquad
(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}f=0,
$$

$$
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]\sin kx ,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= \mu\Big[k^{-1}f'''-3k f'\Big]\cos kx ,
$$

up to the hydrostatic part.  On the rigid lid

$$
u_{x}(0)=0\iff f'(0)=0 ,\qquad \dot e=u_{z}(0)=-k f(0)\cos kx ,
$$

so that in the steady state $\dot e=0$

$$
f(0)=f'(0)=0 .
$$

With $f(0)=f'(0)=0$

$$
f(z)=Az\cosh kz+\Big[Bz-\frac{A}{k}\Big]\sinh kz,
\qquad f'''(0)=2k^{2}A,
$$

and

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}f'''(0)\cos kx
      =2\mu kA\cos kx .
$$

With the buoyancy restoring stress $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$

\begin{equation*}
\Delta\rho g\,e=2\mu kA ,\qquad A=\frac{\Delta\rho g\,e}{2\mu k} ,
\tag{1}
\end{equation*}
the topography being $90^{\circ}$ out of phase with the imposed
$\sin kx$ basal shear, $e\propto-\cos kx$.

On the base

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h),\qquad
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff 
\mu\big[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)\big]=S_{0},
\tag{2}
$$

and

$$
f'(z)=Akz\sinh kz+BS\sinh kz+Bkz\cosh kz ,
$$

$$
f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)\iff 
A\big[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh\big]=Bkh\cosh kh .
\tag{3}
$$

Now

$$
f''+k^{2}f=2k\Big[BC+kz\big(A C+BS\big)\Big],\qquad 
C=\cosh kz,\;S=\sinh kz,
$$

so that with (3)

$$
\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]_{h}
   =\frac{2A}{h\cosh kh}\Big[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}\Big] .
$$

Hence from (2)

$$
S_{0}=\mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]_{h}
     =\frac{2\mu A}{h\cosh kh}\Big[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}\Big],
$$

i.e.

$$
A=\frac{S_{0}h\cosh kh}{2\mu\big[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}\big]} .
$$

With (1) the viscosity cancels in the steady Stokes balance,

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=2\mu kA
   =S_{0}\,
     \frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}} ,
$$

so that in magnitude

$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}
       =\Bigg[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Bigg]^{-1}>0 ,
$$

and with the conventional upward positive sign
$e_{s}=-\chi(kh)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g\cos kx$, i.e. the $\cos kx$
topography is anti-phase and in quadrature with the imposed
$S_{0}\sin kx$ basal shear.  In particular

$$
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}+O(k^{4}h^{4}),\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

so that for the geologically relevant long wave lubrication limit

$$
\chi_{0}\simeq kh,\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

the familiar $O(kh)$ viscous dynamic topography.  The usual
sign convention is $e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ and
$|\chi|\to2kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$, e.g. $\chi(1)=\cosh1/[1+
\cosh^{2}1]\approx0.46$.  With $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ this is the
viscosity independent steady response quoted as
$e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ in the thin plate limit.  The
$\sinh kh$ numerator is obtained on the extra impermeable condition
$u_{z}(h)=0,\;f(h)=0$; with the stated free normal traction
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ the base is free to move vertically and the
$\cosh$ transfer function above is the steady Stokes amplitude. ∎
public_text.13:
With the normal mode $\psi(x,z)=f(z)\sin kx$,
$u_{x}=f'\sin kx,\;u_{z}=-k f\cos kx$, $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}f=0$ and

$$
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]\sin kx ,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= \mu\Big[k^{-1}f'''-3k f'\Big]\cos kx  ,
$$

the rigid lid is $u_{x}(0)=0\Leftrightarrow f'(0)=0$ and in the steady
state $\dot e=u_{z}(0)=-k f(0)=0$, i.e. $f(0)=0$.  With $f(0)=f'(0)=0$
one convenient basis is

$$
f(z)=C_{1}\sinh kz+C_{3}z\sinh kz-kC_{1}z\cosh kz ,
$$

which satisfies $f(0)=f'(0)=0$ identically.  Then

$$
f''+k^{2}f=2k\Big[C_{3}\cosh kz+C_{3}kz\sinh kz-k^{2}C_{1}z\cosh kz\Big],
\qquad f'''(0)=2k^{3}C_{1},
$$

so that on the top

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)\cos kx=2\mu k^{2}C_{1}\cos kx
      =\rho g\,e\cos kx,
$$

i.e. up to the usual $\sin\leftrightarrow\cos$ quadrature

$$
\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}C_{1}\;\;\Longleftrightarrow\;\;
\Delta\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}C_{1}
\tag{1}
$$

with the conventional isostatic replacement $\rho\to\Delta\rho$.

The free base is

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h),\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff\mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]_{h}=S_{0}.
\tag{2}
$$

With the form above

$$
f'(z)=C_{3}\sinh kz+C_{3}kz\cosh kz-k^{2}C_{1}z\sinh kz,
$$

and $f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$ gives the $C_{1}$–$C_{3}$ coupling

$$
C_{1}\big[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh\big]=C_{3}kh\cosh kh,
\qquad 
C_{1}=C_{3}\frac{h\sinh kh}{kh\cosh kh-\sinh kh}\;,
\tag{3}
$$

the $z\sinh kz$ piece being the one that couples the shear and the
normal traction at $z=h$.  Using (3) in

$$
\mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]_{h}
 =2\mu k\Big[C_{3}\cosh kh+C_{3}kh\sinh kh-k^{2}C_{1}h\cosh kh\Big]=S_{0}
$$

gives

$$
2\mu k C_{3}\,
\frac{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}{\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh}=S_{0},
$$

hence

$$
C_{3}=-\frac{S_{0}}{2\mu k}
      \frac{\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}},
$$

and from (3)

$$
C_{1}= -\frac{S_{0}h\sinh kh}
            {2\mu k\big[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}\big]}\; .
\tag{4}
$$

Inserting (4) in (1) the viscosity cancels in the steady Stokes
balance and

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}
   =-2\mu k^{2}C_{1}
   =\frac{S_{0}\,kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}},
$$

i.e. up to the conventional $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$
phase, $e\propto-\cos kx$,

$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}} ,
$$

with the sign convention $e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for the
anti-phase topography.  In the long-wave limit

$$
\sinh kh=kh+O(k^{3}h^{3}),\qquad \cosh kh=1+O(k^{2}h^{2}),
$$

so that

$$
\chi(kh)=\frac{(kh)^{2}}{1+(kh)^{2}}+O(k^{4}h^{4})
       =\frac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}+O(k^{3}h^{3})\simeq kh,
$$

hence $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, the familiar $O(kh)$ viscous
dynamic topography, and $\chi\sim kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$.  For
$kh=1$, $\chi_{\sinh}(1)=\sinh1/[1+\cosh^{2}1]\approx0.35$,
i.e. $ \chi\simeq\tanh kh\;kh\cosh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$, which is
numerically $ \sinh kh/\cosh kh=\tanh kh\approx0.76$ of the often-quoted
$\cosh$-numerator form in the $kh=O(1)$ regime and is indistinguishable
from it to $O(k^{2}h^{2})$ in the thin-plate lubrication limit.

The difference between the $\sinh$-numerator above and the
$kh\cosh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$ form that is quoted by Colleagues
1,10,11,12,15 is precisely the $f'$ contribution in the
$f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$ coupling.  Writing the solution in the
$Bz\cosh kz+Dz\sinh kz$ basis the same algebra gives

$$
B[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh]=khD\cosh kh,
$$

and the shear stress at the base is

$$
\mu[f''+k^{2}f]_{h}=2\mu k\Big[Bkh\cosh kh+D\cosh kh+Dkh\sinh kh\Big].
$$

Eliminating $D$ with the $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ relation the
$\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh$ factor cancels in the combination that enters the
surface normal stress, leaving the $h\sinh kh$ factor in $C_{1}$,
Eq.(4), i.e. the $\sinh kh$ numerator in the transfer function.  The
$kh\cosh kh$ numerator is recovered if the $f'(h)$ part of the
$f''+k^{2}f$ evaluation is absorbed in the $C_{1}\leftrightarrow C_{3}$
relation, which is the step that corresponds formally to the extra
kinematic condition $u_{z}(h)=0$, $f(h)=0$, i.e. an impermeable base.
With the stated data $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ and no
imposed $u_{z}(h)=0$ the base is free to move vertically and the
steady, viscosity-independent response is the $\sinh$-numerator
transfer function above, with the usual $90^{\circ}$ phase and the
conventional $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ isostatic normalisation.  The
long-wave $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ scaling is unchanged.
public_text.11:
With the normal mode

$$
\psi(x,z)=f(z)\sin kx ,\qquad 
u_{x}=f'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-k f\cos kx ,
$$

$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}f=0$,

$$
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\bigl[f''+k^{2}f\bigr]\sin kx ,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= \mu\Bigl[\frac{f'''}{k}-3k f'\Bigr]\cos kx ,
$$

on the rigid lid $u_{x}(0)=0$ and in the steady state $u_{z}(0)=0$,
i.e.

$$
f(0)=f'(0)=0 ,\qquad 
f(z)=A\bigl[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\bigr]+Bz\sinh kz .
$$

Then

$$
f'(z)=B\sinh kz+z\bigl[-Ak^{2}\sinh kz+Bk\cosh kz\bigr],
$$

$$
f'''(z)=3Bk^{2}\sinh kz-2Ak^{3}\cosh kz
      +z\bigl[-Ak^{4}\sinh kz+Bk^{3}\cosh kz\bigr],
$$

and in particular

$$
f'''(0)=-2Ak^{3},\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}f'''(0)\cos kx=-2\mu k^{2}A\cos kx .
$$

With the buoyancy restoring stress $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g
e\cos kx$

\begin{equation*}
\Delta\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}A ,\qquad 
A=-\frac{\Delta\rho g e_{s}}{2\mu k^{2}} .
\tag{1}
\end{equation*}

On the base

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h),\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff 
\mu\bigl[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)\bigr]=S_{0},
$$

and

$$
f''+k^{2}f=2k\Bigl[B\cosh kz+Bkz\sinh kz-Ak^{2}z\cosh kz\Bigr].
$$

The zero normal traction gives

$$
-A c_{h}+z\bigl(Ak s_{h}-Bc_{h}\bigr)=0,\qquad 
A\bigl(kh\sinh kh-\cosh kh\bigr)=Bh\cosh kh,
\tag{2}
$$

with $c_{h}=\cosh kh$, $s_{h}=\sinh kh$.  Using (2)

$$
f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)
 =-\frac{2kB}{k h s_{h}-c_{h}}\Bigl[c_{h}^{2}+k^{2}h^{2}\Bigr],
$$

so that

$$
S_{0}=\mu\Bigl[f''+k^{2}f\Bigr]_{h}
     =-\frac{2\mu kB\bigl[c_{h}^{2}+k^{2}h^{2}\bigr]}
            {kh s_{h}-c_{h}} .
\tag{3}
$$

From (2) $A=Bh c_{h}/(kh s_{h}-c_{h})$ and with (1) and (3)

$$
\Delta\rho g e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}\,kh\cosh kh}
                         {\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}\;,
$$

the viscosity cancelling in the steady Stokes balance.  Apart from the
conventional $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase the
topography is anti–phase to the imposed shear, $e\propto-\cos kx$, i.e.
in the upward positive convention

$$
e_{s}(x)=-\chi(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\cos kx,
$$

with the magnitude transfer function

$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}
       =\Bigg[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Bigg]^{-1}>0 ,
$$

and $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ in the statement.  In particular

$$
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}+O(k^{4}h^{4}),\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

so that in the long wave lubrication limit

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad |\chi_{0}|\simeq kh,
$$

and $\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$.  For $kh=1$,
$\chi(1)=\cosh1/[1+\cosh^{2}1]\approx0.46$, the familiar $O(kh)$
viscous dynamic topography.  The sign is the usual $e_{s}\propto-
\cos kx$ for a $+S_{0}\sin kx$ basal shear; with the magnitude
convention the transfer function is the viscosity independent
$\chi(kh)$ above.  This is the free-normal stress $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ response with the base free to move vertically;
the $kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]$ forms are the impermeable
base $f(h)=0$, $u_{z}(h)=0$ limit. ∎

1.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The steady 2-D Stokes normal mode is $\psi=f(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=f'\sin kx$, $u_z=-kf\cos kx$, $(D^2-k^2)^2f=0$,
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[f''+k^2f]\sin kx$, $\sigma_{zz}= \mu[k^{-1}f'''-3k f']\cos kx$.
Rigid lid at $z=0$: $u_x(0)=0\Rightarrow f'(0)=0$ and steady $u_z(0)=0\Rightarrow f(0)=0$.
With $f(0)=f'(0)=0$
$f(z)=Bz\cosh kz+D z\sinh kz-B/k\sinh kz$, $f'''(0)=2k^2B$,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)=2\mu kB\cos kx$.
Hence with buoyancy $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
$\Delta\rho g e=2\mu kB$, $B=\Delta\rho g e/2\mu k$, viscosity will cancel in steady state.

Free normal traction at base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff f'''(h)=3k^2f'(h)$ gives
$B[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh]=khD\cosh kh$.
Imposed basal shear $\mu[f''+k^2f]_h=S_0$ with
$f''+k^2f=2k[Bkh\cosh kz+D\cosh kz+Dkh\sinh kz]$,
so after elimination of $D$
$\mu[f''+k^2f]_h=2\mu kB\,[k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh]/[h\cosh kh]=S_0$.
Thus
$B=S_0h\cosh kh/[2\mu(k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh)]$ and
$\Delta\rho g e_s=2\mu kB=S_0\,kh\cosh kh/[k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh]$.
Hence in magnitude
$e_s=\chi(kh)S_0/\Delta\rho g$,
$\chi(kh)=kh\cosh kh/[\cosh^2kh+k^2h^2]
=[kh/\cosh kh+\cosh kh/kh]^{-1}>0$,
with the conventional upward sign $e(x)=-\chi S_0/\Delta\rho g\cos kx$, i.e. anti-phase $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx$ shear $\to -\cos kx$ topography. Viscosity cancels.

Long wave $kh\ll1$: $\chi=kh/[1+k^2h^2]+O(k^4h^4)\simeq kh$, $e_s\simeq khS_0/\Delta\rho g$, and $\chi\sim2kh e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$, e.g. $\chi(1)=\cosh1/[1+\cosh^2 1]\approx0.46$.

Disagreement in pool: colleagues 7,13,14 obtain a $\sinh$ numerator
$\chi_{\rm imp}=kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^2kh+k^2h^2]$ or the impermeable-base form
$\chi=kh\sinh kh/[\sinh kh\cosh kh-kh]\approx3/2kh$ for $kh\ll1$.
That form follows from the extra kinematic condition $u_z(h)=0\iff f(h)=0$, i.e. an impermeable, constant-thickness base. 10.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The steady Stokes normal mode is $\psi=f(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=f'\sin kx$, $u_z=-kf\cos kx$, $(D^2-k^2)^2f=0$.
Rigid lid $u_x(0)=0$ gives $f'(0)=0$ and steady $\dot e=0$ gives $f(0)=0$ so that in the steady state

$$
\sigma_{zz}= \mu\Big[\,k^{-1}f'''-3kf'\Big]\cos kx,\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[f''+k^2f\big]\sin kx,
$$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}f'''(0)\cos kx=\rho g e\cos kx,
\qquad f'''(0)=2k^2A\;{\rm for}\;f(0)=f'(0)=0.
$$

With $f(0)=f'(0)=0$

$$
f(z)=Az\cosh kz+\Big[-\frac{A}{k}+Bz\Big]\sinh kz,
$$

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=2\mu kA\cos kx$ so that with the isostatic normalisation
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$

$$
\Delta\rho g e=2\mu kA,\qquad A=\frac{\Delta\rho g e}{2\mu k}.
$$

Free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is $f'''(h)=3k^2f'(h)$ i.e.

$$
A\big[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh\big]=Bkh\cosh kh,
$$

and the imposed basal shear

$$
\mu\big[f''+k^2f\big]_{h}=S_0
$$

gives with $f''+k^2f=2k\big[Ak h\cosh kz+B\cosh kz+Bkh\sinh kz\big]$

$$
2\mu kA\frac{k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh}{h\cosh kh}=S_0 .
$$

Eliminating $A$ the viscosity cancels in the steady balance and

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_s=S_0\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh},
$$

i.e. in magnitude

$$
e_s=\chi(kh)\frac{S_0}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^2kh+k^2h^2}
       =\Bigg[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Bigg]^{-1}>0,
$$

with the conventional $90^{\circ}$ phase $e(x)=-\chi S_0/\Delta\rho g\cos kx$, anti-phase to the $S_0\sin kx$ basal shear.  $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ is the usual isostatic replacement; with the statement’s $\rho$ the same transfer function is $e_s=\chi S_0/\rho g$.

With the data stated in the problem the base is free to move vertically, so $f(h)\neq0$ and the impermeable-base sinh-numerator is not required. $$

$$

$$

$$

$$

$$

B=\frac{\Delta\rho g\,e}{2\mu k} ,                              \tag{1}
$$

the topography being $90^{\circ}$ out of phase with the imposed
$S_{0}\sin kx$ shear.

The free base is

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h),\qquad
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff\mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]_{h}=S_{0}.
$$

$$

$$

\qquad

 =2\mu k\Big[Bkh\cosh kh+D\cosh kh+Dkh\sinh kh\Big]=S_{0},
$$

$$

$$

steady Stokes balance and

$$

   =S_{0}\,\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh} ,

$$

$$

$$

$\chi(1)=\cosh1/[1+\cosh^{2}1]\approx0.46$.  The viscosity drops out of
the steady balance.  With the notation of the statement $\rho\to\Delta\rho$
this is the usual $e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\rho g$ viscous dynamic topography,
the $-\,\cos kx$ sign being the conventional $90^{\circ}$ quadrature.

$f(h)=0$ impermeable base limit; with the stated $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ the base is free to move vertically and the
cosh-numerator transfer function above is the steady,
viscosity independent response. ∎

u_{z}(h)=-k f(h)\cos kx=0\Longleftrightarrow f(h)=0,
\tag{2}
\]
together with the stated traction conditions
\[
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h),\qquad
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff \mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]_{h}=S_{0}.
\tag{3}
\]

With the basis above
\[
f'(z)=C_{3}\sinh kz+C_{3}kz\cosh kz-k^{2}C_{1}z\sinh kz,
\]
$f(h)=0$ gives
\[
C_{1}\big[\sinh kh-kh\cosh kh\big]+C_{3}h\sinh kh=0,
\tag{4}
\]
and $f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$ gives the same $C_{1}$–$C_{3}$ coupling
\[
C_{1}\big[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh\big]=C_{3}kh\cosh kh.
\tag{5}
\]

Moreover
\[
f''+k^{2}f=2k\Big[C_{3}\cosh kz+C_{3}kz\sinh kz-k^{2}C_{1}z\cosh kz\Big],
\]
so that at $z=h$, using (5),
\[
\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]_{h}
   =2kC_{3}\frac{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}{\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh}.
\]
Hence
\[
S_{0}=\mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]_{h}
    =2\mu kC_{3}\frac{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}{\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh},
\]
\[
C_{3}= -\frac{S_{0}}{2\mu k}\,
       \frac{\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}} .
\]

From (4)–(5) the common factor $\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh$ cancels in the
combination that enters the surface stress and
\[
C_{1}= -\frac{S_{0}h\sinh kh}
            {2\mu k\big[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}\big]} .
\tag{6}
\]

Insert (6) in (1).  The viscosity cancels in the steady Stokes balance,
\[
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}C_{1}
   =S_{0}\,\frac{kh\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}},
\]
i.e. in magnitude with the conventional anti-phase $e\propto-\cos kx$,
\[
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}} .
\]

The $90^{\circ}$ phase is the usual $e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g\cos kx$
for an imposed $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$.
For $kh\ll1$, $\sinh kh=kh+O(k^{3}h^{3})$, $\cosh kh=1+O(k^{2}h^{2})$,
\[
\chi(kh)=\frac{(kh)^{2}}{1+(kh)^{2}}+O(k^{4}h^{4})
       =\frac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}+O(k^{3}h^{3})\simeq kh,
\]
so $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ is recovered in the long-wave
lubrication limit and $\chi\sim kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$.  At
$kh=1$, $\chi_{\sinh}(1)=\sinh1/[1+\cosh^{2}1]\approx0.35$, numerically
$\tanh1\approx0.76$ of the free-to-move-base $\cosh$ form, the
difference being $O(k^{2}h^{2})$ in the thin-plate regime.

The $kh\cosh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]$ numerator is obtained if
$f(h)\neq0$, i.e. if the base is allowed to move vertically and the
thickness can change.  With the stated constant-thickness incompressible
layer the kinematic impermeability $u_{z}(h)=0$, $f(h)=0$, is required
and it is precisely the $f'$ contribution in $f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$ that
converts the apparent $h\cosh kh$ factor into the $h\sinh kh$ factor in
the steady surface normal stress.  This is the viscosity independent
steady transfer function with $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$,
$f(0)=f'(0)=0$ and the material, constant-$h$ base.  With the
conventional $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ isostatic normalisation this is the
usual $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\rho g$ amplitude quoted for viscous dynamic
topography.

13.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I’ve been re-reading the set-up with the material base in mind and I think the
base-kinematics point is the one that decides which numerator you get.

We all agree on the normal mode

$\psi(x,z)=f(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=f'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k f\cos kx$, 
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}f=0$,

$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[f''+k^{2}f]\sin kx$, $\sigma_{zz}=\mu[k^{-1}f'''-3k f']\cos kx$,
$f'(0)=0$, steady $f(0)=0$, and the top traction

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$, i.e.
$\Delta\rho g\,e=2\mu k^{2}C_{1}$ in the basis

$f(z)=C_{1}\sinh kz+C_{3}z\sinh kz-kC_{1}z\cosh kz$, $f(0)=f'(0)=0$,
$f'''(0)=2k^{3}C_{1}$.

Viscosity cancels in the steady balance and the long-wave limit is
$\chi\sim kh$ in either description, which is why the two forms are
so close.

The split is the base. The statement says “the plate has a thickness $h$”
and “the bottom of the layer at $z=h$”.  That is a material interface.
Incompressibility with the rigid lid $u_{z}(0)=0$ in the steady state
requires no net vertical flux through the finite slab, i.e. the
kinematic impermeability

$u_{z}(h)=-k f(h)\cos kx=0\iff f(h)=0$

in the mode, together with the stated tractions

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff\mu[f''+k^{2}f]_{h}=S_{0}$.

With $f(h)=0$,
$C_{1}\big[\sinh kh-kh\cosh kh\big]+C_{3}h\sinh kh=0$,
so that the $C_{1}$–$C_{3}$ coupling is
$C_{1}=C_{3}h\sinh kh/[kh\cosh kh-\sinh kh]$.
The $f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$ condition is then identically satisfied by
the same coupling, and

$\mu[f''+k^{2}f]_{h}=2\mu k\Big[C_{3}\cosh kh+C_{3}kh\sinh kh
-k^{2}C_{1}h\cosh kh\Big]=S_{0}$.

Eliminating $C_{3}$ gives

$C_{3}=-\frac{S_{0}}{2\mu k}\frac{\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}$,
$C_{1}=-\frac{S_{0}h\sinh kh}{2\mu k\big[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}\big]}$.

The surface normal stress is $\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}C_{1}$ up to
the usual $\sin\leftrightarrow\cos$ quadrature, hence, in magnitude,

$\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=S_{0}\frac{kh\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}$,

i.e.

$e_{s}= \chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,
$\displaystyle \chi(kh)=\frac{kh\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}$,
with the conventional anti-phase $e(x)\propto-\cos kx$ to the
$S_{0}\sin kx$ shear.  Viscosity cancels as it must.

In the long wave limit $\sinh kh=kh+O(k^{3}h^{3})$,
$\chi=kh/[1+k^{2}h^{2}]+O(k^{3}h^{3})\simeq kh$, $e_{s}\simeq kh
S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, and $\chi\sim kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$.
For $kh=1$, $\chi_{\sinh}\approx0.35$, i.e. $\tanh kh\approx0.76$ of the
free-to-move-base $\cosh$ value, which is the $O(k^{2}h^{2})$ difference
quoted by 1,10,11,12,15 themselves.

The $kh\cosh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$ form is what you get if you allow
$f(h)\neq0$, $u_{z}(h)\neq0$, i.e. the base is free to move vertically
and the thickness is allowed to change.  The colleagues who quote it
explicitly note that the $kh\sinh kh$ numerator is the $f(h)=0$,
$u_{z}(h)=0$ impermeable base limit.  With the stated constant-thickness
layer the material interface at $z=h$ should be impermeable, which is the
$k h\sinh kh$ transfer function above, essentially indistinguishable
from the $\cosh$ form in the thin-plate lubrication limit but
physically consistent with $h=$ const.  The $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ isostatic
replacement and the usual $90^{\circ}$ phase/sign are the conventional

15.text:
For the $k$–harmonic put

$$\psi(x,z)=f(z)\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{x}=f'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-k f\cos kx,\qquad 
(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}f=0 ,$$

so that with $\mu={\rm const}$

$$\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]\sin kx ,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}=\mu\big[k^{-1}f'''-3k f'\big]\cos kx  $$

on the rigid lid

$$u_{x}(0)=0\iff f'(0)=0 ,\qquad \dot e=u_{z}(0)=-k f(0)\cos kx ,$$

and in the steady state $\dot e=0$, $f(0)=f'(0)=0$.  With

$$f(0)=f'(0)=0\;\;\Longleftrightarrow\; 
f(z)=Bz\cosh kz+\Big[D\,z-\frac{B}{k}\Big]\sinh kz,   \qquad 
f'''(0)=2k^{2}B,$$

$$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}f'''(0)\cos kx=2\mu k B\cos kx.$$

On the free surface

$$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx ,\qquad 
\Delta\rho g\,e=2\mu k B , \tag{1}$$

$\rho\to\Delta\rho$ being the usual isostatic replacement, up to the
conventional $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ quadrature.  The base is
traction free

$$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h),\qquad
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff 
\mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]_{h}=S_{0} . \tag{2}$$

Now

$$f''+k^{2}f=2k\Big[ Bkh\cosh kz+D\cosh kz+Dkh\sinh kz\Big],$$

and $f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$ gives

$$B\big[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh\big]=khD\cosh kh, $$

i.e.

$$D=B\,\frac{\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh}{kh\cosh kh}.$$

Hence

$$\mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]_{h}
 =2\mu k\Big[Bkh\cosh kh+D\cosh kh+Dkh\sinh kh\Big]=S_{0},$$

and on elimination of $D$

$$2\mu k B\,\frac{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}{h\cosh kh}=S_{0}, $$

so that with (1)

$$B=\frac{S_{0}\,h\cosh kh}
        {2\mu\Big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\Big]},\qquad
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=2\mu kB
   =S_{0}\,\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}. $$

The viscosity cancels in the steady Stokes balance.  In magnitude

$$|e_{s}|=\chi(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}
       =\Bigg[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Bigg]^{-1}>0, $$

and with the upward positive sign the $\sin kx$ basal shear produces a
$-\cos kx$ topography

$$e(x)=-\,\chi(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\cos kx,
\qquad e_{s}=-\chi\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},$$

i.e. $90^{\circ}$ out of phase and anti-phase to $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$.
In particular

$$\chi(kh)=\frac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}+O(k^{4}h^{4}),\qquad kh\ll1,$$

so that in the thin-plate lubrication limit

$$|e_{s}|\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
|\chi_{0}|\simeq kh ,$$

and $\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$.  For $kh=1$,
$\chi(1)=\cosh1/[1+\cosh^{2}1]\approx0.46$.
This is the viscosity–independent steady viscous dynamic topography
with the stated $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ free base,
the base being free to move vertically, $u_{z}(h)\neq0$.  The
$\,kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]$ forms are the $u_{z}(h)=0$,
$f(h)=0$ impermeable–base limit.  Up to the inessential overall sign
this is the $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ transfer function normally
quoted as $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ in the long wave limit. ∎

5.text:
With the $k$ mode

$\psi(x,z)=f(z)\sin kx$ , $u_{x}=f'\sin kx$ , $u_{z}=-k f\cos kx$,
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}f=0$,

$$
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]\sin kx ,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= \mu\Big[k^{-1}f'''-3k f'\Big]\cos kx ,
$$

the rigid lid is $u_{x}(0)=0\iff f'(0)=0$.
For a stationary topography $\dot e=u_{z}(0)=-k f(0)\cos kx=0$ so that in
the steady state

$$
f(0)=f'(0)=0 ,
\qquad 
f(z)=Bz\cosh kz+\Big[D\,z-\frac{B}{k}\Big]\sinh kz,
\qquad f'''(0)=2k^{2}B ,
$$

and

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}f'''(0)\cos kx=2\mu k B\cos kx .
$$

With the isostatic normal stress $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$,
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$,

\begin{equation*}
\Delta\rho g\,e=2\mu k B,\qquad B=\frac{\Delta\rho g\,e}{2\mu k},
\tag{1}
\end{equation*}
the topography being $90^{\circ}$ out of phase with the imposed
$\sin kx$ basal shear, $e\propto-\cos kx$.

On the base

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h),\qquad
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff \mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]_{h}=S_{0},
\tag{2}
$$

and

$$
f''+k^{2}f=2k\Big[Bkh\cosh kz+D\cosh kz+Dkh\sinh kz\Big].
$$

$f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$ gives

$$
B\big[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh\big]=kh\,D\cosh kh,\qquad
D=B\frac{\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh}{kh\cosh kh}.
\tag{3}
$$

Hence

$$
\mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]_{h}
=2\mu k\Big[Bkh\cosh kh+D\cosh kh+Dkh\sinh kh\Big]=S_{0},
$$

and with (3)

$$
2\mu kB\,\frac{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}{h\cosh kh}=S_{0}.
\tag{4}
$$

Eliminating $B$ between (1) and (4) the viscosity cancels in the
steady Stokes balance and

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh},
$$

i.e. up to the conventional $ \sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase

$$
e(x)=-\,\chi(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\cos kx,
\qquad 
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}
       =\Bigg[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Bigg]^{-1}>0,
$$

so that in magnitude

$$
|e_{s}|=\chi(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
e_{s}= \chi\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\;\;{\rm mod\; sign},
$$

the well known viscosity independent dynamic topography.  In the
thin–plate lubrication limit

$$
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}+O(k^{4}h^{4})\simeq kh,\qquad 
kh\ll1,
$$

so that

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad |\chi_{0}|\simeq kh,
$$

and $\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$, e.g.
$\chi(1)=\cosh1/[1+\cosh^{2}1]\approx0.46$.  With the usual upward
positive sign the $\sin kx$ basal shear produces an anti-phase
$\cos kx$ topography $e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g\cos kx$.
The sign is inessential; the magnitude transfer function is the
viscosity independent $\chi(kh)$ above.

Remark.  On the additional material impermeability $u_{z}(h)=0\iff
f(h)=0$ the $C_{1}\!-\!C_{3}$ coupling is $C_{1}=C_{3}h\sinh kh/
\big[kh\cosh kh-\sinh kh\big]$ and the steady surface stress becomes

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{kh\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}},\qquad
\chi_{\rm sph}(kh)=\frac{kh\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}},
$$

which is the often quoted $f(h)=0$ impermeable–base limit.  To
$O(k^{2}h^{2})$,
$\chi_{\rm sph}=kh+O(k^{3}h^{3})$, i.e. the long–wave
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ scaling is unchanged, the
$\cosh$–numerator and $\sinh$–numerator forms differing only by the
factor $\tanh kh$ and being numerically indistinguishable in the
thin-plate $kh\ll1$ regime.  With the traction data
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0,\;\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ quoted in the statement the
base is free to move vertically and the $\cosh$ numerator transfer
function above is the literal steady Stokes response. ∎

12.text:
With the normal mode
$\psi=f(z)\sin kx$,
$u_{x}=f^{\prime}\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-kf\cos kx$,
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}f=0$,
$$
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\bigl[f^{\prime\prime}+k^{2}f\bigr]\sin kx,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}=\mu\Bigl[k^{-1}f^{\prime\prime\prime}-3kf^{\prime}\Bigr]\cos kx ,
$$
the rigid lid is $u_{x}(0)=0$, $f^{\prime}(0)=0$ and in the steady state
$\dot e=u_{z}(0)=0$, $f(0)=0$.  With $f(0)=f^{\prime}(0)=0$
$$
f(z)=Az\cosh kz+\Bigl[Bz-\frac{A}{k}\Bigr]\sinh kz,\qquad
f^{\prime\prime\prime}(0)=2k^{2}A
$$
so that
$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}f^{\prime\prime\prime}(0)\cos kx
          =2\mu kA\cos kx =\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx ,
\tag{1}
$$
i.e. up to the usual $90^{\circ}$ $\sin\leftrightarrow\cos$ phase
$\Delta\rho g\,e=2\mu kA$ and the topography is in quadrature with the
imposed $\sin kx$ basal shear.  On the base
$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff f^{\prime\prime\prime}(h)=3k^{2}f^{\prime}(h),
\qquad
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff\mu\bigl[f^{\prime\prime}+k^{2}f\bigr]_{h}=S_{0},
$$
and
$$
f^{\prime\prime}+k^{2}f=2k\Bigl[Akh\cosh kz+B\cosh kz+Bkh\sinh kz\Bigr].
$$
The zero normal traction,
$A\bigl[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh\bigr]=Bkh\cosh kh$, gives on elimination of
$B$
$$
\mu\bigl[f^{\prime\prime}+k^{2}f\bigr]_{h}
   =\frac{2\mu A}{h\cosh kh}\Bigl[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}\Bigr]=S_{0},
$$
i.e.
$$
A=\frac{S_{0}h\cosh kh}{2\mu\bigl[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}\bigr]} .
$$
With (1) the viscosity cancels in the steady Stokes balance and
$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=2\mu kA
   =S_{0}\,\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}\;,
$$
so that up to the conventional $90^{\circ}$ phase
$$
e(x)=-\chi(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\cos kx,
\qquad 
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}
       =\Bigg[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Bigg]^{-1}>0,
$$
and in magnitude
$e_{s}= \chi(kh)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.  With the upward positive sign the
$+S_{0}\sin kx$ basal shear gives the anti-phase $\cos kx$ topography
$e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.  In particular
$$
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}+O(k^{4}h^{4}),\qquad kh\ll1,
$$
so that in the long-wave lubrication limit
$$
|e_{s}|\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi_{0}\simeq kh,
$$
and $\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$, e.g.
$\chi(1)=\cosh1/[1+\cosh^{2}1]\simeq0.46$.  With the notation of the
statement $\Delta\rho\to\rho$ this is the familiar viscosity
independent viscous dynamic topography $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\rho g$,
the $90^{\circ}$ anti-phase $e\propto-\cos kx$ to $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$.
The $kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]$ form is the $u_{z}(h)=0$,
$f(h)=0$ impermeable base limit; with the stated $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ data the base is free to move vertically and the
$\cosh$–numerator transfer function above is the steady Stokes
response.  In the thin plate limit the two forms coincide to $O(kh)$,
$|e_{s}|\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$. ∎

The $90^{\circ}$ phase is the usual $e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g\cos kx$
for an imposed $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$.
For $kh\ll1$, $\sinh kh=kh+O(k^{3}h^{3})$, $\cosh kh=1+O(k^{2}h^{2})$,
\[
\chi(kh)=\frac{(kh)^{2}}{1+(kh)^{2}}+O(k^{4}h^{4})
       =\frac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}+O(k^{3}h^{3})\simeq kh,
\]
so $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ is recovered in the long-wave
lubrication limit and $\chi\sim kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$.  At
$kh=1$, $\chi_{\sinh}(1)=\sinh1/[1+\cosh^{2}1]\approx0.35$, numerically
$\tanh1\approx0.76$ of the free-to-move-base $\cosh$ form, the
difference being $O(k^{2}h^{2})$ in the thin-plate regime.

The $kh\cosh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]$ numerator is obtained if
$f(h)\neq0$, i.e. if the base is allowed to move vertically and the
thickness can change.  With the stated constant-thickness incompressible
layer the kinematic impermeability $u_{z}(h)=0$, $f(h)=0$, is required
and it is precisely the $f'$ contribution in $f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$ that
converts the apparent $h\cosh kh$ factor into the $h\sinh kh$ factor in
the steady surface normal stress.  This is the viscosity independent
steady transfer function with $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$,
$f(0)=f'(0)=0$ and the material, constant-$h$ base.  With the
conventional $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ isostatic normalisation this is the
usual $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\rho g$ amplitude quoted for viscous dynamic
topography.

I’ve been re-reading the set-up with the material base in mind and I think the
base-kinematics point is the one that decides which numerator you get.

We all agree on the normal mode

$\psi(x,z)=f(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=f'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k f\cos kx$, 
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}f=0$,

$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[f''+k^{2}f]\sin kx$, $\sigma_{zz}=\mu[k^{-1}f'''-3k f']\cos kx$,
$f'(0)=0$, steady $f(0)=0$, and the top traction

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$, i.e.
$\Delta\rho g\,e=2\mu k^{2}C_{1}$ in the basis

$f(z)=C_{1}\sinh kz+C_{3}z\sinh kz-kC_{1}z\cosh kz$, $f(0)=f'(0)=0$,
$f'''(0)=2k^{3}C_{1}$.

Viscosity cancels in the steady balance and the long-wave limit is
$\chi\sim kh$ in either description, which is why the two forms are
so close.

The split is the base. The statement says “the plate has a thickness $h$”
and “the bottom of the layer at $z=h$”.  That is a material interface.
Incompressibility with the rigid lid $u_{z}(0)=0$ in the steady state
requires no net vertical flux through the finite slab, i.e. the
kinematic impermeability

$u_{z}(h)=-k f(h)\cos kx=0\iff f(h)=0$

in the mode, together with the stated tractions

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff\mu[f''+k^{2}f]_{h}=S_{0}$.

With $f(h)=0$,
$C_{1}\big[\sinh kh-kh\cosh kh\big]+C_{3}h\sinh kh=0$,
so that the $C_{1}$–$C_{3}$ coupling is
$C_{1}=C_{3}h\sinh kh/[kh\cosh kh-\sinh kh]$.
The $f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$ condition is then identically satisfied by
the same coupling, and

$\mu[f''+k^{2}f]_{h}=2\mu k\Big[C_{3}\cosh kh+C_{3}kh\sinh kh
-k^{2}C_{1}h\cosh kh\Big]=S_{0}$.

Eliminating $C_{3}$ gives

$C_{3}=-\frac{S_{0}}{2\mu k}\frac{\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}$,
$C_{1}=-\frac{S_{0}h\sinh kh}{2\mu k\big[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}\big]}$.

The surface normal stress is $\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}C_{1}$ up to
the usual $\sin\leftrightarrow\cos$ quadrature, hence, in magnitude,

$\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=S_{0}\frac{kh\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}$,

i.e.

$e_{s}= \chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,
$\displaystyle \chi(kh)=\frac{kh\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}$,
with the conventional anti-phase $e(x)\propto-\cos kx$ to the
$S_{0}\sin kx$ shear.  Viscosity cancels as it must.

In the long wave limit $\sinh kh=kh+O(k^{3}h^{3})$,
$\chi=kh/[1+k^{2}h^{2}]+O(k^{3}h^{3})\simeq kh$, $e_{s}\simeq kh
S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, and $\chi\sim kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$.
For $kh=1$, $\chi_{\sinh}\approx0.35$, i.e. $\tanh kh\approx0.76$ of the
free-to-move-base $\cosh$ value, which is the $O(k^{2}h^{2})$ difference
quoted by 1,10,11,12,15 themselves.

The $kh\cosh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$ form is what you get if you allow
$f(h)\neq0$, $u_{z}(h)\neq0$, i.e. the base is free to move vertically
and the thickness is allowed to change.  The colleagues who quote it
explicitly note that the $kh\sinh kh$ numerator is the $f(h)=0$,
$u_{z}(h)=0$ impermeable base limit.  With the stated constant-thickness
layer the material interface at $z=h$ should be impermeable, which is the
$k h\sinh kh$ transfer function above, essentially indistinguishable
from the $\cosh$ form in the thin-plate lubrication limit but
physically consistent with $h=$ const.  The $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ isostatic
replacement and the usual $90^{\circ}$ phase/sign are the conventional
notational choices.

For the $k$–harmonic put

$$\psi(x,z)=f(z)\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{x}=f'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-k f\cos kx,\qquad 
(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}f=0 ,$$

so that with $\mu={\rm const}$

$$\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]\sin kx ,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}=\mu\big[k^{-1}f'''-3k f'\big]\cos kx  $$

on the rigid lid

$$u_{x}(0)=0\iff f'(0)=0 ,\qquad \dot e=u_{z}(0)=-k f(0)\cos kx ,$$

and in the steady state $\dot e=0$, $f(0)=f'(0)=0$.  With

$$f(0)=f'(0)=0\;\;\Longleftrightarrow\; 
f(z)=Bz\cosh kz+\Big[D\,z-\frac{B}{k}\Big]\sinh kz,   \qquad 
f'''(0)=2k^{2}B,$$

$$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}f'''(0)\cos kx=2\mu k B\cos kx.$$

On the free surface

$$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx ,\qquad 
\Delta\rho g\,e=2\mu k B , \tag{1}$$

$\rho\to\Delta\rho$ being the usual isostatic replacement, up to the
conventional $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ quadrature.  The base is
traction free

$$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h),\qquad
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff 
\mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]_{h}=S_{0} . \tag{2}$$

Now

$$f''+k^{2}f=2k\Big[ Bkh\cosh kz+D\cosh kz+Dkh\sinh kz\Big],$$

and $f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$ gives

$$B\big[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh\big]=khD\cosh kh, $$

i.e.

$$D=B\,\frac{\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh}{kh\cosh kh}.$$

Hence

$$\mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]_{h}
 =2\mu k\Big[Bkh\cosh kh+D\cosh kh+Dkh\sinh kh\Big]=S_{0},$$

and on elimination of $D$

$$2\mu k B\,\frac{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}{h\cosh kh}=S_{0}, $$

so that with (1)

$$B=\frac{S_{0}\,h\cosh kh}
        {2\mu\Big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\Big]},\qquad
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=2\mu kB
   =S_{0}\,\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}. $$

The viscosity cancels in the steady Stokes balance.  In magnitude

$$|e_{s}|=\chi(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}
       =\Bigg[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Bigg]^{-1}>0, $$

and with the upward positive sign the $\sin kx$ basal shear produces a
$-\cos kx$ topography

$$e(x)=-\,\chi(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\cos kx,
\qquad e_{s}=-\chi\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},$$

i.e. $90^{\circ}$ out of phase and anti-phase to $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$.
In particular

$$\chi(kh)=\frac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}+O(k^{4}h^{4}),\qquad kh\ll1,$$

so that in the thin-plate lubrication limit

$$|e_{s}|\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
|\chi_{0}|\simeq kh ,$$

and $\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$.  For $kh=1$,
$\chi(1)=\cosh1/[1+\cosh^{2}1]\approx0.46$.
This is the viscosity–independent steady viscous dynamic topography
with the stated $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ free base,
the base being free to move vertically, $u_{z}(h)\neq0$.  The
$\,kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]$ forms are the $u_{z}(h)=0$,
$f(h)=0$ impermeable–base limit.  Up to the inessential overall sign
this is the $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ transfer function normally
quoted as $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ in the long wave limit. ∎

With the $k$ mode

$\psi(x,z)=f(z)\sin kx$ , $u_{x}=f'\sin kx$ , $u_{z}=-k f\cos kx$,
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}f=0$,

$$
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]\sin kx ,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= \mu\Big[k^{-1}f'''-3k f'\Big]\cos kx ,
$$

the rigid lid is $u_{x}(0)=0\iff f'(0)=0$.
For a stationary topography $\dot e=u_{z}(0)=-k f(0)\cos kx=0$ so that in
the steady state

$$
f(0)=f'(0)=0 ,
\qquad 
f(z)=Bz\cosh kz+\Big[D\,z-\frac{B}{k}\Big]\sinh kz,
\qquad f'''(0)=2k^{2}B ,
$$

and

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}f'''(0)\cos kx=2\mu k B\cos kx .
$$

With the isostatic normal stress $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$,
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$,

\begin{equation*}
\Delta\rho g\,e=2\mu k B,\qquad B=\frac{\Delta\rho g\,e}{2\mu k},
\tag{1}
\end{equation*}
the topography being $90^{\circ}$ out of phase with the imposed
$\sin kx$ basal shear, $e\propto-\cos kx$.

On the base

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h),\qquad
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff \mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]_{h}=S_{0},
\tag{2}
$$

and

$$
f''+k^{2}f=2k\Big[Bkh\cosh kz+D\cosh kz+Dkh\sinh kz\Big].
$$

$f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$ gives

$$
B\big[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh\big]=kh\,D\cosh kh,\qquad
D=B\frac{\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh}{kh\cosh kh}.
\tag{3}
$$

Hence

$$
\mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]_{h}
=2\mu k\Big[Bkh\cosh kh+D\cosh kh+Dkh\sinh kh\Big]=S_{0},
$$

and with (3)

$$
2\mu kB\,\frac{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}{h\cosh kh}=S_{0}.
\tag{4}
$$

Eliminating $B$ between (1) and (4) the viscosity cancels in the
steady Stokes balance and

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh},
$$

i.e. up to the conventional $ \sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase

$$
e(x)=-\,\chi(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\cos kx,
\qquad 
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}
       =\Bigg[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Bigg]^{-1}>0,
$$

so that in magnitude

$$
|e_{s}|=\chi(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
e_{s}= \chi\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\;\;{\rm mod\; sign},
$$

the well known viscosity independent dynamic topography.  In the
thin–plate lubrication limit

$$
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}+O(k^{4}h^{4})\simeq kh,\qquad 
kh\ll1,
$$

so that

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad |\chi_{0}|\simeq kh,
$$

and $\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$, e.g.
$\chi(1)=\cosh1/[1+\cosh^{2}1]\approx0.46$.  With the usual upward
positive sign the $\sin kx$ basal shear produces an anti-phase
$\cos kx$ topography $e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g\cos kx$.
The sign is inessential; the magnitude transfer function is the
viscosity independent $\chi(kh)$ above.

Remark.  On the additional material impermeability $u_{z}(h)=0\iff
f(h)=0$ the $C_{1}\!-\!C_{3}$ coupling is $C_{1}=C_{3}h\sinh kh/
\big[kh\cosh kh-\sinh kh\big]$ and the steady surface stress becomes

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{kh\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}},\qquad
\chi_{\rm sph}(kh)=\frac{kh\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}},
$$

which is the often quoted $f(h)=0$ impermeable–base limit.  To
$O(k^{2}h^{2})$,
$\chi_{\rm sph}=kh+O(k^{3}h^{3})$, i.e. the long–wave
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ scaling is unchanged, the
$\cosh$–numerator and $\sinh$–numerator forms differing only by the
factor $\tanh kh$ and being numerically indistinguishable in the
thin-plate $kh\ll1$ regime.  With the traction data
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0,\;\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ quoted in the statement the
base is free to move vertically and the $\cosh$ numerator transfer
function above is the literal steady Stokes response. ∎

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The normal mode $\psi=f(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=f'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k f\cos kx$, $(D^2-k^2)^2f=0$, is the established basis in rounds 0-4. With rigid lid $u_x(0)=0\Rightarrow f'(0)=0$ and steady state $\dot e=u_z(0)=0\Rightarrow f(0)=0$,

$f(z)=Bz\cosh kz+[Dz-B/k]\sinh kz$,
$f'''(0)=2k^2B$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu[k^{-1}f'''-3k f']\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[f''+k^2f]\sin kx$.

Hence $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)=2\mu kB =\Delta\rho g\,e$, $B=\Delta\rho g e/2\mu k$, viscosity cancels in steady state.

This gives $B[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh]=kh D\cosh kh$ and
$2\mu k B\,[k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh]/[h\cosh kh]=S_0$.

Eliminating $B$,
$\Delta\rho g e_s=S_0\,kh\cosh kh/[k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh]$,
i.e. in magnitude
$e_s=\chi(kh)S_0/\Delta\rho g$,
$\chi(kh)=kh\cosh kh/[\cosh^2kh+k^2h^2]=[kh/\cosh kh+\cosh kh/kh]^{-1}>0$.

Signed convention $e(x)=-\chi S_0/\Delta\rho g\cos kx$, $90^{\circ}$ anti-phase of basal $\sin kx$ shear to topography. 11.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The steady 2-D Stokes mode is $\psi=f(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=f'\sin kx$, $u_z=-kf\cos kx$, $(D^2-k^2)^2f=0$, $\sigma_{xz}=\mu[f''+k^2f]\sin kx$, $\sigma_{zz}=\mu[k^{-1}f'''-3k f']\cos kx$. Rigid lid $u_x(0)=0$ gives $f'(0)=0$ and steady $\dot e=0$ gives $f(0)=0$. Hence up to a constant

$f(z)=A[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+Bz\sinh kz$, $f'''(0)= -2k^{3}A$, 
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)\cos kx$, $\rho g e =\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)$.

With the stated traction free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$ and imposed shear $\mu[f''+k^{2}f]_{h}=S_{0}$ the viscosity cancels in the steady balance. Eliminating $A,B$ gives

$\rho g e_s = S_{0}\,kh\cosh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]$,

i.e. in magnitude with the isostatic restoring $\Delta\rho g$,

$e_s =\chi(kh)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, 
$\chi(kh)=kh\cosh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]=[kh/\cosh kh+\cosh kh/kh]^{-1}>0$,

and with upward positive convention $e(x)=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g\cos kx$: the $S_{0}\sin kx$ basal shear produces a $\cos kx$ topography $90^{\circ}$ out of phase, anti-phase. Long wave $kh\ll1$ : $\chi=kh/[1+k^{2}h^{2}]+O(k^{4}h^{4})\simeq kh$, $e_s\simeq kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, $\chi\sim2kh e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$. For $kh=1$, $\chi\approx0.46$. Viscosity drops out.

Disagreement persists in the deliberation. Colleagues 7,13,14 impose the material impermeability $u_z(h)=0\iff f(h)=0$, i.e. a constant thickness, material base. With $f(h)=0$ the $A$–$B$ coupling changes and the steady normal stress becomes

$\Delta\rho g e_s =S_{0}kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]$,

$\chi_{\rm imp}(kh)=kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]$,

$\chi_{\rm imp}=kh/[ \cosh kh/kh +\tanh kh]$. This is the $f(h)=0$, $u_z(h)=0$ limit. To $O(kh)$ the two forms coincide, $\chi_{\rm imp}=kh+O(k^{3}h^{3})$, $\chi_{\rm free}=kh+O(k^{3}h^{3})$, and differ only by $\tanh kh$ factor, e.g. $\chi_{\rm imp}(1)\approx0.35$ vs $\chi_{\rm free}(1)\approx0.46$.

The statement gives $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$, $u_x(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$, and does not impose $u_z(h)=0$. The stated “thickness $h$” is taken by the majority in rounds 0-4 as the geometric domain $0\le z\le h$ with a traction free base free to move vertically, $f(h)\neq0$ allowed. The impermeable-base variant is the physically motivated constant-thickness material interface, but it is an extra kinematic condition not written explicitly.

Sign convention remains a notational difference: magnitude $|\chi|$ as above, signed form $e_s=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for anti-phase $\sin\leftrightarrow\cos$. Replacement $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ for buoyancy is conventional. Unresolved is whether the problem intends the strict traction-only base or the material $u_z(h)=0$ base; the thin-plate long-wave scaling $e_s\approx kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ is stable in either case.

$\Delta\rho g e_{s}= \mu k^{-1}F'''(0)=2\mu k^{2}C_{1}$ up to the $\sin\leftrightarrow\cos$ $90^{\circ}$ phase. In magnitude

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}$,

2.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The steady normal mode is the common scaffold. With $\psi=f(z)\sin kx$,
$u_x=f'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k f\cos kx$, $(D^2-k^2)^2f=0$,
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[f''+k^2f]\sin kx$, $\sigma_{zz}=\mu[k^{-1}f'''-3k f']\cos kx$.
Rigid lid $u_x(0)=0\Rightarrow f'(0)=0$ and steady $\dot e=0\Rightarrow f(0)=0$.
Then $f(z)=Bz\cosh kz+[Dz-B/k]\sinh kz$, $f'''(0)=2k^2B$ and
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)=2\mu kB =\Delta\rho g\,e$, i.e.
$\Delta\rho g e=2\mu kB$ up to the $\sin\leftrightarrow\cos$ $90^{\circ}$ quadrature.
The base tractions stated are $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff f'''(h)=3k^2f'(h)$
and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0\iff\mu[f''+k^2f]_h=S_0$. No vertical velocity condition
is stated at $z=h$.

With $f(0)=f'(0)=0$,
$f''+k^2f=2k[Bkh\cosh kz+D\cosh kz+Dkh\sinh kz]$ and
$f'''(h)=3k^2f'(h)$ gives $B[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh]=khD\cosh kh$.
Hence
$\mu[f''+k^2f]_h=2\mu kB\,[k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh]/[h\cosh kh]=S_0$.
Eliminating $B$ with $\Delta\rho g e=2\mu kB$ the viscosity cancels:

$\Delta\rho g\,e_s=S_0\,kh\cosh kh/[k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh]$,
i.e. in magnitude
$e_s=\chi(kh)S_0/\Delta\rho g$ with

$\chi(kh)=kh\cosh kh/[k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh]=[kh/\cosh kh+\cosh kh/kh]^{-1}>0$,

and with upward positive sign $e(x)=-\chi S_0/\Delta\rho g\cos kx$, 
the $\sin kx$ basal shear being $90^{\circ}$ out of phase and anti-phase to the
$\cos kx$ topography.  Long wave $kh\ll1$:
$\chi=kh/[1+k^2h^2]+O(k^4h^4)\simeq kh$, $e_s\simeq kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$,
$\chi\sim2kh e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$, e.g. $\chi(1)\approx0.46$.
The viscosity drops out of the steady balance.

Round 4 public: Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9,10,11,12,15 converge on the
cosh-numerator free-base transfer function above, viscosity independence,
$kh$ thin-plate limit and anti-phase sign, with $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ the
usual isostatic replacement. Colleagues 7,13,14 persist with the
material/constant-thickness kinematic condition $u_z(h)=0\iff f(h)=0$.
That extra condition changes the $C_1\!-\!C_3$ coupling to
$C_1=-S_0h\sinh kh/[2\mu k(\cosh^2kh+k^2h^2)]$ and gives the
impermeable-base form

$\chi_{imp}(kh)=kh\sinh kh/[k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh]$,
i.e. $\chi_{imp}=\tanh kh\,\chi$,
$\chi_{imp}\simeq kh$ to $O(kh)$ and $\chi_{imp}\approx0.35$ at $kh=1$.
The two forms are $O(k^2h^2)$ close in the thin-plate regime, the
difference being precisely the $f(h)=0$/$u_z(h)=0$ condition not stated
in the problem. With the stated traction data $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0$ and no imposed vertical velocity at the base the
base is free to move vertically, $f(h)\neq0$, and the cosh-numerator
$\chi$ is the literal steady Stokes response. The $\rho$ vs $\Delta\rho$
labelling and the overall $-$ sign are conventional cosmetic issues;
the magnitude transfer function is as above and reduces to the familiar
$e_s\approx kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$ in the long-wave limit. ∎

12.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The steady Stokes normal mode is 
$\psi = f(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=f'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k f\cos kx$, $(D^2-k^2)^2f=0$.
Rigid lid $u_x(0)=0$, steady $\dot e=0\Rightarrow u_z(0)=0$ gives
$f(0)=f'(0)=0$.  With $f(0)=f'(0)=0$

$f(z)=Az\cosh kz+[Bz-A/k]\sinh kz$, $f'''(0)=2k^2A$,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)\cos kx=2\mu kA\cos kx$.
With the isostatic top $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$,
$\Delta\rho g\,e=2\mu kA$ up to the usual $\sin\leftrightarrow\cos$
$90^{\circ}$ quadrature, i.e. $e\propto-\cos kx$ for $\tau_b\propto\sin kx$.

Free base tractions are
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff f'''(h)=3k^2f'(h)$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0\sin kx\iff\mu[f''+k^2f]_h=S_0$.
With $f(0)=f'(0)=0$, $f''+k^2f=2k\Big[Akh\cosh kz+B\cosh kz+Bkh\sinh kz\Big]$
and $f'''(h)=3k^2f'(h)$ gives
$A[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh]=Bkh\cosh kh$.
Hence
$\mu[f''+k^2f]_h=2\mu kA\,[k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh]/[h\cosh kh]=S_0$,
so that
$A=S_0h\cosh kh/\{2\mu[k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh]\}$.

Eliminating $A$ with $\Delta\rho g e=2\mu kA$ the viscosity cancels in the
steady balance,
$\Delta\rho g e_s=S_0\,kh\cosh kh/[k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh]$,
i.e. in magnitude
$e_s=\chi(kh)S_0/\Delta\rho g$,
$\chi(kh)=kh\cosh kh/[\cosh^2kh+k^2h^2]
      =[kh/\cosh kh+\cosh kh/kh]^{-1}>0$,
with signed convention $e(x)=-\chi S_0/\Delta\rho g\cos kx$, the
$90^{\circ}$ anti-phase between the imposed $S_0\sin kx$ shear and the
$\cos kx$ topography.  Long wave
$\chi\simeq kh/[1+k^2h^2]\simeq kh$ for $kh\ll1$, $e_s\simeq kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$,
and $\chi\sim2kh e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$, e.g. $\chi(1)\approx0.46$.
The response is viscosity independent.

The $kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^2kh+k^2h^2]$ numerator is the $f(h)=0$, $u_z(h)=0$
impermeable-base limit.  Colleagues 7,13,14 impose the extra kinematic
condition $u_z(h)=0\iff f(h)=0$, i.e. strictly constant thickness, which
gives $C_1[\sinh kh-kh\cosh kh]+C_3h\sinh kh=0$ and
$\chi_{\rm imp}=kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^2kh+k^2h^2]$, essentially
$\tanh kh$ times the free-base form.  With the data as stated
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0$, $u_x(0)=0$,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the base is free to move vertically,
$f(h)\neq0$, and the cosh-numerator transfer function above is the literal
steady Stokes response.  To $O(kh)$ the two forms coincide,
$|\chi|\simeq kh$, and the $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ isostatic replacement is the
usual notational choice.  The overall sign is the inessential
$\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ quadrature; the magnitude is the
$\chi$ quoted above. ∎

$\mu[f''+k^2f]_h=2\mu kB\,[k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh]/[h\cosh kh]=S_0$.

$\Delta\rho g e_s=2\mu kB=S_0\,kh\cosh kh/[k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh]$.
